name: Card
summary: A bordered, filled or raised container for one item: optional media, a header with a title and a description, a body, and a footer with actions. The whole card can be one link.
useWhen: One item among several that each need a title, a short summary and an action, such as a board, a project or a plan
A whole card that opens a detail page, through one CardLink in the title
A group of related settings or figures that reads as one block on a page
avoidWhen: A dense grid of files or boards in Studio, where tiles split by a 1px gap read better
Rows that people scan and compare, such as a list of messages or a table
A choice of one option out of several
Wrapping a whole page section only to draw a border around it: use Surface or Section

emphasis.description: outline: a hairline border on the surface. soft: one tone step up, no border. solid: the tone step plus elevation.menu, a soft drop shadow in both Studio and Desk, which steps to elevation.panel on hover.

size.description: Padding and the gap between parts: space l, 2xl and 4xl. sm takes radius.panel, md and lg take radius.card.

selected.description: Draws a 2px ring inside the border (not color alone) and sets data-selected. Say it in words too: aria-current on the CardLink or a checkbox in the card.

disabled.description: Sets data-disabled, mutes the title, dims the media with opacity.disabled and removes the CardLink href (aria-disabled, role link). Text stays at 4.5:1: a card is not a control, so the contrast exception does not cover it. Actions are disabled by the caller.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element as the root, for example an li inside a ul of cards or an article.

level.description: On CardTitle: the heading level, so the card fits the outline of its page.

href.description: On CardLink: the link target. Its hit area covers the whole card.

children.description: The parts: CardMedia, CardHeader (CardTitle, CardDescription), CardBody, CardFooter (CardActions).

a11y.role: None on the root (a div, or the asChild element). The title is a heading. A whole card link is one native link inside the title.
a11y.focus: The card itself never takes focus. Tab reaches the CardLink, then each action. While the link has keyboard focus the whole card shows the 2px ring from focus.shadow.ring.

keys.Tab: Moves to the card link, then to each action in the footer
keys.Enter: On the card link: opens it

a11y.announce: The link is named by the title text. Description and body are read in order after it. Selection is announced through aria-current on the link or a checkbox, which the caller sets.
notes: A whole card link is one real link and a stretched target (the link's ::before covers the card). Never wrap the card in a link and never put a button inside the link.

Actions sit above the stretched target, so they keep their own 24px targets and do not open the link. Interactive content goes in CardActions only: a link or button in the body sits under the target and cannot be clicked.
A disabled CardLink keeps tabIndex 0 and aria-disabled, so it stays in the tab order (convention 5); a click does nothing.
Text under the stretched target cannot be selected with the pointer. Keep long text that people copy out of an interactive card.
Forced colors: the border becomes CanvasText, the selected card gets a Highlight outline inside its border and focus shows as a Highlight outline.

en.title: The item's name, sentence case, no end period: Spring launch.
en.description: One line of context: Updated 2 hours ago, 4 boards.
en.actions: A verb plus a noun: Share board. An icon only action names its item: More actions for Spring launch.

ar.title: The item's name in white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: إطلاق الربيع.
ar.description: Short and plain, Western digits: آخر تحديث قبل 3 أيام.

react.note: Motion (card-lift, order 1.22): an interactive card rises distance.lift and grows to scale.lift on the soft spring under the pointer, and a decorative aria-hidden span (last child, not with asChild) draws a highlight that follows the pointer by transform; off under reduced motion.

angular.note: dsCard on the host, parts as attribute directives (dsCardTitle, a[dsCardLink]). Card.css as is.

native.note: A View with the same parts. A whole card link is a Pressable root with the title as its label; actions as separate Pressables beside it.

styles.studio: outline is the surface with the default border, soft is the surface 2 tone step. solid adds Studio's menu shadow (12 by 28px). An interactive card rises by space.4xs on hover, takes elevation.card-hover (a soft two layer shadow) and a 5% veil; soft and solid also step to surface 3.
styles.desk: The same parts on the Desk surfaces; solid takes the Desk menu shadow and the panel shadow on hover.
styles.neutral: Planned: small soft shadows and 1px borders from Neutral's tokens, no recipe expected.
styles.liquid: Planned: cards stay solid content under the glass layer.

mistakes.wrong: Wrapping the whole card in an anchor with buttons inside it
mistakes.right: One CardLink inside CardTitle; buttons in CardActions sit above its stretched target

mistakes.wrong: Showing selection only with a border color
mistakes.right: selected draws a 2px ring, and aria-current or a checkbox says it in words

mistakes.wrong: A Studio file grid of outlined cards with gaps
mistakes.right: Tile inside TileGrid, split by the 1px gap

mistakes.wrong: An action labelled More with no item name
mistakes.right: More actions for Spring launch

name: Checkbox
summary: One on or off choice that is saved with a form, with an indeterminate state for a parent of mixed children.
useWhen: One yes or no choice that takes effect when the form is saved, such as agreeing to terms
Picking rows in a table or items in a list, where several can be picked
A parent that checks or clears a set of children, shown indeterminate when only some are checked
avoidWhen: A setting that takes effect the moment it changes
One choice among options that exclude each other
Several related choices under one question with one value array

size.description: Box of 12, 16 and 24 px in a target of 24 px, 24 px and the lg control height (40 to 48 px by density). Inside a CheckboxGroup it follows the group.

tone.description: The fill of a checked box. neutral is the text color, accent the primary fill of the style, danger for a destructive choice.

onCheckedChange.description: Called with true or false when the person toggles the box. Never called while read only.

label.description: Visible text after the box, a native label bound to the control. Without it, pass aria-label.

description.description: A hint under the label. Joins aria-describedby.

value.description: Sent with the form when checked. Inside a CheckboxGroup it is the value this box adds to the group array, and the group owns the checked state.

name.description: The form name. Inside a CheckboxGroup it follows the group.

id.description: The control id. Inside a Field it defaults to the Field control id.

invalid.description: Danger border on an empty box and aria-invalid. Inside a Field or a CheckboxGroup it follows them.

disabled.description: Native disabled on the control. Inside a Field or a CheckboxGroup it follows them.

readOnly.description: Keeps the value and focus, ignores clicks and Space, sets aria-readonly.

required.description: Sets aria-required. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

rootProps.description: Props for the root element. className and style also go to the root; the ref and every other prop go to the control.

a11y.role: checkbox, on the control (a Radix button). aria-checked is true, false or mixed.
a11y.focus: The control is the one tab stop. Focus shows the glow and a 2px ring around the box.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the control, and on to the next control
keys.Space: Toggles the box. Enter does nothing, as a native checkbox.

a11y.announce: Name from the label (or aria-label), the state as checked, not checked or mixed, the description through aria-describedby, and invalid and required.
notes: The box is 16px inside a 24px target. The label is a native label bound to the control, so it extends the target.
A checked box shows a check and an indeterminate box a minus, so the state never relies on color alone.
Read only is not part of Radix: clicks are prevented, aria-readonly is set and the box draws dashed.
Indeterminate is a display state. The next click checks the box.

Motion, round 3 (check-draw and check-mixed, proposed): the fill grows from the centre of the box (clip-path) and the mark part, an aria-hidden svg of two strokes, is drawn with stroke-dashoffset, the short arm then the long arm; unchecking retracts it faster. The dash and the check are the same strokes (data-glyph check or minus on the mark), so mixed and checked bend into each other. Reduced motion: the fill and the mark change at once.

en.label: A statement in sentence case that is true when checked: Email me a weekly summary. No question, no trailing period.
en.negative: Never a negative label such as Do not email me. A checked box turns something on.
en.terms: For agreement, say what is agreed: I agree to the terms of use.

ar.label: جملة قصيرة بصيغة الاسم، تصير صحيحة لما ينحدد المربع، بدون تشكيل
ar.negative: لا تستخدم النفي في العنوان، المربع المحدد يشغل الشي
ar.terms: في الموافقة، اذكر وش اللي ينوافق عليه بالضبط

angular.behavior: div[dsCheckbox], hand built on a native button, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root. Inputs take the React prop names; onCheckedChange is the checkedChange output of [(checked)]. aria-label, aria-labelledby and aria-describedby are inputs, as React spreads them on the control. label and description take text. Behavior by hand with the Radix DOM: Space toggles, Enter does nothing, a hidden native checkbox inside a form. Works with reactive and template forms. Checkbox.css is used as is.

styles.studio: Achromatic: the checked box fills with the text color and the glyph takes the body color. accent is a quiet overlay fill.
styles.desk: The same box. accent fills with the yellow primary and a dark glyph.

mistakes.wrong: A checkbox that saves a setting the moment it changes
mistakes.right: A Switch

mistakes.wrong: Color alone shows that the box is checked
mistakes.right: The check and minus glyphs, which this component draws

mistakes.wrong: A disabled checkbox to show a value that cannot change
mistakes.right: readOnly, which stays readable and focusable

mistakes.wrong: A row of checkboxes with one label above them in a div
mistakes.right: A CheckboxGroup, a fieldset with a legend

mistakes.wrong: A Field label and a Checkbox label on the same box, which joins both into one name
mistakes.right: The Checkbox label only; use Field for its error and description

mistakes.wrong: A 16px box with no label and no wider target
mistakes.right: The control, which is a 24px target, and aria-label when there is no visible label

name: CheckboxGroup
summary: Several Checkbox items under one question, in a fieldset with a legend, with one value array.
useWhen: One question with several answers that can all be true, such as notification channels
A list of filters where any number can be on
A set of items with a select all item that checks or clears them
avoidWhen: Only one answer can be picked
One yes or no choice with no question around it
More than about fifteen options, or options that need search

legend.description: The question, in a legend. Required: it names the group.

description.description: A hint under the legend. Joins the group's aria-describedby.

error.description: What is wrong and how to fix it. While it shows, the group and every item are invalid.

value.description: Controlled value: the values of the checked items. Pair with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: Uncontrolled starting value.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new array of checked values.

size.description: Size of every item.

orientation.description: vertical: one item per line. horizontal: items wrap on a line.

selectAll.description: The label of an optional first item that checks or clears every item. It is indeterminate when some are checked.

name.description: The form name every item submits under.

invalid.description: When not passed, the group is invalid while it shows an error. false hides the error.

disabled.description: Disables every item.

readOnly.description: Every item keeps its value and focus and ignores clicks and Space.

a11y.role: group, from the native fieldset, named by the legend. Each item is a checkbox.
a11y.focus: Every item is its own tab stop, in DOM order. The select all item comes first.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next item, and out of the group after the last
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus to the item before

a11y.announce: The legend when focus enters the group, then the item name and state. The description and the error through the group's aria-describedby; each item also carries aria-invalid.
notes: Items are Checkbox components with a value. They read checked, size, name, disabled, invalid and read only from the group.
The error is not a live region and never role alert. A form that checks on submit moves focus to the first item of the invalid group.
Arrow keys do not move between items: that is a RadioGroup. Each checkbox is its own tab stop, as native checkboxes are.
checked, unchecked and indeterminate are on the select all part, a Checkbox root that carries the group's select-all part. The group root has no data-state.
Motion, round 3: select all cascades the draw of the boxes one delay.stagger apart, capped at three steps, in reading order when it checks and from the last box when it unchecks.

en.legend: The question in sentence case: Notify me about. Never a bare noun that does not say what to pick.
en.items: Short statements that are true when checked, in a parallel form. A logical order, never alphabetical by accident.
en.selectAll: All plus the noun: All channels. Not Select all.
en.error: What to do: Pick at least one way to reach you.

ar.legend: سؤال واضح بدون تشكيل: وش تبي يوصلك

react.behavior: native fieldset, hand built on Checkbox

angular.behavior: fieldset[dsCheckboxGroup], hand built on DsCheckbox through DS_CHECKBOX_GROUP, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root. Inputs take the React prop names; onValueChange is the valueChange output of [(value)]. legend, description, error and selectAll take text. aria-describedby is an input, joined with the group's own ids. Items are div[dsCheckbox] with a value; they read the value, size, name, disabled, invalid and read only from the group through DI. The select all item renders as React does it, a DsCheckbox with data-part select-all first in the items. The group is the ControlValueAccessor for the string array. CheckboxGroup.css is used as is.

styles.studio: A semibold legend over a tight list of Checkbox items, the error in the danger text color with its icon
styles.desk: The same layout, in Instrument Sans

mistakes.wrong: Checkboxes under a plain text heading in a div
mistakes.right: A CheckboxGroup, so the legend names the group for a screen reader

mistakes.wrong: Arrow keys that move between checkboxes
mistakes.right: Tab between items; arrows belong to a RadioGroup

mistakes.wrong: A select all item that is unchecked while some items are checked
mistakes.right: The selectAll prop, which shows indeterminate

mistakes.wrong: One answer only, drawn with checkboxes
mistakes.right: A RadioGroup

name: Chip
summary: A compact pill you press (a filter, toggled with selected) or remove (a picked value).
useWhen: A row of filters that each turn on and off
Values the user picked that can be removed one by one: tags, recipients, filters in use
A quick attribute choice in a toolbar
avoidWhen: A label that cannot be pressed or removed
One choice out of several where only one may be on
The main action of a view

children.description: The visible label, one to three words.

size.description: From size.control: 24, 28 and 32 px at default density. Never under 24 by 24.

start.description: Leading content, drawn in the icon part: a system icon name or node, hidden from assistive tech. A selected chip shows check in its place. Named start by rule 6 of anatomy.md; the part keeps the order's name icon.

selected.description: Pressable form only. Set (true or false) makes the chip a toggle: aria-pressed, data-selected, the solid fill of its tone and a check. Undefined is a plain action.

onClick.description: Pressable form: called on click, Enter and Space.

onRemove.description: Makes the chip removable: the root becomes a span with a remove button. Called on the remove button's click, Delete and Backspace. Move focus after removing.

removeLabel.description: The name of the remove button. Default Remove followed by the label when it is text, or إزالة under an Arabic Theme. Name what is removed: Remove filter Arabic.

disabled.description: aria-disabled and data-disabled on the pressable root or on the remove button. Stays focusable.

a11y.role: button (the pressable root, aria-pressed when selected is set). The removable form is a span with text and a remove button.
a11y.focus: The pressable chip is one tab stop; the removable chip's remove button is one tab stop. A 2px ring on keyboard focus. Both stay focusable when disabled.

keys.Enter: Presses the chip, or the remove button
keys.Space: Presses the chip, or the remove button
keys.Delete: On the remove button: removes the chip
keys.Backspace: On the remove button: removes the chip
keys.Tab: Moves to the next chip or remove button

a11y.announce: The label as the button name, with pressed or not pressed when selected is set. The remove button is named by removeLabel.
notes: A chip is pressable or removable, never both, so a button never sits inside a button.
The chip and its remove button are two targets of at least 24 by 24 px (WCAG 2.5.8): the remove button is an xs CloseButton. An xs removable chip stays 24px tall, in line with a pressable one.
Selected is shown by fill and a check icon, not by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
In forced colors a selected chip is the system Highlight fill with HighlightText; it opts out of forcing so the text backplate does not hide the label.
After a removal, move focus to the next chip's remove button, else the previous one, else a nearby control; the demo shows it (WCAG 2.4.3).

en.label: A noun or a short noun phrase in sentence case: Images, Shared with me.
en.removeLabel: Remove plus what it is: Remove filter Arabic.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: الصور، مشاركة معي.
ar.removeLabel: إزالة plus what it is: إزالة فلتر العربية.

react.note: Motion: none of its own today; colors swap at once. A chip list may use fade-rise for added chips from the catalog (1.11). The remove part is a CloseButton root carrying data-part remove.

styles.studio: A semibold pill on the overlay steps; selected is the inverted fill with a check.
styles.desk: The same; the selected accent chip is yellow with ink text and the doubled focus ring.
styles.neutral: Planned: follows the tokens, no recipe.
styles.liquid: Planned.

mistakes.wrong: A Chip with no onClick and no onRemove
mistakes.right: Badge

mistakes.wrong: A remove button named only Remove
mistakes.right: removeLabel="Remove filter Arabic"

mistakes.wrong: Selected shown by a color change alone
mistakes.right: selected, which fills the chip and adds a check

mistakes.wrong: Focus lost to the page after a chip is removed
mistakes.right: Move focus to the next chip's remove button

name: CloseButton
summary: The one close control for dialogs, toasts, banners, chips and drawers: a ghost icon button with the close icon and a default name.
useWhen: Closing a dialog, a drawer, a panel, a banner or a toast
Removing a chip or a filter, named for what it removes
Any close control, so every close looks and reads the same
avoidWhen: Cancelling a form or a task: say what happens with a Button (Cancel edit)
Deleting data: a close never deletes
A back step in a flow

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px in the default density. A ButtonGroup passes its size; this prop wins.

tone.description: Fixed: stamped so the shared Button.css draws it. Not a prop.

emphasis.description: Fixed: a close is always quiet. Not a prop; a ButtonGroup cannot change it.

shape.description: default takes radius.control (Desk draws it as a pill), pill is fully round, square takes radius.sm.

label.description: The accessible name (aria-label). Close, or إغلاق under an Arabic Theme. Name what closes when a screen has more than one (Close panel).

asChild.description: Renders the single child element, for example a link, as the control.

a11y.role: button
a11y.focus: In the tab order. A 2px ring on keyboard focus.

keys.Enter: Activates the close
keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: The label is the accessible name: Close by default, إغلاق under an Arabic Theme.
notes: Emphasis is always ghost and tone neutral; a ButtonGroup passes only size and shape.
The default name reads the lang of the nearest Theme, not a lang attribute on a plain element.
Dialog, Toast and Window draw their own close parts today; they can adopt CloseButton later (orders 1.6.1 and on).
At least 24 by 24 CSS px at xs.

Motion of round 3 (order 1.23, proposed, interaction close-turn): on hover, keyboard focus and press a round fill opens from the glyph (a circle clip on ::before) while the glyph turns a quarter turn on the snappy spring; a press pinches the glyph to scale.anticipate and it springs back on release. Hover only where the device can hover. Reduced motion: the fill shows whole at once, no turn, no pinch.

en.label: Close, or Close plus the thing: Close panel, Remove filter.

ar.label: إغلاق، أو إغلاق مع الشيء: إغلاق اللوحة.

angular.behavior: button[dsCloseButton] and a[dsCloseButton] on DsButtonBase
angular.note: No asChild: a[dsCloseButton] is the link form. The default name follows the lang of the nearest dsTheme. tone and loading are inherited inputs of the base; leave them unset.

native.note: 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android.

styles.studio: Ghost, the control radius.
styles.desk: Ghost, a circle (Desk controls are pills).
styles.neutral: Tokens only.
styles.liquid: Planned.

mistakes.wrong: A close button labelled X
mistakes.right: The default name, or Close plus the thing

mistakes.wrong: A close button that deletes the item
mistakes.right: A close only hides; deleting is a Button with tone danger

name: Combobox
summary: A text field that filters a long list as you type and keeps one value from it. The list opens under the field; focus stays in the field while the arrow keys move through the matches.
useWhen: One value from a long list (more than about 12 options) that people find faster by typing, such as a city, a country or a person
Options people know by name or by a code, such as an airport code, which keywords on the options can match
A value that must be one of the options, never free text
avoidWhen: Any text is a valid answer and the options are only suggestions
A short list of options that reads well without typing
Several values at once
Searching a whole site or running commands

items.description: The options, plain ({ value, label, description?, start?, disabled?, keywords? }) or in titled groups ({ label, options }), as ListBox takes them. Filtered by the label, then the keywords, best matches first inside each group.

value.description: The chosen option value, controlled with onValueChange. null: none.

defaultValue.description: Uncontrolled starting value.

onValueChange.description: Called with the chosen value, or null when cleared (the clear button, a second Escape, or an emptied field on blur).

inputValue.description: The text in the field, controlled with onInputValueChange. Use it to fetch options from a server as people type, with loading.

onInputValueChange.description: Called with the text on every keystroke.

open.description: The popup is open, controlled with onOpenChange.

size.description: Field height from size.control (28, 32, 44px at default density). sm lists use sm rows; md and lg lists use list.row.height. lg uses a fixed 16px type so phones do not zoom.

shape.description: default: the style's control radius (a pill in Studio and Desk). pill: always fully round.

invalid.description: The danger border and aria-invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field's error.

disabled.description: Native disabled on the input; the list never opens. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: The value shows and can be copied, not changed: no list, no clear button, a dashed border.

loading.description: Options are on their way: the trigger shows a spinner, the popup and the status say loadingLabel, data-loading and aria-busy are set.

loadingLabel.description: What the popup and the status say while loading. Arabic default: جار تحميل الخيارات.

empty.description: Shown in the popup when nothing matches. Arabic default: ما فيه نتائج. جرب كلمة ثانية. null shows no popup.

formatCount.description: The words read for the result count, once typing pauses. Default 3 results, pluralized with Intl.PluralRules in Arabic (نتيجة وحدة، نتيجتين، 5 نتائج، 12 نتيجة).

loop.description: ArrowDown on the last option goes to the first.

triggerLabel.description: The name of the opener button. Arabic default: عرض الخيارات.

clearLabel.description: The name of the clear button. Arabic default: مسح القيمة.

name.description: Submits the value under this name in a form, through a hidden input.

placeholder.description: A hint inside the empty field. Never the only label: wrap the Combobox in a Field with a label.

a11y.role: combobox (ARIA 1.2) on the input, aria-autocomplete list, aria-expanded, aria-controls pointing at the listbox in the popup, aria-activedescendant pointing at the highlighted option. The popup has no role of its own; it holds a ListBox named like the field. Not modal.
a11y.focus: Focus stays in the input the whole time, so the open popup holds no tab stop. data-state open and closed is stamped on the popup part, not on the field root. The trigger and clear buttons are not in the tab order (tabindex -1) and keep focus in the input when pressed. On blur the list closes and the field shows the chosen label again.

keys.Tab: Moves into the field and out of it; the list closes
keys.ArrowDown: Closed: opens the list on the chosen option, else the first. Open: moves to the next option, skipping disabled ones, wrapping at the end
keys.ArrowUp: Closed: opens the list on the last option. Open: moves to the previous option
keys.Alt+ArrowDown: Opens the list without moving the highlight
keys.Alt+ArrowUp: Chooses the highlighted option and closes the list
keys.Enter: Chooses the highlighted option and closes the list; it does not submit the form while an option is highlighted
keys.Escape: Open: closes the list and puts the chosen label back. Closed: clears the field and the value. Inside a Dialog, the Escape after the list closed closes the Dialog (Radix handles Escape on the document first); clear with the clear button or by selecting the text there
keys.Typing: Filters the list and opens it; the first match is highlighted so Enter picks it

a11y.announce: The input reads its Field label, its value, and that it has a list. Moving through the list reads each option (label, description, selected, position). After each query the count is read once, politely, from a visually hidden status (3 results; in Arabic 3 نتائج).
notes: Matching ignores case, accents, Arabic diacritics and the tatweel, and unifies alef forms, alef maqsura, ta marbuta and the hamza seats (normalize in @the-system/shared filter.ts).
The matched part of each option is wrapped in mark, drawn heavier and underlined, never by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
The trigger and clear buttons are 24px IconButtons (WCAG 2.5.8) with names; the list can also be opened with the keys.
The popup is portaled into a Theme copied from the field's Theme and is its own root carrying data-part popup, as a DropdownMenu submenu is; its z-index is z.menu so it shows over a Dialog.

Contract: the suite reads Combobox as a field, not an overlay: its popup never holds a tab stop (focus stays in the input), which the overlay checks require. data-state open and closed is on the popup root only. ArrowDown is checked on the input of the many case (aria-expanded changes) and Escape there with the list closed (the value clears). Opening, the popup anatomy and axe on the open popup are covered by the unit tests and a lane axe run (docs/reports/lanes/lane-3c.md).
The list is named like the field: through the Field label, else aria-label or aria-labelledby on the Combobox. Without a Field, pass one of them.

en.label: A noun in a Field label: City, Country, Assignee.
en.placeholder: Optional, a verb plus a noun: Search cities. Not a repeat of the label.
en.options: Nouns as people write them, sentence case: Abu Dhabi, Al Ahsa.
en.empty: Say what to try next: No results. Try another word.
en.error: Say what to do: Choose a city from the list.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: المدينة.
ar.empty: ما فيه نتائج. جرب كلمة ثانية.
ar.count: Pluralized with Intl.PluralRules (one, two, few, many and other forms), Western digits.

react.behavior: radix:Popover (Root, Anchor, Content); the combobox and the list hand built on ListBox
react.note: The base (ComboboxBase.tsx) is shared with Autocomplete. The popup surface is styled in Combobox.css for the whole list family; MultiSelect and TagField add their names to its selector lists. Sources GoBanana and Figma-Killer-2 were not reachable in the lane session; the field follows Input and the popup the DropdownMenu surface.

angular.behavior: div[dsCombobox], hand built: a CDK ComponentPortal popup placed with the Radix Popper steps (internal/popper.ts), a ListBox with virtualFocus, the highlight on the CDK ActiveDescendantKeyManager, the shared filter.ts and listbox.ts, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root (the Radix Anchor, with its class and data-radix-popper-side and -align). Inputs take the React prop names; onValueChange, onOpenChange and onInputValueChange are the valueChange, openChange and inputValueChange outputs of [(value)], [(open)] and [(inputValue)]. Native input props React spreads on the input (placeholder, id, name, aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby) are inputs. empty takes text or a TemplateRef. The popup is not a CDK Overlay pane: the same DOM and position as Radix Popover. Angular Aria Combobox would replace the key manager once @angular/aria is installed. Combobox.css is used as is.

native.behavior: hand built: a TextInput and a FlatList in a sheet

styles.studio: The field is the Input box: a transparent pill with the control border, the glow and the ring on focus. The popup is the Studio menu surface: surface-3, the card radius, the menu shadow; the lit row takes the overlay step.
styles.desk: The same field. The popup is the Desk menu glass: the strong material and blur, a hairline, the panel radius with field radius rows, regular weight; the lit row is the yellow primary fill with dark text. Under reduced transparency and more contrast the glass turns solid.
styles.neutral: Planned: tokens only.

mistakes.wrong: A Combobox where any typed text is a fine answer
mistakes.right: Autocomplete, which keeps the text

mistakes.wrong: A placeholder as the only label
mistakes.right: A Field with a label around the Combobox

mistakes.wrong: Moving focus into the list with the arrow keys
mistakes.right: Focus stays in the input; aria-activedescendant points at the option (built in)

mistakes.wrong: An empty popup that says nothing when no option matches
mistakes.right: empty says what to try next: No results. Try another word.

mistakes.wrong: Filtering only the exact spelling of Arabic names
mistakes.right: The shared normalize: أبها matches ابها, جدة matches جده

mistakes.wrong: Announcing the result count on every keystroke
mistakes.right: Once per query after typing pauses, in a polite status (built in)

mistakes.wrong: A Combobox with no Field and no aria-label
mistakes.right: A Field label, or aria-label: the input and its list both need a name

name: CommandPalette
summary: A modal search box over the page that finds a command by name and runs it. It opens from anywhere with Mod+K (Command K on a Mac, Control K elsewhere) or from a trigger Button.
useWhen: An app with more commands than its toolbars and menus can show at once
Power users who work from the keyboard and know the names of the actions they want
Jumping to a place by name: a board, a page, a setting
avoidWhen: The only way to reach an action: every command must also live in a visible menu, toolbar or page
Picking a value for a form field
A site search over documents or records with filters and rich results
An app with a handful of actions that all fit in a toolbar

parts.CommandPaletteTrigger: trigger (outside the root): one system Button, asChild, says the shortcut through aria-keyshortcuts

onOpenChange.description: Called with true for the shortcut and the trigger, false for Escape, a backdrop click and a run.

items.description: The commands, plain or in titled groups ({ label, commands }). A command: value (unique), label (verb plus noun), description, start (an icon name or a node), shortcut (its own shortcut, drawn as keycaps), keywords (more words it is found by), disabled, onRun.

onRun.description: Called with the value and the command after the command's own onRun. Commands run once the palette has closed and focus is back, so a command may move focus.

recent.description: Values of recently run commands, newest first. Shown as the first group while the query is empty. The app keeps the list.

recentLabel.description: Arabic default under lang ar: آخر الأوامر.

size.description: md 520px wide with 32px rows; lg 640px wide with 44px rows. Never wider than the viewport minus a gutter.

shortcut.description: Opens and closes the palette from anywhere on the page. Mod is Command on a Mac and Control elsewhere. A letter also matches by its physical key when the key typed is not a Latin letter or digit, so it works on an Arabic layout. Without Ctrl, Meta or Alt it is ignored in text fields. null turns it off. Only one palette on a page should keep it.

label.description: The accessible name of the dialog and of the list (a visually hidden title). Arabic default: لوحة الأوامر.

closeLabel.description: The accessible name of the close IconButton at the inline end of the search band. Arabic default: إغلاق لوحة الأوامر.

query.description: The query, controlled, with onQueryChange. Uncontrolled, it empties when the palette closes.

loading.description: A spinner in the search box and a polite status. With no commands yet, the list area says the loading label.

empty.default: No commands match. Try another word.
empty.description: Shown when no command matches. Say what to do next. An error with a retry Button goes here too.

formatCount.description: The announced result count. Default: 3 results, pluralized in Arabic with Western digits.

footer.description: The key hints at the bottom. false hides them. Default: move, run and close with their keycaps.

closeOnRun.description: false keeps the palette open after a run, for commands that toggle a setting.

rootProps.description: Props for the root layer. className and style go to the root too.

a11y.role: dialog (the panel), modal: Radix hides the rest of the page and keeps focus inside. The search input is a combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant; the list is a listbox of options, in groups when the commands are grouped.
a11y.focus: On open, focus goes to the search input and stays there: the highlighted command is pointed at with aria-activedescendant, rows never take focus. On close, focus returns to the element that had it when the shortcut opened the palette, or to the trigger that opened it; when that element is gone, to its nearest connected focusable ancestor, else the first tab stop of main.

keys.Mod+K: Opens the palette from anywhere on the page, and closes it, also from inside a text field. The shortcut prop changes or turns it off. A shortcut with no Ctrl, Meta or Alt (such as / or ?) types a character, so it is ignored while focus is in an input, a textarea, a select or contenteditable content (WCAG 2.1.4). A letter or digit also matches by its physical key only when the key typed is not a Latin letter or digit, as on an Arabic layout.
keys.ArrowDown: Highlights the next command, skipping disabled ones, and wraps from the last to the first
keys.ArrowUp: Highlights the previous command and wraps from the first to the last
keys.Enter: Runs the highlighted command and closes the palette
keys.Escape: Clears the query; on an empty query, closes the palette
keys.Tab: Moves from the search input to its clear button (there only while the box holds a query), then to the close button, and wraps inside the palette
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves back inside the palette and wraps from the first to the last

a11y.announce: The dialog is named by its label and the search box by the placeholder words. The result count is read once per query, after typing pauses, through a polite status. Loading is read by the SearchField status.
notes: Typing filters through filterListBoxItems: the label and the keywords, case and diacritics folded, Arabic letter forms folded (alef, yeh, teh marbuta), word starts first.
The highlight lands on the first enabled command when the palette opens and after every keystroke, so Enter runs the best match.
Each row with a shortcut carries aria-keyshortcuts; its keycaps are hidden from assistive tech.
The recent group shows only while the query is empty. A command in it is the same command as in its own group.
A pointer click on a row runs it without moving focus out of the search box.
The close IconButton is the pointer and touch way out next to Escape and the backdrop.
The trigger Button is optional: the shortcut alone opens the palette. A visible way in is still needed for touch and for people who do not know the shortcut.
No native title attribute.

en.label: Verb plus noun, sentence case: Create board, Invite people, Export as PDF. Never a bare noun for an action.
en.description: One short line that says what the command does when its name is not enough.
en.empty: Say what to do next: No commands match. Try another word.

ar.label: Noun form labels, no diacritics: إنشاء لوحة، دعوة أعضاء، تصدير PDF.
ar.empty: ما فيه أوامر مطابقة. جرب كلمة ثانية.
ar.digits: Western digits, Latin names (PDF) in place inside the Arabic line.

react.note: Built on DialogBase (Dialog folder) with a SearchField and a hand built listbox on the shared listbox logic (listbox.ts, filter.ts, shortcut.ts).

angular.behavior: cdk:portal, cdk:a11y ActiveDescendantKeyManager
angular.note: On the Angular Dialog layer, with the Angular SearchField.

native.note: A full screen sheet with the search on top; no global shortcut on touch, a visible trigger only.

styles.studio: A flat panel high on the screen: the solid surface, the panel radius, the dialog shadow. The search sits in a band on surface-2, borderless, with a line under it that turns into a 2px focus ring line while it has focus. Rows of the menu height light up with the overlay step; group titles are small and muted; a line separates groups. The hints sit in a footer band.
styles.desk: A glass window: the strong glass with a 24px blur, the window radius, a hairline inside, the deep window shadow. Bands are clear on the glass under hairlines. The lit row takes the yellow primary fill with dark text, as Desk menus do. It grows from 92% on the window open timing.
styles.neutral: Tokens only: the Neutral surface, borders and accent ring apply with no recipe.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass sheet.

mistakes.wrong: A command that exists only in the palette
mistakes.right: The same action in a visible menu or toolbar; the palette is a faster way to it

mistakes.wrong: Labels that are nouns, such as Settings or Board
mistakes.right: Verb plus noun: Open settings, Create board

mistakes.wrong: Two palettes on one page that both listen for Mod+K
mistakes.right: One palette per app; shortcut null on any other

mistakes.wrong: Moving focus inside a command's onRun while the palette is still open
mistakes.right: Let the palette run it: commands run after it has closed and focus is back, so focus moves stay

mistakes.wrong: A Kbd in the label text for the shortcut
mistakes.right: The command's shortcut field: it draws keycaps at the row end and sets aria-keyshortcuts

mistakes.wrong: Filtering the commands yourself and passing the result
mistakes.right: Pass every command: the palette filters with filter.ts, Arabic folding included, and marks the match

name: ConsentField
summary: One consent: a Checkbox or Switch whose label is one purpose, a link to the details, an optional record line, and a record of the choice handed to the app. Never ticked in advance.
useWhen: Asking for consent to one use of personal data, such as marketing email or sharing with a partner
A settings list where each use of data can be turned on or off at any time
A consent the service truly cannot work without, such as sharing health data with the clinic being booked
avoidWhen: Accepting terms of service or a contract, which is not consent to a use of data
A preference with no personal data in it, such as dark mode
Asking for several purposes with one control

purpose.description: One sentence that names one purpose. It is the control's label. Required.

checked.description: Controlled: a choice already on record. Needs onCheckedChange, so it can always be withdrawn. There is no defaultChecked.

onCheckedChange.description: Called with true when given, false when withdrawn.

onDecision.description: Called with a record: name, granted, version and the time as ISO 8601, for the app to store.

control.description: checkbox in a form that is sent, switch in settings that save at once.

name.description: The form name. Inside a Form, the Form's error for this name shows here.

value.description: The value sent while granted.

detailsHref.description: Where the details live: who gets the data, for how long, how to withdraw. Renders the details link.

detailsLabel.description: The details link text. Arabic default under lang ar.

detailsExternal.description: Opens the details in a new tab.

meta.description: A record line: the version of the text, or when the choice was made.

version.description: The version of the purpose text, passed back in the record.

required.description: The service cannot work without it. Shows an aria-hidden mark and sets aria-required.

disabled.description: Disables the control.

invalid.description: When not passed, invalid while an error shows. false hides the error.

error.description: An error shown now, for a required consent left off.

requiredError.description: Inside a Form, with name: the error when the Form finds this required consent left off. Registered with the Form by name, so the field and the summary show the same message. Default the Form's requiredChoice message, Tick this box to go on.

size.description: Control and text size.

a11y.role: checkbox or switch, from the control. The root has no role.
a11y.focus: The control is the one tab stop of the consent; the details link is the next.

keys.Tab: Moves to the control, then to the details link

a11y.announce: The purpose is the control's name (a native label and aria-labelledby). The record line and the error are read through aria-describedby. Nothing is live.
notes: Design note, not legal advice: the component follows the consent rules of the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) and its Implementing Regulations from SDAIA as a design aid only. Consent is explicit (an action by the person), specific (one purpose per control), never given in advance, and as easy to withdraw as to give. The purpose copy, the details page and whether consent is the right legal basis must be checked by someone qualified in PDPL for each product.
Never ticked in advance: there is no defaultChecked prop and the uncontrolled state starts denied. A test proves it.
Withdrawing is the same control and the same one action as giving. In settings, use control switch, so the change saves at once.
Keep the record: store what onDecision returns (granted, the text version, the time) with the account. In a form that is sent, store the last record when the form is sent.
The details link sits outside the label, so a click on it never toggles the consent.
Do not mark a marketing consent required. Required is for a consent the service truly cannot work without.
checked and unchecked are on the control part, a Checkbox or Switch root that carries the consent field control part. The consent root says granted or denied.

Development warnings catch what the types cannot: a stray defaultChecked, a controlled checked that starts true with no meta (show the record of the choice), disabled with checked true (a given consent must stay withdrawable), and no detailsHref when the surrounding Fieldset description has no link to the notice either.

en.purpose: A first person sentence that names one use and who gets the data: Share my order history with the delivery partner to plan delivery times. A list of data items for that one use is fine; two uses are two ConsentFields. Never a bundle joined with and.
en.details: Names the page: How we use your data. Never Learn more.
en.meta: The version or the date of the choice: You agreed on 3 November 2026. Text version 2.1.
en.error: Why it is needed and the other way: The booking needs this consent. Tick the box, or book by phone instead.

ar.purpose: جملة بصيغة المتكلم تبدأ بأوافق وتذكر استخدام واحد ومين يستلم البيانات: أوافق على مشاركة سجل طلباتي مع شريك التوصيل. تقدر تعدد البيانات لنفس الاستخدام، لكن كل استخدام له موافقة لحاله
ar.error: يوضح ليش مطلوبة والبديل: الحجز يحتاج موافقتك على المشاركة. حدد المربع أو احجز بالاتصال

react.behavior: hand built on Checkbox and Switch, FieldError as the error part, reads the Form error by name

angular.behavior: div[dsConsentField] host bindings, ControlValueAccessor with a boolean value; the error is p[dsFieldError] with its own DsFieldContext through viewProviders; reads the dsForm error for its name through DsFormContext
angular.note: No default checked: there is no defaultChecked input, a static checked does not type check and the state starts denied. onCheckedChange is the checkedChange output of [(checked)], onDecision is the decision output. The Checkbox and Switch are private stand ins with the React DOM until the A3 port merges. ConsentField.css is used as is.

styles.desk: The same layout, in Instrument Sans

name: Container
summary: Centers page content at a max width with a gutter on both inline sides.
useWhen: The content column of a page or a landing section, centered on wide screens
Capping the line length of reading text at a narrow width
Keeping the 16px phone gutter on any page content
avoidWhen: Inside a panel, card or dialog that already has its own padding
Laying out children in a row or columns
A full bleed band of color or media that must reach the screen edges
Inside another Container: the gutters add up

width.description: The max inline size, gutter included: sm 30rem (breakpoint.phone), md 48rem (breakpoint.tablet), lg 68.75rem (breakpoint.desktop), xl desktop plus half a phone (about 84rem), full no cap. Named width, not size, because size is the shared control axis. Sets data-width.

gutter.description: Padding on both inline sides, a space.* step. 3xl is 16px on phones in the default density. Sets data-gutter.

as.description: The element to render. One main per page.

children.description: The page content.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div, or the landmark of as
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: Nothing. A Container is layout only.
notes: Content never scrolls sideways at 320px: the width is a max, the box is 100% and the gutter sits inside it (WCAG 1.4.10).
Width sm keeps reading text near 70 characters a line.

ar.body: No copy of its own. The gutter is the same on both sides, so nothing changes in Arabic.

react.note: No motion: a static layout has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies.

angular.behavior: [dsContainer] attribute directive
angular.note: The host element is the root, so as is not needed.

native.behavior: react-native:View with maxWidth, alignSelf center and paddingHorizontal

styles.studio: Layout only.
styles.desk: Layout only. Pages sit inside windows, so a Container is mostly for site pages.
styles.neutral: Layout only.
styles.liquid: Layout only. Content scrolls under the glass bars; the gutter stays.

mistakes.right: No Container: the panel already pads its content

name: ContextMenu
summary: The actions of an item, opened on right click, a long press, or Shift+F10 and the Menu key on the focused item. The DropdownMenu surface and parts: items, checkbox and radio items, labels, separators and submenus.
useWhen: Shortcuts to the actions of an object people already work with by pointer: a file, a canvas layer, a table row
Dense work surfaces where a visible button per object would crowd the page, as long as each object also has a visible way to its actions
The same actions as an object's DropdownMenu, offered where the pointer already is
avoidWhen: The only way to reach an action: every action in a context menu must also be reachable without it, through a DropdownMenu on the item, a toolbar or a keyboard shortcut
Touch first screens where people do not know to press and hold
Primary actions that should be seen on the page
Choosing a value for a form field
Rich content or a small form in the panel

onOpenChange.description: ContextMenu: called with true on open and false on close (an item chosen, Escape, a click outside). There is no controlled open prop: the menu opens where the pointer or the focused item is.

modal.description: ContextMenu: true hides the rest of the page from assistive tech and blocks pointer input outside while open. Default false, as DropdownMenu: Tab never leaves the open menu and a click outside closes it.

size.description: ContextMenu: row height and type size. sm rows are 24px (size.control.xs), md rows follow menu.item.height (24, 28 and 32px in the compact, default and comfortable densities). Submenus take the size of their menu.

collisionPadding.description: ContextMenuContent and ContextMenuSubContent: the space kept from the viewport edge in px. Near an edge the menu flips to the other side of the pointer; it is never taller than the room left and scrolls inside.

ContextMenuItem.tone.description: An item's tone. danger marks a destructive action: the danger text color, and the label names what is destroyed. The menu root has no tone.

start.description: Items and the sub trigger: leading content, a system icon name or a node. Decorative: the text names the item. Rows without it line their text up with rows that have it.

end.description: Items: trailing content, a system icon name or a node. The sub trigger always shows chevron-forward here, mirrored in RTL.

shortcut.description: Items: a key hint shown at the inline end as plain text, left to right in every language (for example Ctrl+D). It does not bind the key; the app does.

disabled.description: Items: aria-disabled and data-disabled; the item stays in the menu, the arrow keys skip it and it does not select. ContextMenuTrigger: right click, long press and the keys open nothing, and the browser menu shows.

onSelect.description: Items: runs on click, Enter and Space, then the menu closes. Call event.preventDefault() to keep it open.

checked.description: ContextMenuCheckboxItem, with onCheckedChange. The check icon shows it, a minus for indeterminate.

value.description: ContextMenuRadioGroup, with onValueChange: the chosen ContextMenuRadioItem value.

textValue.description: Items: the text typeahead matches. Default: the label when it is plain text.

ContextMenuSub.description: A submenu: a ContextMenuSubTrigger, then a ContextMenuSubContent. open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange as on the root.

ContextMenuTrigger.description: One child element, the item the menu acts on (a file tile, a row, a layer), rendered as the trigger (always asChild) with data-state open or closed. It, or an element inside it, must take focus, so Shift+F10 and the Menu key can open the menu under it.

a11y.role: menu (the root and each submenu). Not modal by default: the page stays in the accessibility tree, Tab does not leave the open menu, and a click or focus outside closes it. Items are menuitem, menuitemcheckbox (aria-checked true, false or mixed) and menuitemradio inside a group. The trigger is the item itself and keeps its own role and name.
a11y.focus: Opened with Shift+F10 or the Menu key: the menu opens under the focused item and focus goes to the first item. Opened with the pointer: focus on the menu, the first arrow key goes to an item. The highlight follows the pointer and the keys. On close, focus returns to the element that had it.

keys.Shift+F10: On the focused item or an element inside the trigger, opens the menu under it with focus on the first item
keys.ContextMenu: The Menu key: the same as Shift+F10
keys.ArrowDown: Moves to the next item, skipping disabled ones
keys.Enter: On an item, selects it and closes the menu; on a sub trigger, opens the submenu
keys.ArrowRight: On a sub trigger, opens the submenu with focus on its first item. In right to left layouts this is ArrowLeft
keys.ArrowLeft: In a submenu, closes it and returns focus to its sub trigger. In right to left layouts this is ArrowRight
keys.Escape: Closes the menu, or only the open submenu, and returns focus to where it was
keys.Typeahead: Typing letters moves to the next item whose label starts with them

a11y.announce: The menu is read when it opens. Each item reads its label, its shortcut, its checked state and whether it is disabled or opens a submenu.
notes: Right click and the long press (700ms, touch and pen) open the menu at the pointer. Shift+F10 and the Menu key open it at the inline start and block end corner of the focused element, in every browser: the trigger handles both keys itself.
Nothing is reachable only through a context menu: the item also has a DropdownMenu (a More actions IconButton), a toolbar or a key. The demo shows the DropdownMenu on every tile.
Tab does not move focus while the menu is open (Radix keeps it in the menu); Escape or choosing an item returns focus to the element that had it.
Disabled items use aria-disabled: they stay in the menu, and the arrow keys skip them.
Checked state is shown by a check icon, a minus for indeterminate, never by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
A danger item is drawn in the danger text color and its label names the action (Delete board).
The menu opens toward the inline end of the pointer, so to the left in Arabic, and flips near the viewport edge. It never grows past the viewport and scrolls inside. Rows are at least 24px tall.
Contract keys: Shift+F10 and the Menu key are checked on a focused tile (focus moves into the menu). The other keys work inside an open menu and are covered by the unit tests.
The demo's Show menu buttons focus a tile and send Shift+F10, so the gallery and the contract suite can open the menu with a plain click.
No native title attribute.

en.items: Verb plus noun, sentence case: Rename board, Copy link. The same words as the item's DropdownMenu, in the same order.
en.label: A short noun over the group: Board, Sort layers by.
en.danger: Name what is destroyed: Delete board, never Delete alone.
en.count: Up to 12 entries at the top level, the most used first. Move the rest into a submenu.

ar.items: Noun form labels, white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: فتح اللوحة، إعادة تسمية اللوحة، حذف اللوحة.
ar.label: A short noun: اللوحة.
ar.shortcut: Key names stay in Latin letters and left to right: Ctrl+D.

react.note: Styled by DropdownMenu.css (the shared menu surface); no ContextMenu.css of its own. The content and each submenu are portaled into a Theme that copies the axes of the Theme the trigger is in. Shift+F10 and the Menu key are handled by the trigger.

angular.behavior: cdk:menu (cdkContextMenuTriggerFor)

native.note: Long press only; the actions also on a visible menu.

styles.studio: The DropdownMenu surface: surface-3, the card radius with concentric rows, the menu shadow, the overlay step on the lit row.
styles.desk: The Desk menu: the strong glass material and blur, a hairline, the panel radius, the yellow primary fill on the lit row. Solid under reduced transparency and more contrast.
styles.neutral: Planned: the DropdownMenu surface of the Neutral pack.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass menu, never on top of other glass.

mistakes.wrong: An action that only the context menu offers
mistakes.right: The same action on a DropdownMenu on the item, a toolbar or a key; the context menu is a shortcut

mistakes.wrong: A trigger that cannot take focus, such as a plain div
mistakes.right: A focusable item (tabindex 0 or a focusable child), so Shift+F10 and the Menu key reach the menu

mistakes.wrong: Different words in the context menu and the item's DropdownMenu
mistakes.right: The same labels in the same order

mistakes.wrong: A menu of 30 actions in one flat list
mistakes.right: Up to 12 entries: group with labels and separators, or move the rest into a submenu

mistakes.wrong: Replacing the browser menu on text people may want to copy
mistakes.right: Put the ContextMenuTrigger on the object, not on running text, or pass disabled

mistakes.wrong: A shortcut typed into the label: Duplicate board (Ctrl+D)
mistakes.right: The shortcut prop, which sets the hint apart and keeps it left to right

name: CopyButton
summary: Copies a value to the clipboard and confirms it once: the icon turns to a check and a hidden status says Copied.
useWhen: A command, a link, an id or a color the person will paste somewhere else
Beside a code block or a read only field that shows the value
An icon only copy control next to its value, named by label
avoidWhen: The value is long text the person edits first
Copying needs a choice of format
The value is not shown anywhere on the page

insteadUse.Share a link to people: Button that opens a share Dialog
insteadUse.Edit then copy: Input with a CopyButton at its end

value.description: The text to copy.

label.description: The action name: visible text, and always the accessible name (aria-label), so the name never changes while the label shows the result. Copy, or نسخ under an Arabic Theme. Name what is copied when it helps: Copy command.

iconOnly.description: Shows only the icon; label becomes the accessible name.

copiedLabel.description: What the label rolls to and the status says after a copy (تم النسخ in Arabic).

failedLabel.description: What the label rolls to and the status says after a failure (تعذر النسخ in Arabic).

target.description: The id of the element that shows the value. A failed copy selects its text, so the keyboard can copy it.

onCopied.description: Called with the value after it reached the clipboard.

onCopyFailed.description: Called with the value after the copy failed.

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px in the default density. A ButtonGroup passes its size; this prop wins.

emphasis.description: ghost: a copy control sits beside the value it copies.

shape.description: default takes radius.control (Desk draws it as a pill), pill is fully round, square takes radius.sm.

a11y.role: button
a11y.focus: In the tab order. Focus stays on the button through the copy.

keys.Enter: Copies the value
keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: A visually hidden polite status inside the button says Copied, or Could not copy, once per copy (WCAG 4.1.3): each copy writes a new text node, so a second copy is heard again, and the status is emptied when the button returns to idle. The visible words and the bubble are aria-hidden; the accessible name stays the label. No native title.
notes: The Clipboard API is called inside the click handler. Where it is missing or refused, a hidden textarea and the copy command are tried; if both fail, the state is failed and the target text is selected.
The result shows for delay.feedback, then the button returns to idle. Hold time, not motion: it is kept under reduced motion.
The result is not told by color alone: the icon changes from copy to check or warning, and the status says it.

Motion of round 3 (order 1.23, proposed, interaction copy-swap): the copy glyph closes into its centre (a circle clip and scale.morph) while the check wipes in along its strokes (clip-path) and pops on the bouncy spring, in the success text color; the warning pops in and the button shakes once after a failure. The label rolls from the action name to Copied (or the failure words) like a counter and rolls back after delay.feedback. The three words sit in one grid cell, so the button keeps the width of the widest and never changes size.
The icon only form shows a small aria-hidden bubble above the button with the result word; it rises in on the snappy spring and keeps rising as it fades.
A second copy restarts the hold time, draws the check again and replays the bubble. Everything is CSS on data-state: nothing waits for an animation.
Reduced motion (the system setting and data-motion reduce): CopyButton.css sets its own durations to 0s and turns every travel off, so each state shows at once; the status still says the result.

en.label: Copy, or Copy plus the thing: Copy command, Copy link.

ar.label: نسخ، أو نسخ مع الشيء: نسخ الرابط.

react.behavior: native button on ButtonBase, Clipboard API

angular.behavior: button[dsCopyButton] on DsButtonBase, the clipboard inside the click handler
angular.note: onCopied and onCopyFailed are the copied and copyFailed outputs. A (click) of the caller that calls preventDefault cancels the copy, as onClick does in React. The copy logic is a copy of the React copy.ts until it moves to packages/shared.

native.note: Announce through AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility.

styles.studio: Ghost by default; the check in the success color, the warning in the danger color.
styles.desk: Pill shaped; the same result colors.
styles.neutral: Tokens only.
styles.liquid: Planned.

mistakes.wrong: A toast for every copy
mistakes.right: The check and the hidden status of CopyButton

mistakes.wrong: A copy button with no visible value nearby
mistakes.right: Show the value, and pass its id as target

mistakes.wrong: A title tooltip that says Copied
mistakes.right: The status part; a Tooltip arrives in wave 1

name: DescriptionList
summary: Term and value pairs on a dl: the details of an order, a summary of settings, the facts about a record.
useWhen: Read only facts about one thing: order number, date, payment, total
A summary of settings before people confirm or edit them
Metadata in a side panel or a card: owner, created on, size
avoidWhen: Values people edit in place
Many records with the same fields, compared row by row
A single headline number
A list of rows people open or act on

insteadUse.Values people edit: Field with the matching control, in a form

orientation.description: horizontal: terms in a column at the start, values beside them; the column takes the longest term up to 40 percent and every item stacks under breakpoint.phone. vertical: each term above its value. Sets data-orientation.

size.description: Text size font.size s or m, with the gaps to match.

items.description: The pairs as data: an array of { key?, term, details }, where details is one node or an array of nodes (one dd each). Rendered before children.

children.description: DescriptionListItem elements: term, and the value as children or several values as details (each in its own dd).

a11y.role: None beyond the native dl, dt and dd. Each pair sits in a div, which HTML allows inside dl.
a11y.focus: Never focusable itself. Links or buttons inside a value keep their own focus.
a11y.announce: Screen readers read each term with its value. Some also say it is a list.
notes: Terms are nouns without a colon; the layout shows the pairing.
Values wrap anywhere, so a long URL or a long Arabic address never scrolls sideways at 320px.
Terms are muted text; check that a recipe keeps 4.5:1 on the surface the list sits on.
Latin codes inside Arabic values (order numbers, URLs) go through Bidi.
The stack under breakpoint.phone follows the viewport, not the list width; use vertical in a narrow panel.

en.term: A noun in sentence case, no colon: Order number, Delivery address.
en.details: The value as people read it: dates in words, amounts with the currency. An unset value says Not set.

ar.term: Noun form, no diacritics, no colon: رقم الطلب، عنوان التوصيل.
ar.details: Western digits. Latin codes such as GB-20481 stay left to right inside the value.

angular.behavior: dl[dsDescriptionList] and [dsDescriptionListItem], hand built

native.note: Rows of Text with the same props; no dl on native, so the role is text and pairs are read in order.

styles.studio: Muted terms, default text values, compact gaps.
styles.desk: The same on the Desk tokens in Instrument Sans.
styles.neutral: The same on the Neutral tokens; no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: Terms written as Order number: with a colon
mistakes.right: Order number; the columns pair the term and the value

mistakes.wrong: A table of two columns for one record's details
mistakes.right: DescriptionList, which screen readers read as pairs

mistakes.wrong: Inputs inside details to edit values in place
mistakes.right: A form with Field, or an edit button that opens one

mistakes.wrong: An empty dd for a missing value

name: Dialog
summary: A modal task that must be finished or dismissed. The page behind it is covered by a backdrop, hidden from assistive tech and out of reach until the dialog closes.
useWhen: A decision blocks the rest of the page
A short form of up to five fields
A destructive action that needs one more look before it runs
avoidWhen: Long content, or content compared with the page
A message that needs no decision
Work the person does next to the page, moving between both
An action that cannot be undone and must not be dismissed by accident

onOpenChange.description: Called with false for Escape, a backdrop click, the close control and DialogClose.

size.description: The width from the dialog.width tokens: 360, 440, 520, 640 and 820 px, never wider than the viewport minus a gutter.

tone.description: danger: a destructive decision. The title takes the danger color and focus opens on the Cancel action.

dismissible.description: false: only the dialog's own actions close it. Escape and a backdrop click do nothing and the close control is disabled (aria-disabled). For short waits while an action runs: the app sets it back to true when the action ends.

title.description: DialogContent: the title for the common case, the same as a DialogTitle as its first child.

description.description: DialogContent: the description for the common case.

closeLabel.description: DialogContent: the accessible name of the close control. Arabic default under lang ar: إغلاق النافذة.

controlsLabel.description: DialogContent: the accessible name of the Desk lights group.

rootProps.description: DialogContent: props for the root layer. className and style go to the root too; ref and every other prop go to the panel, the element with role dialog, Radix Content props included. The useful ones: onOpenAutoFocus (preventDefault to place focus yourself), onCloseAutoFocus (preventDefault and focus another element when the trigger is gone, for example after a delete), onEscapeKeyDown (preventDefault to keep the dialog open, for example while a field holds unsaved text).

DialogTrigger.description: One child element, a system Button, rendered as the trigger (always asChild). It opens the dialog, gets aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls, and takes focus back on close.

DialogClose.description: One child element, a system Button, that closes the dialog (always asChild). It is marked data-dialog-cancel: in a danger dialog focus opens on it. Wrap only the Cancel action.

data-autofocus.description: Put on any focusable element inside the dialog to take focus on open, before every other rule of the focus rule.

a11y.role: dialog (the panel), modal: Radix hides the rest of the page from assistive tech and keeps focus inside. Named by the title (aria-labelledby), described by the description (aria-describedby).
a11y.focus: On open, focus goes to an element marked data-autofocus; else to the first field in the body; else to the first footer action that is not tone danger; when tone is danger, to the Cancel action (the DialogClose) or else the first footer action that is not tone danger, never a destructive one; else to the close control. On close, focus returns to the trigger, or to the element that had focus before the dialog opened; when that element is gone, to its nearest connected focusable ancestor, else the first tab stop of main, else the body.

keys.Escape: Closes the dialog, unless dismissible is false. Escape from inside the dialog closes the dialog even while a toast shows above it. A nested dialog or a menu on top closes first.
keys.Tab: Moves to the next control inside the dialog and wraps from the last to the first
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves to the previous control inside the dialog and wraps from the first to the last

a11y.announce: The title and the description are read when the dialog opens. The close control and the Desk lights carry their own labels.
notes: role dialog in every tone. A danger dialog stays a dialog: AlertDialog arrives in wave 1 for actions that cannot be undone.
The page behind does not scroll while the dialog is open (Radix scroll lock); pinch zoom stays on.
A body taller than dialog.height-max scrolls inside, and joins the tab order while it scrolls so the keyboard can scroll it. The title and the footer stay in view.
A click on the backdrop closes the dialog, unless dismissible is false. The close control is the button path for the same action.

Toasts sit above an open dialog (z.toast over z.dialog): they stay visible, their live region is not hidden from screen readers, and a pointer click on a toast action or close button works without closing the dialog. Keyboard focus stays in the dialog: F8 and Tab do not reach the toasts (DECISIONS.md, Components 1). Toasts with an action or the danger tone never time out, so they are still there when the dialog closes.
A dialog opened from a dialog stacks above it; Escape closes the top one first and focus returns to its trigger in the first.
The long title wraps, never cut: it is the question being asked.
No native title attribute.

In Desk the title and the close control sit inside the title bar, so they are parts of TitleBar and WindowControls there (a part belongs to the nearest root). The dialog's own parts in Desk are titlebar, description, body and footer; title, close and controls are listed here for Studio and for style.json optionalParts.

dismissible false is for short waits, while the dialog's own action runs. The app must set it back to true when the action ends, success or failure. The close control (the Studio CloseButton or the Desk close light) is aria-disabled and stays focusable.
Development builds warn in the console when a dialog opens with no title, and when its footer holds more than three actions.

A form in a dialog: the form element lives in DialogBody with an id and an onSubmit; the submit Button sits in DialogFooter with type="submit" and form={id}, so Enter in a field and the button both submit. Close the dialog from onSubmit when the save succeeds, not from a DialogClose around the submit button.

Order 1.23 motion: the backdrop blurs the page in (backdrop-filter, a solid scrim where it is missing, under reduced transparency and more contrast); the parts read within 200ms. With dismissible false a backdrop press or Escape is refused: the panel nudges once along the inline axis (interaction dialog-refuse), never under reduced motion.

en.title: The question being asked, in sentence case: Delete the project Spring launch? A task title is fine for a form: Create a board.
en.description: One sentence that says what happens: Its 12 boards go to the trash for 30 days.
en.buttons: Verb plus noun: Delete project, Keep project. Never OK, Yes, Continue or Confirm. Cancel first, the primary action last.

ar.title: The question in white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: تبي تحذف المشروع؟
ar.buttons: Noun form labels, no diacritics: حذف المشروع، إبقاء المشروع. Never نعم or موافق.

react.note: The portal is a Theme that copies the axes of the Theme the Dialog is in (the Toaster pattern), so tokens, language and direction apply inside it.

angular.behavior: cdk:portal, cdk:a11y InteractivityChecker
angular.note: Directives dsDialog (on an ng-container), dsDialogTrigger, dsDialogContent (an ng-template), dsDialogClose, dsDialogBody, dsDialogFooter, dsDialogTitle, dsDialogDescription. The layer renders through a CDK ComponentPortal straight into body, so the DOM equals React's: no cdk-dialog-container and no overlay pane. The portal theme copies every axis of the opening dsTheme. Focus trap on the CDK InteractivityChecker; exit waits for getAnimations. The panel also carries aria-modal. Dialog.css is used as is. Order 1.23: dialog-refuse plays React's WAAPI shake on a backdrop press or Escape when dismissible is false; there is no Angular AlertDialog for the alert form.

native.note: Renders as a sheet on phones

styles.studio: A flat panel: the solid surface, the panel radius, the dialog shadow. The title sits in a band on surface-2 with a line under it and the CloseButton (part close) at its inline end; the footer is a band on surface-2 with a line over it. The backdrop is the scrim with a light blur. The panel rises 4px and scales up from 98% on duration.base.
styles.desk: Renders as a window with traffic lights: glass with a 24px blur, radius 1rem, a hairline inside, the deep window shadow. The title bar (optional part titlebar) starts with the lights (optional part controls): only the close light works, minimize and zoom are idle and out of the tab order, and the close light is part close. The title sits in the bar and wraps when long. The window grows from 92% on the window open timing. In right to left layouts the lights stay at the top left and the title is centered.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass sheet.
