mistakes.right: A toast

mistakes.wrong: Buttons that say OK and Cancel
mistakes.right: Verb plus noun: Delete project and Keep project

mistakes.wrong: Focus on the destructive button of a danger dialog
mistakes.right: tone danger and the Cancel action in DialogClose: focus opens on it

mistakes.wrong: A DialogTitle wrapped in a div inside the body
mistakes.right: DialogTitle as a direct child of DialogContent, or the title prop, so it renders once at the top and in the Desk title bar

mistakes.wrong: Hiding the close button in Desk with CSS
mistakes.right: The style turns the titlebar and controls parts on in style.json; Dialog then renders the close light instead of the CloseButton

mistakes.wrong: A dialog that closes while its action is still saving
mistakes.right: dismissible false and the primary Button loading until the action ends

mistakes.wrong: Waiting for animationend before removing a closed dialog
mistakes.right: Dialog.css sets the animations to none under reduced motion, so Radix removes the dialog at once

mistakes.wrong: A <form> that wraps the whole DialogContent, or a submit Button inside DialogClose
mistakes.right: <form id="rename" onSubmit={save}> inside DialogBody; <Button type="submit" form="rename" tone="accent" emphasis="solid"> in DialogFooter; close on success

name: Dock
summary: A row of app shortcuts at the block end of the screen: Desk's glass dock with a magnify effect, a plain row of icon tiles in other styles.
useWhen: A desktop style shell with a set of apps the person opens and switches between
App shortcuts that show which apps are open
A launcher row of up to about a dozen destinations with strong icons
avoidWhen: Bottom navigation on a phone
Commands that act on the current content
Destinations whose icons do not say what they are
Main site navigation

aria-label.description: Dock: required unless aria-labelledby is set. Names the landmark: Apps.

size.description: Dock: md tiles are size.control.lg (44px); lg tiles are 1.25 times that, for a desktop home screen.

label.description: DockItem: the app name. It is the link text, drawn above the tile on hover and focus; never only a native title.

icon.description: DockItem: a system icon name drawn in a tile, or a node such as an app image (decorative, empty alt).

href.description: DockItem: the app's route. An app that opens a window still has one (a route or a hash) and handles onClick.

active.description: DockItem: the current page belongs to this app. aria-current page, data-active and a ring on the tile.

open.description: DockItem: the app has an open window. data-open, the dot under the tile, and the word open in the name.

openLabel.description: DockItem: the words the open state adds to the name: Files, open. Arabic: مفتوح.

asChild.description: DockItem: renders its one child element (a router link) as the item.

a11y.role: navigation (the nav landmark) with a name; each item is a link, the current app's with aria-current page. Separators are decorative.
a11y.focus: Every item is a tab stop, in reading order. Focus shows the ring on the tile and draws the name.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next app
keys.Enter: Follows the link, or runs the item's onClick
keys.Escape: Hides the drawn name of the focused app, and of the hovered app wherever focus is (the item listens on the document while hovered), until focus or the pointer leaves

a11y.announce: Each link reads the app name, open when the app is open, and current page for the current app.
notes: The name is always the link text (WCAG 2.4.4, 4.1.2). It is drawn on hover and focus with opacity, so it is read at all times; no native title attribute.
Open is shown by the dot and said in the name; current is shown by a ring on the tile and aria-current, never by color alone.
The current app ring is 2px in the default text color: 6.57:1 or better against its tile and 12.59:1 or better against the dock in Studio, Desk and Neutral, dark and light (WCAG 1.4.11).
Magnify (Desk) scales the tile with transform only and is off under reduced motion; the name still appears.
A fixed dock covers content unless the page keeps the same room at its block end (WCAG 2.4.11): the layout (PageShell) reserves it.
Tiles are 44px at md (WCAG 2.5.8).
Many apps wrap onto a second row rather than scroll the page sideways (WCAG 1.4.10).

The first and the last item anchor the name to the tile's inline edge, so an edge name grows into the dock and stays inside a 320px viewport (WCAG 1.4.10). The name sits above the tile at its magnified size, so it never covers the tile or its ring.
Every item is a link. The order allows buttons; a system Button would own the item's parts, so an app that opens a window keeps an href and handles onClick.

The drawn name is dismissable (Escape, heard on the document while the item is hovered), hoverable (the pointer can move from the tile onto the name: the name takes the pointer while it shows and an undrawn bridge covers the gap) and persistent until focus or the pointer leaves (WCAG 1.4.13). It is a part of the link, not a Tooltip, because it is the link's own text.
The demo case many shows the reserved room: the page pads its block end and its scroll padding by the dock's height (size.control.lg plus the dock padding).
Contract keys: Escape sets data-label-hidden on the item, a part, which the generic suite does not watch; the unit tests cover it.

en.label: The app name, a noun, sentence case: Files, Mail, Calendar.

ar.label: Noun form labels, white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: الملفات، البريد، التقويم.

react.note: The name fades in on hover and focus (the opacity half of fade-rise; the rise is left out so the name sits still over a moving tile). Desk magnifies the tile with a transform. Both collapse under reduced motion. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction dock-lift: the tile lifts toward the pointer on the bouncy spring, the next tiles follow at a half and a quarter, and a tile that becomes current pops (animation-composition add). Reduced motion: nothing moves.

angular.behavior: hand built

native.note: A desktop shell part. Phone layouts use TabBar.

styles.studio: A plain row: a surface-2 bar with a subtle hairline, overlay-10 tiles, no magnify.
styles.desk: Glass: the dock material with the glass blur, the window radius and soft window shadow, larger tile corners, and magnify: the tile under the pointer or focus grows 1.25 times and lifts, its neighbors 1.1 times. Solid under reduced transparency and more contrast; no magnify under reduced motion.
styles.neutral: Token driven; applies once the Neutral pack is merged.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass dock.

mistakes.right: label: the link text, drawn on hover and focus

mistakes.wrong: Open apps shown only by a brighter icon
mistakes.right: open: the dot, and the word open in the name

mistakes.wrong: A fixed dock over the last line of the page
mistakes.right: Reserve the dock's height at the end of the page

mistakes.wrong: A Dock as phone navigation
mistakes.right: TabBar

mistakes.wrong: Commands in the dock: Save, Share
mistakes.right: Toolbar

name: Drawer
summary: A full height panel over the page at the inline end or start, for a secondary task such as filters or the details of a selected item. Modal by default; non modal keeps the page usable next to it.
useWhen: Filters or settings for the list or canvas on the page
The details of a selected item, read next to the page (modal false)
A form too long for a Dialog that still belongs to the current page
avoidWhen: A short decision or a form of a few fields
Phone layouts where the panel should rise from the bottom
Navigation between sections of the app
A question about an action that cannot be undone

onOpenChange.description: Called with false for Escape, a backdrop click, the close control and DrawerClose.

size.description: The width from the dialog.width tokens: 360, 440, 520 and 640 px. Under breakpoint.phone it fills the width.

side.description: The edge it comes from, in reading order: end is the right in English and the left in Arabic.

modal.description: true: a backdrop covers the page, focus stays inside and the page does not scroll. false: no backdrop, no focus trap, and a click on the page keeps the drawer open.

dismissible.description: false: Escape and a backdrop click do nothing and the close control is aria-disabled. For short waits while an action runs.

title.description: DrawerContent: the title for the common case, the same as a DrawerTitle child.

description.description: DrawerContent: the description for the common case.

closeLabel.description: DrawerContent: the accessible name of the close control. Arabic default under lang ar: إغلاق الشريط الجانبي.

rootProps.description: DrawerContent: props for the root layer. className and style go to the root too; ref and every other prop go to the panel, Radix Content props included.

DrawerTrigger.description: One child element, a system Button, rendered as the trigger (always asChild). Focus returns to it on close.

DrawerClose.description: One child element, a system Button that closes the drawer (always asChild), marked data-dialog-cancel.

data-autofocus.description: Put on any focusable element inside the drawer to take focus on open.

a11y.role: dialog (the panel). Modal by default: Radix hides the rest of the page from assistive tech and keeps focus inside. With modal false it is not modal: the page stays reachable. Named by the title, described by the description.
a11y.focus: The Dialog focus rule: an element marked data-autofocus, else the first field in the body, else the first footer action that is not tone danger, else the close control. On close, focus returns to the trigger, or to the element that had focus before.

keys.Escape: Closes the drawer, unless dismissible is false
keys.Tab: Modal: moves to the next control inside the drawer and wraps from the last to the first
keys.Shift+Tab: Modal: moves to the previous control inside the drawer and wraps from the first to the last

a11y.announce: The title and the description are read when the drawer opens. Loading and errors in the body use role status and role alert.
notes: data-side holds start or end; start is the right in Arabic, and the slide mirrors with the reading direction.
A body taller than the screen scrolls inside and joins the tab order while it scrolls. The header and the footer stay in view.
Toasts sit above an open drawer and stay readable and clickable, as with Dialog.

Non modal: Tab leaves the drawer for the page, as for any region. Escape from inside the drawer closes it; an Escape in a page field stays with that field. When the drawer closes while the person works on the page, focus stays where it is.
No native title attribute.
Order 1.23 motion: the backdrop blurs the page in as a dialog does. Swipe to dismiss is not built: the close control and Escape close it.

en.title: A noun phrase for the task: Filter boards, Board activity.
en.description: One sentence about what the drawer changes or shows.
en.buttons: Verb plus noun: Apply filters, Clear filters. Never OK or Continue.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics: فلترة اللوحات
ar.buttons: Noun form labels: تطبيق الفلاتر، مسح الفلاتر.

react.note: Built on DialogBase (Dialog folder). Styled by the drawer block of Dialog.css.

angular.behavior: cdk:portal, cdk:a11y InteractivityChecker
angular.note: On the Angular Dialog layer, with data-side and the header part.

native.note: Tablets only: a side panel. Phones use Sheet.

styles.studio: A full height surface panel with the inner corners rounded, the header band on surface-2 with the CloseButton, the footer band. It slides in from its side on duration.slow, ease.emphasized.
styles.desk: The Desk dialog glass, hairline and window shadow, with the window radius on the inner corners. The slide keeps duration.slow and ease.emphasized.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned.

mistakes.wrong: side left or right
mistakes.right: side start or end: the drawer mirrors in Arabic

mistakes.wrong: A drawer for a two button decision
mistakes.right: Dialog, or AlertDialog when it cannot be undone

mistakes.wrong: A modal drawer for details the person reads next to the page
mistakes.right: modal false

mistakes.wrong: Waiting for animationend before removing a closed drawer
mistakes.right: Dialog.css sets the animations to none under reduced motion, so Radix removes it at once

name: DropdownMenu
summary: A menu of actions or options that opens from a trigger button. Items, checkbox and radio items, labels, separators and submenus, with arrow keys, typeahead and Escape.
useWhen: More actions than fit next to the object they act on
A set of related commands behind one button, such as the actions of a board
Options that are switched on and off, or one chosen from a short set, next to the commands they change
avoidWhen: Choosing a value for a form field
Actions that need a right click to find
Rich content, a form or a picture in the panel
One or two actions that fit on the page as buttons
Navigation between pages of a site

open.description: DropdownMenu: controlled open state, with onOpenChange.

onOpenChange.description: DropdownMenu: called with true on open and false on close (an item chosen, Escape, a click outside).

modal.description: DropdownMenu: true hides the rest of the page from assistive tech (aria-hidden) and blocks pointer input outside while open. Default false: the menu button pattern needs neither, and axe flags focusable content under aria-hidden when no aria-modal dialog is open.

size.description: DropdownMenu: row height and type size. sm rows are 24px (size.control.xs), md rows follow menu.item.height (24, 28 and 32px in the compact, default and comfortable densities). Submenus take the size of their menu.

side.description: DropdownMenuContent: where the menu opens, in logical words. block-end is under the trigger; inline-end is after it in reading order, so on its left in Arabic. It flips to the other side when there is no room.

align.description: DropdownMenuContent: how the menu lines up with the trigger. start is the trigger's inline start edge, its right edge in Arabic.

sideOffset.description: DropdownMenuContent: the gap to the trigger in px.

collisionPadding.description: DropdownMenuContent and DropdownMenuSubContent: the space kept from the viewport edge in px. The menu is never taller than the room left: it scrolls inside.

loop.description: DropdownMenuContent: ArrowDown on the last item goes to the first.

DropdownMenuItem.tone.description: An item's tone. danger marks a destructive action: the danger text color, and the label names what is destroyed. The menu root has no tone.

start.description: Items and the sub trigger: leading content, a system icon name or a node. Decorative: the text names the item. Rows without it line their text up with rows that have it.

end.description: Items: trailing content, a system icon name or a node. The sub trigger always shows chevron-forward here, mirrored in RTL.

shortcut.description: Items: a key hint shown at the inline end as plain text, left to right in every language (for example Ctrl+D). It does not bind the key; the app does.

disabled.description: Items and DropdownMenuTrigger: aria-disabled and data-disabled. A disabled item stays in the menu, is skipped by the arrow keys and does not select. Drawn with opacity.disabled.

onSelect.description: Items: runs on click, Enter and Space, then the menu closes. Call event.preventDefault() to keep it open.

checked.description: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, with onCheckedChange. The check icon shows it, a minus for indeterminate.

value.description: DropdownMenuRadioGroup, with onValueChange: the chosen DropdownMenuRadioItem value.

textValue.description: Items: the text typeahead matches. Default: the label when it is plain text.

DropdownMenuTrigger.description: One child element, a system Button or IconButton, rendered as the trigger (always asChild). It gets aria-haspopup menu, aria-expanded and data-state, names the menu, and takes focus back on close.

DropdownMenuSub.description: A submenu: a DropdownMenuSubTrigger, then a DropdownMenuSubContent. open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange as on the root.

a11y.role: menu (the root and each submenu). Not modal by default: the page stays in the accessibility tree, Tab does not leave the open menu, and a click or focus outside closes it. Items are menuitem, menuitemcheckbox (aria-checked true, false or mixed) and menuitemradio inside a group. The trigger has aria-haspopup menu and aria-expanded, and names the menu (aria-labelledby).
a11y.focus: Opened with Enter, Space or ArrowDown on the trigger: focus on the first item. Opened with ArrowUp: focus on the last item. Opened with the pointer: focus on the menu, the first arrow key goes to an item. The highlight follows the pointer and the keys. On close, focus returns to the trigger.

keys.ArrowDown: On the trigger, opens the menu with focus on the first item. In the menu, moves to the next item, skipping disabled ones
keys.ArrowUp: On the trigger, opens the menu with focus on the last item. In the menu, moves to the previous item
keys.Enter: On the trigger, opens the menu. On an item, selects it and closes the menu; on a sub trigger, opens the submenu
keys.ArrowRight: On a sub trigger, opens the submenu with focus on its first item. In a submenu, nothing. In right to left layouts this is ArrowLeft
keys.ArrowLeft: In a submenu, closes it and returns focus to its sub trigger. In right to left layouts this is ArrowRight
keys.Escape: Closes the menu, or only the open submenu, and returns focus to the trigger
keys.Typeahead: Typing letters moves to the next item whose label starts with them

a11y.announce: The menu is read with the trigger's name when it opens. Each item reads its label, its shortcut, its checked state and whether it is disabled or opens a submenu.
notes: Tab does not move focus while the menu is open (Radix keeps it in the menu); Escape or choosing an item returns focus to the trigger.
Disabled items use aria-disabled: they stay in the menu so a screen reader user learns they exist, and the arrow keys skip them.
Checked state is shown by a check icon, a minus for indeterminate, never by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
A danger item is drawn in the danger text color; its label also names the action (Delete board), so color is never the only cue.
The menu never grows past the viewport: it takes the room Radix measures on the open side, minus collisionPadding, and scrolls inside. Rows are at least 24px tall (size.target-min).
Shortcut hints are plain text set left to right, so key names read the same inside Arabic.
The submenu chevron is chevron-forward and mirrors in right to left layouts; the submenu opens toward the inline end and Radix follows the direction set by Theme.

Contract keys: ArrowDown and ArrowUp are checked on the trigger (they open the menu and move focus). Home, End, Enter, Space, the submenu arrows and typeahead are covered by the unit tests, since the generic suite cannot press them inside an open menu.
No native title attribute.

en.trigger: Names the menu: a noun (Board actions, Edit) or a verb plus a noun. An icon only trigger names the object too: More frame actions, never only More.
en.items: Verb plus noun, sentence case: Duplicate board, Copy link. Options are nouns or short phrases: Show grid, Name. No ending punctuation, no ellipsis unless the item opens a dialog that asks for more.
en.label: A short noun over the group: Board, Sort by.
en.danger: Name what is destroyed: Delete board, never Delete alone or Remove.
en.count: Up to 12 entries at the top level. Group or split longer menus, or use a submenu.

ar.items: Noun form labels, white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: تكرار اللوحة، نسخ الرابط، حذف اللوحة.
ar.label: A short noun: اللوحة، الترتيب حسب.
ar.shortcut: Key names stay in Latin letters and left to right: Ctrl+D.

react.note: The content and each submenu are portaled into a Theme that copies the axes of the Theme the menu is in (the Toaster pattern), so tokens, language and direction apply inside. A submenu is its own root carrying data-part sub-content.

angular.behavior: hand built on the CDK (Portal, Directionality) with Radix DropdownMenu's keys and focus rules; positioning in behavior/popper.ts
angular.note: Root on an ng-container (dsDropdownMenu), dsDropdownMenuTrigger on the system button, the content and each submenu are ng-templates rendered through a CDK ComponentPortal whose host is the themed layer (data-menu-layer), as in React. onOpenChange, onCheckedChange and onValueChange are the openChange, checkedChange and valueChange outputs of [(open)], [(checked)] and [(value)]; onSelect is the select output and preventDefault keeps the menu open. The DOM keeps Radix's attribute and variable names (data-radix-popper-content-wrapper, --radix-dropdown-menu-content-*), which DropdownMenu.css reads. Not done: Radix's focus guard spans in body and the pointer grace area toward a submenu.

styles.studio: A flat surface: surface-3, the card radius (16px) with 12px rows inside, the menu shadow, no border. The lit row takes the overlay step; a danger row a danger tint. Rows use the menu weight. Separators on surface-2.
styles.desk: Glass, from the macOS style menu bar menu: the strong glass material with the strong blur, a hairline, the soft window shadow, the panel radius (12px) with 8px rows inside, regular weight. The lit row is the yellow primary fill with dark text, a danger row lights in the danger fill. Under reduced transparency and more contrast the glass turns solid and the blur goes.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass menu, never on top of other glass.

mistakes.right: Select, which shows the chosen value in the field

mistakes.wrong: An icon only trigger named More
mistakes.right: Name the object: More frame actions

mistakes.wrong: A checked option shown only by a colored label
mistakes.right: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem or DropdownMenuRadioItem: the check icon carries the state

mistakes.wrong: A menu of 30 actions in one flat list
mistakes.right: Up to 12 entries: group with labels and separators, or move the rest into a submenu

mistakes.wrong: A bare button or a div with onClick as the trigger
mistakes.right: A system Button or IconButton inside DropdownMenuTrigger

mistakes.wrong: Hiding an action that cannot run now
mistakes.right: disabled: the item stays in the menu with aria-disabled, and a Tooltip or the page says why

mistakes.wrong: A shortcut typed into the label: Duplicate board (Ctrl+D)

name: EmptyState
summary: A place with no content yet that says what is missing, what to do next and how, with the action that does it.
useWhen: A list, grid, table or panel that has no items yet, the first time someone opens it
A search or a filter that returns nothing, with live set so it is announced
A view that needs a first step from the person before it can show anything, such as connecting an account
avoidWhen: Something failed to load or save: that is an error, not an empty place
Content is still loading
A blocking message that needs a decision
A one word note inside a row or a field, such as None: write it as plain text

size.description: sm inside a list or a card, md for a panel, lg for a whole view. Sets the block padding (space xl, 6xl, 11xl), the icon box and the type sizes. The inline padding stays at space l or xl, so a narrow column keeps its width.

icon.description: A system icon name or a node, in a square on surface 2. 16px at sm, 24px at md and lg. Hidden from assistive tech.

title.description: What is empty, as a heading: No boards yet.

headingLevel.description: The heading level of the title.

children.description: The body: what to do next, naming the mechanism (Create a board, or drag a file onto this page).

actions.description: One or two Buttons. The first is the main action, a verb plus a noun, usually tone accent with emphasis solid.

live.description: Adds role status so the empty state is announced when it replaces content, such as a search with no results. Off for a place that is empty on page load.

a11y.role: None by default; status when live. The title is a heading.
a11y.focus: Not focusable. Tab reaches the actions, in order.

keys.Tab: Moves to the first action, then the next

a11y.announce: Read in order: title, body, actions. With live, the whole region (actions included) is announced once when it appears. Some screen readers miss a live region that mounts with its content; for a sure announcement, mount the EmptyState inside a live region that is already on the page.
notes: The icon is decoration and hidden; the title says what is empty.
Keep live off for a place that is empty when the page opens, so nothing is announced twice.
Shares icon, title, body and actions with ErrorState, which adds details and its own states.

en.title: Name what is missing, sentence case, no end period: No boards yet. For a search: No boards match Spring 2027.
en.body: Say what to do next and name the mechanism: Create a board to plan a project, or drag a file onto this page to import it. No blame, no exclamation marks.
en.actions: A verb plus a noun: Create board, Clear search. Never OK or Continue.

ar.title: White Saudi dialect, no diacritics: ما فيه لوحات.
ar.body: Say what to do next plainly, Western digits.
ar.actions: Noun form labels: إنشاء لوحة، استيراد ملف.

react.note: No motion of its own: fade-rise names how a parent brings it in, from the 1.11 catalog list.

angular.note: dsEmptyState on the host with icon, title and headingLevel inputs; body and actions projected. EmptyState.css as is.

native.note: A centered View with the same parts; the title with accessibilityRole header.

styles.studio: Centered, no surface of its own; the icon sits in a surface 2 square with radius.panel.
styles.desk: The same on Desk's surfaces and type. No recipe.
styles.neutral: Planned: no recipe expected.
styles.liquid: Planned: no recipe expected.

mistakes.wrong: A title that only says Nothing here
mistakes.right: Name what is missing and what to do: No boards yet, then Create a board

mistakes.wrong: An empty state shown while the data is still loading
mistakes.right: Skeleton until the request ends, then the empty state

mistakes.wrong: An empty state for a failed request
mistakes.right: ErrorState with a way to try again

mistakes.wrong: Three or more actions of equal weight
mistakes.right: One main action, at most one quiet one

name: ErrorState
summary: Stands in for a section or a page that failed to load: says what happened, what to do next, and offers a retry, with the error code behind a disclosure.
useWhen: A section, a panel or a page could not load its content
A load can be retried, or there is another way forward such as going back
Replacing skeletons after a load failed
avoidWhen: The content loaded but is empty
An action the person took failed and the page still works
A problem with one form field
A page wide notice that stays while the rest of the page works

title.description: What happened, naming the thing: Could not load members.

body.description: What to do next and what is safe.

icon.description: A system icon name, a node, or false for none. Hidden from assistive tech.

size.description: sm inside a card or panel, md for a section, lg for a whole page.

headingLevel.description: The heading level of the title, to fit the page outline.

onRetry.description: Renders the retry Button first in the actions (accent solid, refresh icon, data-part retry) and is called by it.

retryLabel.description: A verb plus a noun. Arabic default under lang ar: إعادة التحميل.

retrying.description: A retry is in flight: data-state retrying, and the retry Button shows loading with a hidden status.

retryingLabel.description: What the retry Button's hidden status says while retrying.

actions.description: More Buttons after retry, a verb plus a noun: Open boards.

code.description: The error code, inside the details disclosure, left to right in every language.

details.description: More detail inside the disclosure, after the code: a request id to send to support.

detailsOpen.description: Renders the details open at first.

live.description: role alert on the root with aria-atomic false, so an error that replaces content after load is read once. Off by default: an error present at page load must not shout, and the root is then role group named by its title, with no live role.

a11y.role: group named by its title (default); alert with aria-atomic false while live. The title is a real heading (h2 by default). The details part is a native details element.
a11y.focus: Focus does not move to it. Tab reaches the retry Button, the other actions, then the details summary.

keys.Tab: Moves to the retry Button, the other actions, then the details summary
keys.Enter: Runs the focused action, or opens and closes the details
keys.Space: Runs the focused action, or opens and closes the details

a11y.announce: With live, the role alert (aria-atomic false, so a retry does not read it all again) reads the title, body and actions once when the error replaces content after load. Retrying is said by the retry Button's hidden status (Retrying). An error present at page load is not announced, which is the default; pass live when the error replaces content after load. The default words follow the lang prop, else the Theme language.
notes: The retry Button stays focusable while retrying (aria-disabled through loading), so focus is not lost.
The summary is at least 24px tall (WCAG 2.5.8) and draws the focus ring from the focus tokens.

en.title: Say what failed and name the thing: Could not load members. Not Oops or Something went wrong alone.
en.body: What to do next and what is safe: Check your connection, then retry. Your draft is safe.
en.actions: A verb plus a noun: Retry loading, Open boards. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes.
en.code: The code as the system gives it, for support. Not the only explanation.

ar.title: Noun forms, no diacritics: تعذر تحميل الأعضاء.
ar.actions: Noun form labels: إعادة التحميل، فتح اللوحات.
ar.code: The code stays left to right; Western digits.

angular.behavior: div[dsErrorState], host bindings, cdk:a11y _IdGenerator
angular.note: The host element is the root. title, body, actions and details take a string or a TemplateRef; icon takes an icon name, a TemplateRef or false. onRetry is a function input: the retry Button renders only with a handler. The heading level picks h2 to h6. The title id comes from the CDK id generator. ErrorState.css is used as is.

native.note: The details disclosure becomes a pressable row that shows the code.

styles.studio: Tokens only: a danger tint tile behind the icon, muted body text.
styles.desk: Tokens only; the retry Button is the yellow primary.
styles.neutral: Tokens only.

mistakes.wrong: Something went wrong, with nothing else
mistakes.right: Could not load members. Check your connection, then retry.

mistakes.wrong: The error code as the only message
mistakes.right: Plain words first; the code behind Error details

mistakes.wrong: A retry that blanks the section while it runs
mistakes.right: Keep the ErrorState with retrying set, then swap in skeletons or content

mistakes.wrong: ErrorState for a list that loaded with no items
mistakes.right: EmptyState

name: Field
summary: Wires one label, one description and one error message to one form control, and passes the invalid, disabled, read only and required state to it.
useWhen: Any form control that needs a visible label
A control with a hint that helps fill it, or an error that says how to fix the value
A settings row with the label at the start and the control at the end (orientation horizontal)
avoidWhen: A search box in a toolbar whose purpose is plain from an icon and an aria-label
A group of checkboxes or radios that shares one question
Read only text that is not a control

orientation.description: vertical: label above the control. horizontal: label at the start of the control's line.

invalid.description: Marks the control invalid. When not passed, the field is invalid while an error message shows. false hides the error.

disabled.description: Passed to the control.

readOnly.description: Passed to the control. Still focusable and readable.

required.description: Shows the required mark and sets aria-required on the control.

label.description: One line API: renders FieldLabel, the system Label with data-part label.

error.description: One line API: renders the system FieldError with data-part error.

floating.description: A floating label: the label rests inside the control's box while it is empty and has no focus, and rises above it on focus or with a value. The label renders after the control. Use with the label prop and one single line control.

a11y.role: none on the root. The label is a native label bound to the control with for and id.
a11y.focus: The root is never focusable. Clicking the label focuses the control.

keys.Tab: Moves to the control. The field adds no stop of its own.

a11y.announce: The description, then the error, are read with the control through aria-describedby when focus lands there. The error is not a live region and never role alert, so an error that is there when the page loads does not interrupt.
notes: The required mark is an asterisk glyph, so it does not rely on color, and it is aria-hidden. The control carries aria-required, not the native required attribute, so the browser shows no validation bubble.
The error starts with a danger icon, so it does not rely on color.
Controls read the wiring with useFieldControl(): id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, aria-required, disabled and readOnly. A value the control passes itself wins.
A form that checks on submit moves focus to the first invalid control.
Validate on blur or on submit, never on every key. On submit, move focus to the first invalid control.
The label part is a Label root (data-ds label) and the error part a FieldError root (data-ds field-error). The required mark and the error icon belong to those components' anatomy.

The error part of a Field, through the error prop or as a child
An error for a group of choices, under a Fieldset

a11y.focus: Never focusable. On submit the form moves focus to the first invalid control, which reads the error.
a11y.announce: Read with the control through aria-describedby when focus lands there. The control carries aria-invalid. Inside a Field both are wired while the error renders.
notes: Never color alone: a danger icon and words. The icon is aria-hidden; the words carry the meaning.
Not a live region and never role alert: an error that is on the page when it loads must not interrupt, and a screen reader reads it with the control.
Rendered only when there is an error, so it has no state attributes. invalid false on the Field hides it.

name: Fieldset
summary: A group of fields or choices under one legend: a native fieldset, so the legend names the group and native disabled disables everything inside.
useWhen: Several fields that answer one question together, such as a delivery address or a date of birth in three parts
A long form split into named sections, each with its own legend
A group of Checkbox or Switch items that needs a group level error, such as Pick at least one. Inside a Form, set name to the name the controls share.
Turning off a whole section at once with native disabled
avoidWhen: One field alone: the legend would repeat its label
A group of checkboxes with one value array
A heading over unrelated content that holds no controls
A form split into steps the person moves through

legend.description: The name of the group, in a native legend. Required.

description.description: A hint under the legend. Joins the group's aria-describedby.

error.description: What is wrong with the group as a whole and how to fix it. Renders a FieldError root with data-part error, above the body.

name.description: The name the controls of a checkbox or radio group share. Inside a Form, the Form's error for that name shows in the error part, in place of error. Rendered as data-name, not as the fieldset name attribute.

size.description: Legend size and the space between the fields.

disabled.description: Native disabled: every control inside is disabled, buttons included. The body takes the one disabled look.

invalid.description: When not passed, the group is invalid while it shows an error. false hides the error.

a11y.role: group, from the native fieldset, named by the legend
a11y.focus: The fieldset is never focusable. Each control inside is its own tab stop, in DOM order.

keys.Tab: Moves to the first control in the group, then on through the controls. The group adds no stop of its own.

a11y.announce: The legend is read with the first control when focus enters the group. The description and the group error are read through the group's aria-describedby. The error is not a live region and never role alert.
notes: The legend is a native legend, the first child of the fieldset, so every browser and screen reader takes it as the group name.

The group error sits above the body, so it is seen before a long list of choices. Inside a Form, give the Fieldset the name its controls share: a Form validator error for that name then shows in the error part, the summary link names the group by its legend, and focus on submit moves to the first control of the group.
Native disabled reaches every control inside, including the Radix Checkbox and Switch buttons, without a prop on each.
Keep the legend short: some screen readers read it again before every control in the group.
The controls inside do not get aria-invalid from the group yet. The error reaches a screen reader through the group's aria-describedby, which some readers skip on entry.

en.legend: A noun phrase or a question in sentence case that names the group: Delivery address, How should we reach you. No colon.
en.description: One sentence that helps fill the group. Not a repeat of the legend.
en.error: What to do with the group: Pick at least one way to reach you. Never only Required.

name: FilterBar
summary: The row above a list: a search box, quick filter chips, more filters in a menu, the active filter count, clear all, and an end slot for view toggles. One value array holds every filter that is on.
useWhen: A list, grid or table the person narrows with a search and a few filters
Quick filters that are on or off, with rarer ones tucked in a menu
A gallery or file browser with view toggles at the end of the filter row
avoidWhen: Picking one view from a few, such as All, Mine, Shared
Filters that each need a range, a date or a typed value
A search that opens a list of suggestions to pick from

search.description: Props for the search box, aria-label included. Leave it out for no search.

filters.description: Quick filters as chips: value, label, textValue, disabled.

more.description: Rarer filters, as checkbox items in the more menu. The menu stays open while the person picks.

value.description: Controlled: the values of every filter that is on, from the chips and the menu.

defaultValue.description: Uncontrolled starting value.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new list of values.

onClear.description: Called by clear all, after the value and the search box are cleared.

resultCount.description: The results the filters leave. Shown in the count part, and announced once when it changes after a filter or search change.

end.description: View toggles or a sort menu, at the end of the row.

size.description: Height of the search box, the chips and the buttons.

labels.description: Copy for the group name, more, clear and the counts. Default from the Theme language, English or Arabic.

a11y.role: none on the root. The chips sit in a role group named Filters; each chip is a toggle button with aria-pressed.
a11y.focus: Each part is a tab stop in DOM order: search, each chip, more, clear, then the end slot. When clear all is used it hides, and focus moves to the search box, else the first chip.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next part, and to each chip in turn
keys.Space: Turns the focused chip on or off

a11y.announce: The result count is read once, politely, when resultCount changes after a filter or search change, 600ms after the last such change: typing does not read every count, and a slow count is not read stale. A change that leaves the count the same is not announced. Each chip says pressed or not pressed.
notes: The order names ToggleGroup, MultiSelect and Select. They do not exist yet, so filters are Chips in a role group and more is a DropdownMenu with checkbox items. Arrow keys do not move between chips: each chip is a tab stop, as in the Figma-Killer-2 source. The anatomy stays when ToggleGroup lands.

The chip strip scrolls sideways inside itself and never scrolls the page at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10). The root carries data-overflow-start and data-overflow-end in logical terms, so the edge fades flip in RTL.
A selected chip shows a check, not color alone.
Each selected chip carries data-selected on its own Chip root; that state belongs to the Chip manifest, not to this one.

open and closed are data-state on the more part, the Button that opens the DropdownMenu; they stay in states because the contract suite reads data-state on every part. Escape in the search box clears the query; Escape in the more menu closes it and returns focus to the more button.
A search query counts as one filter on in the count part, and clear all empties it too.
The FilterBar root carries data-active and the overflow states; open and closed are on the more part. data-selected sits on the Chip roots and belongs to the Chip manifest.

en.filters: One to three words in sentence case, a noun: Images, Shared with me. Never a verb.
en.more: More filters, with the number on in brackets: More filters (2). An agreed exception to the verb plus noun rule: it is the usual name for a menu trigger, like Next page.
en.count: 1 filter on, 2 filters on (a search query counts as one), then the results: 24 results. No results when none.

On glass or over a floating bar

a11y.focus: In the tab order where it sits in the DOM: render it after the content it acts on. The doubled focus ring.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

Reduced motion: no lift, no slide, no reveal.

name: Form
summary: A native form that checks on submit, lists the errors in a summary with links to the fields, moves focus to the first invalid field, announces the result once and maps server errors to fields by name.
useWhen: Any set of fields sent together with one submit button
A form that needs custom checks next to the browser's own (type, pattern, required)
A form whose server answer can say which field is wrong
A short form inside a Dialog, with the submit Button in the footer
avoidWhen: A long form the person fills over several steps
One setting that saves the moment it changes
A search box or a filter row that updates a list as the person types

size.description: Space between the fields and the parts. Shared with the fields through useFormContext().

orientation.description: The default orientation of every FormField: label above, or label at the start of the line.

validators.description: Custom checks by field name. An empty required field keeps the required message; otherwise a validator message wins over the built in constraint copy, so a validator can name the format: Enter the 5 digit postal code.

onSubmit.description: Called with the values when every check passes. May return server errors in any shape mapServerErrors reads; a promise keeps the form in submitting.

onErrors.description: Called with the field errors each time a submit finds some.

serverErrors.description: Errors from outside, such as a server action rendered with the page. Shown without moving focus.

actions.description: The buttons, in the actions part. FormSubmit first.

labels.description: Copy for the summary, the submitted announcement and the built in errors: required, requiredChoice (a box left off), requiredOption (a radio group with nothing picked), and one message per ValidityState flag (typeMismatch, patternMismatch, tooShort, tooLong, rangeUnderflow, rangeOverflow, stepMismatch, badInput). Default from the Theme language, English or Arabic. The browser validationMessage is never shown.

a11y.role: form, the native element. Give it aria-label or aria-labelledby when the page has more than one form.
a11y.focus: On a submit with errors, focus moves to the first invalid field in form order; when no field can take it, to the summary. Values are kept.

keys.Tab: Moves through the fields, then the actions. The form adds no stop of its own.
keys.Enter: In a single line field, submits the form through its submit button. On a summary link, moves focus to that field.

a11y.announce: Once per submit with errors, a polite status says how many fields to fix (WCAG 4.1.3). After a submit that passes, the same status says the form was sent (labels.submitted, empty to say nothing). The summary itself is not a live region, so nothing is read twice. Each field reads its error through aria-describedby when focus lands on it.
notes: Hand built on the native form with noValidate: the browser bubble never shows, and type, pattern, min and maxLength still feed the check through checkValidity(). Each failure is read from its ValidityState flag and gets copy from labels in the page language; the browser validationMessage is never used, since it is in the browser language and does not say how to fix the value.

An empty control with native required or aria-required (Field sets aria-required) gets the required message: requiredChoice for a checkbox or switch, requiredOption for a radio group, required for the rest. A ConsentField requiredError replaces it for that name, in the field and in the summary.
After a submit, a change that fixes a field removes its error at once. A change never adds an error: checks run on submit.
autocomplete is never changed and values are never cleared on an error, so nothing is asked twice (WCAG 3.3.7, 3.3.8).
aria-busy is true while onSubmit runs, and FormSubmit shows its loading state.

A form in a Dialog: the form sits in DialogBody with an id, and the submit Button in DialogFooter takes form set to that id and type submit. Enter in a field still submits. That footer Button is outside the Form context, so it shows no loading state: give it loading from your own state when onSubmit is slow.
The action prop is not taken: the form checks before it sends, and React does not run an action on a submit that is stopped. Call the server action from onSubmit and return its errors.
When onSubmit throws, the summary says the form could not be sent and focus moves to it. Values are kept.
Read only controls, hidden inputs and controls in a disabled Fieldset are not checked.

Several checkboxes or radios with one name are one group: the summary link takes the legend of the nearest Fieldset, and a Fieldset with the same name shows the error in its error part. Without that Fieldset name the error shows only in the summary.

en.submit: A verb plus a noun that names the result: Send request, Save address, Create account. Never Submit, OK or Continue.

en.errors: Each says what to do with the field: Add your city. Use your work email, not a personal one. For a pattern, a validator that names the format: Enter the 5 digit postal code.
en.required: Say once, above the form, that fields marked * are required.

name: FormWizard
summary: A long form split into steps: a Stepper, one panel per step, back and next, a review step and a submit at the end. Each step is checked before the user moves past it.
useWhen: A form with more than about eight fields that falls into three to seven groups with an order: checkout, onboarding, an application
Later steps depend on answers in earlier ones, so the user should finish them in order
The user should check every answer on a review step before sending
avoidWhen: A short form that fits on one screen
Settings the user changes one at a time, in any order
Steps that are separate tasks and save on their own

insteadUse.Settings in any order: Tabs with a Form per tab

steps.description: One entry per step: id, title (a short noun), description, content (a node, or a function of { values, errors } to show errors and the review), validate (values to errors by field name, may be async), nextLabel, backLabel.

mode.description: Passed to the Stepper. linear: a later step opens only when the ones before it passed their check. free: any step; moving forward still checks the current step, and submit checks every step. Read once, at mount, with the number of steps.

onSubmit.description: Called with every value of every step when the last step is sent. While a promise runs the state is submitting and the submit button shows the sending status. When it resolves the state is done. When it rejects the wizard goes back to editing, shows the submitError words in the error part and says them once.

submitLabel.description: The submit button on the last step: a verb plus a noun, Place order. Arabic default إرسال النموذج.

done.description: Shown in the panel after a successful submit.

doneTitle.description: The heading after a successful submit, also said by the status.

orientation.description: The Stepper layout, on the Stepper's data-orientation. Vertical puts the steps in a column at the start side; on a phone they stack above the panel.

size.description: The Stepper size, the action buttons and the title size.

stepsLabel.description: The name of the steps list: Checkout steps.

labels.description: Default words: next, back, submit, required, done, submitError, checking, sending, separator. English Go to next step, Go to previous step, Send form, Fill in this field, Form sent. Arabic الانتقال للخطوة التالية، الرجوع للخطوة السابقة، إرسال النموذج، هذا الحقل مطلوب، تم الإرسال. Demos pass a verb plus a noun per step instead.

defaultErrors.description: Errors by step index, then field name, shown before the user checks a step: errors a server sent back. A step's own check replaces its entry.

formProps.description: Props of the panel form: name, action, autoComplete.

a11y.role: The panel is a form named by the step title (aria-labelledby). The steps are a Stepper list. The status is a polite live region.
a11y.focus: Tab order: the steps the user may reach, then the fields of the current step, then back and next. On a step change focus moves to the step title (tabindex -1), which shows the focus ring. A failed check moves focus to the first field with an error, after the error is linked to it.

keys.Tab: Moves through the steps, the fields and the actions, in that order
keys.Enter: In a single line field: checks the step and moves to the next one, or sends the form on the last step. On a step: goes to that step

a11y.announce: On a step change the status says the position and the title once: Step 2 of 4, Address (WCAG 4.1.3). After a submit it says the done title. Field errors are read with their field through aria-describedby when focus lands there.
notes: Every step stays in the DOM; steps that are not current carry hidden. What the user typed is kept when they go back, and is never asked for twice (WCAG 3.3.7). autocomplete values on the fields are kept as given.

The panel is noValidate. The wizard checks one step at a time: an empty field marked required on its Field gets the required words, then the browser's constraint validation (type, pattern, min, max), then the step's validate function.
The next button is the form's submit button, so Enter in a field moves on. Back is type button.
One check or submit runs at a time: a second Enter while a check runs does nothing, and Back and the steps are inactive until it ends. A check that resolves after the user moved away is dropped.
Form (1.4.1) will render the panel later, as <Form data-part="panel">, and bring the error summary and the server error mapping. Until then the panel is a plain form and works with Field.
No native title attribute. Hints come from Tooltip.

en.title: Each step a short noun: Account, Address, Delivery, Review.
en.buttons: A verb plus a noun that names what happens: Save address, Review order, Place order, Edit account. Never Next, Back, Continue or OK on their own.
en.errors: Say what is wrong and how to fix it: Enter the five digit postal code.
en.review: The last step shows every answer with its label, so the user can check before sending.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics: الحساب، العنوان، التوصيل، المراجعة.
ar.buttons: Noun form labels: حفظ العنوان، مراجعة الطلب، إرسال الطلب، تعديل الحساب.
ar.errors: White Saudi dialect, direct: اكتب الرمز البريدي من خمسة أرقام.
ar.digits: Western digits in the status: الخطوة 2 من 4.

react.behavior: hand built on a native form; Stepper; state from packages/shared/src/stepper.ts
react.note: Motion fade-rise: the current step body fades in and rises by space.xs through @starting-style; under reduced motion it only fades, and every duration is 0ms.

angular.behavior: [dsFormWizard] on a div with a form panel in its template and the dsStepper, state from packages/shared/src/stepper.ts
angular.note: A step content is a TemplateRef with values and errors in its context. onSubmit is a function input, onStepChange the stepChange output, formProps a record of attributes for the panel form, formRef the formElement of exportAs dsFormWizard. FormWizard.css and Stepper.css are used as is.

native.behavior: react-native:View with a Stepper, one step mounted with its values held in state
native.note: On phones the Stepper is vertical or a compact Step 2 of 4 line; the keyboard avoids the actions.

styles.studio: Flat: the panel sits on the surface, a hairline above the actions, the next button the neutral fill.
styles.desk: The next and submit buttons are the yellow primary; the Stepper takes the yellow family.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: Buttons labeled Next and Back
mistakes.right: A verb plus a noun per step: Save address, Edit account

mistakes.wrong: Steps unmounted on next, so going back shows empty fields
mistakes.right: FormWizard, which keeps every step in the form and hides the ones that are not current

mistakes.wrong: A wizard for a form of four fields
mistakes.right: Form on one page

mistakes.wrong: Checking every field only at the end
mistakes.right: A validate function per step, so errors show where the user is

mistakes.wrong: Sending the form with no review step

name: Grid
summary: Lays out children in columns and rows: a fixed column count, or as many columns as fit at a minimum item size.
useWhen: Cards, files or tiles of the same kind that line up in columns and rows
A form or settings page with two or three columns on wide screens and one on phones
A twelve column page layout where some cells span more columns
avoidWhen: Items in one line or one column only
Tiles of deliberately mixed sizes on an overview or landing section
Tabular data a person compares across rows
A visual order that differs from the reading order

columns.description: A number from 1 to 12 gives equal tracks. auto-fit fits as many columns as minItemSize allows and grows them to fill the row. Fixed counts fall to one column under breakpoint.phone unless keepColumns is set. Sets data-columns.

minItemSize.description: The smallest item width with auto-fit: sm 10rem, md 15rem, lg 24rem, derived from the breakpoint tokens until a size.grid scale exists. Capped at 100% of the grid, so one item never overflows at 320px. Sets data-min.

gap.description: Space between cells on both axes, a space.* step.

rowGap.description: Space between rows when it differs from gap.

keepColumns.description: Keeps a fixed column count on phones. Sets data-keep-columns. Only for short cells, such as a calendar or a keypad.

as.description: The element to render. ul and ol get role list and lose their bullets; use GridItem as li inside.

GridItem.span.description: Columns the item spans; full spans the whole row. Sets data-span. On phones every item fills the one column.

GridItem.rowSpan.description: Rows the item spans. Sets data-row-span.

GridItem.as.description: The element of the item. li inside a list Grid.

children.description: The cells, plain elements or GridItem.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div, or list on ul and ol
a11y.focus: Never focusable. Focus and reading order are the DOM order: cells fill from the start side, the right in Arabic.
a11y.announce: Nothing. A Grid is layout only.
notes: This is a layout grid, not role grid. A grid of interactive cells with arrow key navigation is a different component (DataGrid).
No dense packing and no order property: the visual order must match the DOM order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
One column under breakpoint.phone and capped track minimums keep the page free of sideways scroll at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10).

en.items: No copy of its own. Cells carry their own labels.

ar.items: No copy of its own. Cells fill from the right in Arabic because the tracks follow dir.

react.note: No motion: a static layout has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies. The phone fallback is a viewport media query; a Grid in a narrow sidebar on a wide screen keeps its columns, so use auto-fit there.

angular.behavior: [dsGrid] and [dsGridItem] attribute directives
angular.note: The host element is the root and the item, so as is not needed.

native.note: No CSS grid in React Native: fixed columns map to a percentage basis per item and auto-fit to a basis from onLayout width.

styles.studio: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.desk: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.neutral: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.liquid: Layout only. The gap follows density.

mistakes.wrong: columns 4 with fixed pixel widths on each cell
mistakes.right: columns 4, or auto-fit with minItemSize, so tracks shrink and fall to one column on phones

mistakes.wrong: A GridItem span larger than an auto-fit grid has tracks
mistakes.right: span full, or a fixed column count, since auto-fit has fewer tracks on narrow screens

mistakes.wrong: keepColumns on a grid of cards with text
mistakes.right: Leave the phone fallback on; keepColumns is for short cells like a keypad

mistakes.wrong: role grid on a layout Grid
mistakes.right: No role; arrow key navigation between cells belongs to DataGrid

mistakes.wrong: keepColumns with a GridItem span larger than the column count
mistakes.right: Spans no larger than columns; on phones keepColumns keeps the count, so a wider span adds a track and scrolls sideways

name: HoverCard
summary: A read only preview card for a link or a person, shown on hover and on keyboard focus of the link. The link works on its own; the card only saves a click.
useWhen: A preview of a person behind a name link (avatar, role, a line of bio)
A preview of a page, a file or a board behind a link in running text
Extra context that sighted pointer users like to peek at, and that the link target also shows
avoidWhen: Content with actions or fields a person must use
The only place some information or a link is reachable
A one line hint for a control
Touch first screens, where nothing hovers

size.description: The width: sm 240 (tooltip.width.max), md 320 px (menu.width.min times 1.6).

openDelay.description: Open delay on hover in ms. Focus opens at once.

closeDelay.description: Close delay in ms after the pointer leaves the link and the card.

side.description: HoverCardContent: the preferred side. start and end follow the reading direction. It flips when there is no room.

align.description: HoverCardContent: alignment along the link, mirrored in right to left layouts.

hideWhenDetached.description: HoverCardContent: hides the card while its link is out of view or hidden.

HoverCardTrigger.description: One child element, a link that works on its own (always asChild). Hover and focus open the card.

a11y.role: No role: a visual preview next to the link. The trigger gets no aria-describedby; the card is not announced and takes no focus.
a11y.focus: Never takes focus. Keyboard focus on the link opens the card; focus stays on the link. Links inside the card are taken out of the tab order (tabindex -1).

keys.Escape: Hides the card; focus stays on the link

a11y.announce: Nothing: the card is a visual preview. Screen reader users follow the link to the full page.
notes: The card is never the only way to reach its content or its links: the link target shows the same and more.
WCAG 1.4.13: hoverable (the pointer can move onto the card), dismissable with Escape, persistent until the pointer leaves both or focus leaves the link.
The root carries data-side and data-align from Radix; data-side is physical after the logical side prop is mapped by direction.
The gallery demo sets openDelay 0 so the contract suite and screenshots open a card with one hover; products keep the 500 ms default.
A card short of room scrolls inside, and the keyboard cannot scroll it (the card takes no focus). That is acceptable only because the link target repeats the content; keep cards short.
Order 1.23 motion: the card unfolds out of its trigger side, more along the axis away from the trigger (--_hover-card-enter-stretch) than across it.

en.body: Short facts in sentence case: the name and handle, one line of bio, one line of meta. An empty field says so: No bio yet.

ar.body: Short facts, no diacritics, Western digits: سارة أحمد، 12 لوحة.

react.note: Shares the themed portal and side mapping of Popover (FloatingLayer.tsx).

angular.behavior: cdk:overlay

native.note: Nothing hovers on touch screens: the link opens the page directly.

styles.studio: The Popover surface: color.bg.surface, the default border, the panel radius and the menu shadow, with the arrow. Grows from 97% out of the link side.
styles.desk: Glass: the strong glass fill, the glass border, the window blur and the soft window shadow (recipe).
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned.

mistakes.wrong: A Follow button inside the hover card
mistakes.right: A Popover, or the button on the profile page

mistakes.wrong: A hover card on a span that does not take focus
mistakes.right: A link as the trigger, so focus opens it too

mistakes.wrong: Facts that appear only in the hover card
mistakes.right: The same facts on the page the link opens

name: Icon
summary: One system icon drawn from the icon set of the active style, sized by the size.icon tokens.
useWhen: A glyph next to a label in a control, a menu item or a status line
An icon only control, where the control carries the accessible name
A status glyph that a label beside it already explains
avoidWhen: An icon that is the only way to tell a meaning and has no label
A brand logo or an illustration
A glyph drawn from a file outside the system names

name.description: A system icon name. Directional names say forward and back.

size.description: 12, 16 and 24 px. The numbers are accepted too.

set.description: An icon set id, pixel or line. Overrides the set of the active style.

label.description: Gives the icon role img and this accessible name. Without it the icon is hidden.

a11y.role: img when label is set, otherwise hidden with aria-hidden
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
notes: Icons are decoration by default. The control around them carries the name.
Names in the mirror list flip in right to left layouts. Brand marks, clocks and media controls never flip.

react.note: Lives in @the-system/icons/react, re-exported by @the-system/react.

angular.behavior: svg[dsIcon], a directive
angular.note: Generated by packages/icons/build.ts into packages/icons/src/angular. The host svg is the root, glyph nodes come from the Renderer (no innerHTML), the style's icon set comes from dsTheme through the DS_ICON_STYLE signal. Used by dsButton and dsIconButton. No Angular demo yet, so the contract suite does not cover it on its own.

native.note: react-native-svg Icon is generated by packages/icons/build.ts and waits in generated-pending until React Native is installed.

styles.studio: Pixel set, crisp edges
styles.desk: Pixel set, crisp edges
styles.neutral: Line set
styles.liquid: Line set, round caps

mistakes.wrong: An icon named chevron-right that points the wrong way in Arabic
mistakes.right: chevron-forward, which flips in right to left layouts

mistakes.wrong: An icon only button with the label on the icon
mistakes.right: An IconButton with its own label and a hidden icon

name: IconButton
summary: A square action button with only an icon. Its label is the accessible name and the text of its Tooltip.
useWhen: A toolbar, a header or a row where the icon is well known: close, more, settings
A repeated action in a list where a text label would crowd the row
A close control in a dialog, a panel or a toast
avoidWhen: The icon alone does not say what happens
The main action of a form or a dialog
A choice that stays on or off

insteadUse.The main action of a view: Button with tone accent and emphasis solid

icon.description: A system icon name or a node. Hidden from assistive tech. 16px at every size, lg included, as in both sources.

label.description: The accessible name, set as aria-label. A verb plus a noun. Never the native title attribute. The Tooltip pairing that shows it on hover arrives with Tooltip in wave 1.

size.description: A square of size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px. Never under 24 by 24.

emphasis.description: ghost, because icon buttons sit in toolbars and headers. No link: an icon only link reads as neither.

shape.description: pill is a circle, square takes radius.sm, default takes radius.control (a circle in Desk).

loading.description: The spinner replaces the icon, a visually hidden status says loadingLabel, aria-busy is set, activation is blocked, focus stays.

loadingLabel.description: What the hidden status says while loading.

disabled.description: aria-disabled and data-disabled. Stays focusable so a Tooltip can say why.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element, for example an empty link, as the button.

a11y.role: button (native button element), or the role of the asChild element
a11y.focus: In the tab order in every state. A 2px ring on keyboard focus; solid fills get the doubled ring.

keys.Enter: Activates the button
keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: The label prop is the accessible name. While loading, a visually hidden status says loadingLabel and aria-busy is set.
notes: label is required by the type, so an icon button always has a name.
At least 24 by 24 CSS px at xs (WCAG 2.5.8). Use lg (44px) in touch layouts.
No native title attribute. The Tooltip pairing that shows the label on hover and focus arrives with Tooltip in wave 1.
Directional icons (chevron-back, arrow-forward) mirror in right to left layouts.
A disabled asChild link loses its href and keeps role link.

en.label: A verb plus a noun in sentence case: Close panel, Open settings. Not the icon name.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: إغلاق اللوحة، فتح الإعدادات.

react.note: Motion: press (scale.press, spring.press). On the web the press is still an instant color swap until the component plays the pattern; the spinner turn and the hover veil fade are component CSS.

angular.behavior: button[dsIconButton] and a[dsIconButton], host bindings
angular.note: Built on the same base directive as dsButton. label is required and becomes aria-label. Button.css and IconButton.css are used as is.

native.note: Built on the Button internals and Button.styles.ts. label becomes accessibilityLabel and is required. hitSlop reaches 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android at every size. Directional icons mirror from the theme dir. No asChild yet.

styles.studio: Ghost by default, the control radius, the overlay steps on hover and press.
styles.desk: A circle by default (Desk controls are pills). The solid accent icon button is yellow with a doubled focus ring, accent soft a yellow tint. No roll: there is no label.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned: capsule glass on toolbars.

mistakes.wrong: An icon button with no label, or the label in a title attribute
mistakes.right: label set; the hint in a Tooltip

mistakes.wrong: label="trash"
mistakes.right: label="Delete file"

mistakes.wrong: A 16px icon button in a dense row
mistakes.right: size xs, which keeps the 24px target

mistakes.wrong: A Button with only an icon child
mistakes.right: IconButton

name: InlineEdit
summary: A value shown as text that turns into an Input to edit in place, with save and cancel, such as a board name in its header.
useWhen: A short value the person renames now and then where it is shown: a board, a file, a layer, a column
A title in a header that should read as text, not as a form field
One value in a list of items, each renamed on its own
avoidWhen: A form with several fields saved together
Text longer than one line
A value the person must fill in to go on

label.description: Required. The name of what is edited: the editor's name, and part of the display's name.

value.description: The value, controlled. Pair it with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: The first value, uncontrolled.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new value when it is saved, and only when it changed.

defaultEditing.description: Opens in the editor, for a new item named right away. Focus moves only when editing starts later, never on the first render.

onEditingChange.description: Called with true when editing starts and false when it ends.

validate.description: Returns a message that says how to fix the value, or nothing. An invalid value is never saved, on Enter, on save or on leaving the editor.

placeholder.description: Shown in the display while the value is empty.

editLabel.description: The display's name after the value. Default Edit plus the label in lower case. Pass it in Arabic.

savedLabel.description: Said once by a polite status after a save.

size.description: Height from size.control, for the display and the editor. The save and cancel buttons are xs, and sm at lg.

disabled.description: The display cannot start editing; it keeps aria-disabled and stays focusable.

invalid.description: Marks the value invalid from outside. Pair it with error, so the state is never color alone.

error.description: A message from outside, such as a server check, that says how to fix the value. Shown under the display or the editor, linked to both by aria-describedby, and marks the value invalid.

inputRef.description: Goes to the native input while editing. ref goes to the root.

a11y.role: button for the display (a ghost Button), textbox for the editor, buttons for save and cancel, status for the saved message
a11y.focus: Viewing, the display is one tab stop. Editing starts with focus in the input and its text selected; the save and cancel buttons follow in the tab order where the browser puts buttons there. Enter, Escape, save and cancel return focus to the display. Leaving the editor with Tab or a click saves a changed valid value, closes an unchanged one, and leaves focus where it went.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the display; while editing, from the input to save and cancel
keys.Enter: On the display: starts editing. In the input: saves and returns focus to the display; an invalid value keeps the editor open with its message
keys.Escape: In the input: drops the change and returns focus to the display. It is handled before a Dialog or Popover around it sees the key, so they stay open

a11y.announce: The display is named by the value and the edit label: Spring launch, Edit board name. The input is named by label. After a save, a polite status says Saved once; a failed save says the message once, which also joins the input's aria-describedby.
notes: The display name starts with the visible text, so voice control works (WCAG 2.5.3).
The save and cancel buttons keep focus in the input on press, so a press never reads as leaving the editor.
The message is an icon plus text, never color alone, and says how to fix the value.
The edit icon at the end of the display shows on hover and focus; the name says edit at all times.
In controlled use, Saved is said when onValueChange is called. A parent that rejects the value should pass error with the reason.
The default edit label lower cases the label and is English. Pass editLabel in other languages and for names with acronyms.

en.label: A noun for what is edited, in sentence case: Board name.
en.placeholder: Add plus the noun: Add a board name.
en.error: Say how to fix it: Add a name of at least 1 letter.

ar.label: اسم اللوحة

react.behavior: hand built on Button, Input and IconButton
react.note: Motion: the edit icon fades in on hover and focus, and the Input focus glow fades in. The swap between viewing and editing is instant.

angular.behavior: div[dsInlineEdit] on dsButton, dsInput and dsIconButton, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: value is a model whose valueChange fires on save only (defaultValue is value); onEditingChange is the editingChange output; validate is a function input; error takes a string or a TemplateRef. Escape cancels in a window capture listener, so a dialog around it stays open.

styles.studio: The value as ghost button text with the Input's inset, so the text does not move when the editor opens.
styles.desk: The same, in Instrument Sans; the editor is the Desk pill.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: Saving on blur whatever was typed
mistakes.right: validate, so an invalid value keeps the editor open with its message

mistakes.wrong: A span with an onClick that turns into an input
mistakes.right: InlineEdit, whose display is a real button with a name that says edit

mistakes.wrong: Announcing Saved on every key or on every render
mistakes.right: One polite status after a save

mistakes.wrong: InlineEdit for a field the person must fill to submit a form
mistakes.right: A Field with an Input

name: Input
summary: A single line text input: a native input in a bordered box with optional start and end adornments.
useWhen: A short value typed on one line: a name, an email, a link, a number
A search box, with the search icon at the start
A value with a unit or a currency shown inside the box
avoidWhen: Text longer than one line
A choice from a known list
A date, a color or a file

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px at default density.

shape.description: default takes radius.control from the style, a pill in Studio and Desk. pill is always fully round.

invalid.description: Marks the value invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

disabled.description: Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: Still focusable, selectable and readable. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

required.description: Sets aria-required. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

start.description: An icon name, a short text such as $, or a node. Icon names and texts are aria-hidden.

end.description: An icon name, a short text such as px, or a node. Icon names and texts are aria-hidden.

rootProps.description: Props for the root box. className and style also go to the root; every other native prop and the ref go to the input.

variant.description: outlined: a border all round. filled: a tinted box. Stamped as data-variant only when passed, so a style or platform can follow it.

a11y.role: textbox, from the native input (spinbutton for type number, searchbox for type search)
a11y.focus: The input is the only tab stop. Clicking anywhere in the box that is not interactive focuses the input. Focus shows the glow and a 2px ring around the box.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the input, and on to the next control
keys.Home, End: Move the caret to the start or the end of the value
keys.ArrowUp, ArrowDown: Change the value for type number
keys.Escape: Clears the value for type search, as the browser does

a11y.announce: Name from the Field label. The Field description and error through aria-describedby. aria-invalid and aria-required from the Field.
notes: No native title attribute. Use Tooltip for a hint, or the Field description.
dir auto is not set: the value follows the page direction, so a field does not jump sides while someone types a Latin word into Arabic. Pass dir auto yourself for free text in a mixed language form.
Email, url, tel and number values always run left to right, and stay on the reading side of the form. Their placeholder runs in the page direction.
A long value scrolls inside the box. It is never cut with an ellipsis.
Read only looks different from disabled: a dashed border and a quiet fill, full contrast text, and it stays focusable.
Validate on blur or on submit, never on every key. On submit, move focus to the first invalid control.
Disabled uses native disabled and draws with opacity.disabled, like every control.
A value being checked shows the loader icon in the end slot for now. A Spinner arrives in wave 1 and replaces it.

en.label: Always a visible Field label, a noun in sentence case. aria-label only for a toolbar search box.
en.placeholder: An example value at most: For example, spring launch. Never the label, never an instruction the person needs after typing.
en.adornment: A unit or a currency the value is in: px, USD. Never words the label needs. No icon that only decorates, such as a paper plane on an email field.

ar.label: عنوان ظاهر دايم، بصيغة الاسم وبدون تشكيل
ar.placeholder: مثال على القيمة بس، مو بديل عن العنوان
ar.latin: البريد والروابط والأرقام تنكتب من اليسار لليمين حتى داخل العربي

react.note: Motion: fade. Only the focus glow fades (an opacity transition in Input.css).

angular.behavior: div[dsInput] around a native input, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host box is the root. React spreads native props on the inner input; Angular cannot forward attributes, so the native props are inputs with the React names (type, placeholder, value as a model, id, name, autoComplete, inputMode, aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby and more). defaultValue is value. start and end take an icon name, a short text or a TemplateRef. Works with ngModel, formControl and formControlName.

styles.studio: Bordered transparent pill, the control border, a soft inner glow and the 2px achromatic ring on focus
styles.desk: The same pill and glow, in Instrument Sans

mistakes.wrong: A placeholder as the only label
mistakes.right: A Field with a FieldLabel

mistakes.wrong: An input with a title attribute for the hint
mistakes.right: A FieldDescription, or a Tooltip

mistakes.wrong: A disabled input to show a value that cannot change
mistakes.right: readOnly, which stays readable and focusable

mistakes.wrong: dir auto on every input in an Arabic form
mistakes.right: No dir: email, url, tel and number run left to right through the CSS

mistakes.wrong: type date or checkbox on Input
mistakes.right: The DatePicker or Checkbox component

name: InputGroup
summary: An Input joined in one row with add on text and action buttons: a unit, a fixed prefix or suffix, or a Button that acts on the value.
useWhen: A value with a fixed prefix or suffix the person does not type: https://, .example.com
A value with a unit or a currency that reads better outside the box: px, SAR
A Button that acts on this one value, joined to it: Copy link, Send invite
avoidWhen: A short unit or currency inside the box with no border of its own
A search box with a clear button
A password with a show and hide button
Several related buttons with no text control

size.description: Passed to every child that does not set its own. The add on takes the group's size, so set size on the group, not on a child.
