shape.description: Passed to every child that does not set its own. Only the outer corners round; inner corners are square.

invalid.description: Marks the control invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

disabled.description: Disables the control and every action. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: Marks the control read only; add ons dash with it. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

children.description: One text control (Input, PasswordField or SearchField), with InputGroupAddon parts and Buttons or IconButtons around it, in reading order. Direct children only: the group stamps the parts on them. Any component child that is not an add on, a Button or an IconButton is taken as the control, and children inside a fragment are not stamped.

a11y.role: group, around the native text control and the buttons
a11y.focus: No focus of its own and no roving focus. The control and every action are tab stops. Joined children draw the focus ring inside their box, so the next part never covers it.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the control, then to each action, then out of the group
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus back through the actions and the control

a11y.announce: The control takes its name from the Field label. Add on text joins the control's aria-describedby, after the Field description and error: it is read as a description, never as part of the name. Each action is named by its own label.
notes: Add on text is visible text and stays readable with the browser zoomed to 200 percent; it never wraps.
The group passes size, shape, invalid and disabled to children that leave them unset. A child's own prop wins.
Actions keep aria-disabled while the group is disabled, so they stay focusable and a Tooltip can say why.
While disabled the root carries aria-disabled, so the dimmed add on text reads as part of an inactive control (WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive components).
A group whose parts make one Latin value, such as https:// and a host, takes dir ltr in an Arabic page, so the prefix stays before the value. The action then sits at the right end.
A long add on shrinks to half the row and its text is cut at the end, so the control keeps room to type at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10). The full text stays in the control's description; keep add ons short.

en.addon: A unit, a currency or a fixed part of the value: px, SAR, https://. Never words the label needs.
en.action: A verb plus a noun: Copy link, Send invite. An IconButton label follows the same rule.

ar.addon: وحدة أو عملة أو جزء ثابت من القيمة: ريال، px، https://
ar.action: فعل واسم: نسخ الرابط، إرسال الدعوة

react.note: No motion of its own: the children keep theirs (the Input focus fade, the Button press). Parts are stamped on direct children: the control through rootProps, actions as a data-part prop.

angular.behavior: div[dsInputGroup], role group, provides DsInputGroupContext through DI
angular.note: React clones its children to stamp the parts. Angular reads the group through DI: the control takes data-part control and the group's size, shape and state where it sets none, and the add on ids in aria-describedby; span[dsInputGroupAddon] is an add on; DsInputGroupAction stamps data-part action on a dsButton or dsIconButton in the group. It cannot fill the button's own inputs, so size, shape, emphasis outline and disabled are written on each action.

styles.studio: The add on is a quiet overlay box with the control border. Joined parts read as one pill with square inner corners.
styles.desk: The same joined pill in Instrument Sans.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: The add on text in the label: Price in SAR, with SAR again in the box
mistakes.right: Label Price, add on SAR

mistakes.wrong: aria-labelledby pointing at the add on, so the control is named https://
mistakes.right: The Field label names the control; the group links the add on as a description

mistakes.wrong: An InputGroup wrapped in a div inside another InputGroup
mistakes.right: Direct children only: the group stamps parts on its own children

mistakes.wrong: An InputGroup for a clear button in a search box
mistakes.right: SearchField

mistakes.wrong: A URL group in an Arabic page left in rtl, so the page shows the host before https://
mistakes.right: dir ltr on the InputGroup when its parts make one Latin value

mistakes.wrong: A Tooltip or another wrapper around an action, as a direct child
mistakes.right: Pass data-part action on the Button inside the wrapper, since the group reads the wrapper as the control

name: Kbd
summary: A key or a keyboard shortcut drawn as keycaps, with the key names spoken to screen readers.
useWhen: Telling people which key or shortcut runs an action: Ctrl+K opens search
The shortcut part of a menu item, a tooltip or a command palette row
A keyboard help sheet that lists shortcuts next to what they do
avoidWhen: Code, a file name or a command people type, which is not a key press
A label on a button people click
The only way to learn an action: a shortcut is an extra path, the action needs a visible control too

insteadUse.Code or a command people type: Code (wave 2), or a monospace text span
insteadUse.A hint that explains a control: Tooltip, with Kbd in its shortcut part

children.description: The key or the shortcut. A string is split into keycaps by splitShortcut: Mod+K, Ctrl+Shift+P, ⌘⇧P, Esc, Ctrl++ or ⌘+ for the plus key. Plus is the only separator. Mod is Command on a Mac and Control elsewhere; on a Mac the modifiers are drawn in Apple order (⌃⌥⇧⌘). A node draws one keycap as is; give it a label, or the node itself stays readable.

size.description: Keycap height: xs 16 (size.icon.md), sm 20, md 24 (size.icon.lg) px. Use xs or sm inside menus, tooltips and running text.

platform.description: The convention to draw. mac: symbols and no separators (⌘⇧P). other: names joined by plus (Ctrl+Shift+P). Default: mac under a Theme with platform ios, otherwise the user agent after hydration; the server draws other.

label.description: What screen readers say instead of the spoken key names (Control Shift P by default), for example names in another language.

decorative.description: Hides the whole root from assistive tech and drops the spoken copy. For a shortcut next to an action that already carries aria-keyshortcuts.

separator.description: Drawn between keycaps. Default plus on other and nothing on mac.

a11y.role: None: a kbd element. Each keycap is hidden; a visually hidden span (spoken) says the key names, so a screen reader hears Control Shift P, not C T R L plus.
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: The spoken key names, or label. Nothing when decorative.
notes: The root is dir ltr and isolated (unicode-bidi isolate), so a shortcut reads Ctrl then K inside an Arabic sentence and does not move the punctuation around it.
Menu items and buttons that have a shortcut set aria-keyshortcuts (ariaKeyShortcuts from the same helpers) and render Kbd decorative.
No hover, press or motion: a keycap is text, not a control.
Under forced colors the gradient and the depth shadow drop; each key keeps a CanvasText border.
The default spoken names are English and carry lang en, so an Arabic page reads them with an English voice. Pass label for names in another language.

en.keys: Key names as printed on keyboards: Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Esc, Enter, Tab, single letters in upper case.
en.sentence: Put the shortcut after the verb: Press Ctrl+K to open search.

ar.keys: Keys stay in Latin letters and read left to right: Ctrl+K, never translated or mirrored.
ar.sentence: اضغط Ctrl+K للبحث. The key names are spoken in English by default; pass label for another wording.

react.note: Parsing, the Mod mapping and spoken names live in @the-system/shared (shortcut.ts), so Angular and native read the same keys. Motion (kbd-press, order 1.22): a passive window key listener presses the keycap of a held key and springs it back on release; nothing under reduced motion.

angular.behavior: kbd[dsKbd], hand built on shortcut.ts

native.note: Touch first apps rarely show shortcuts; useful on iPad and Android with a hardware keyboard. Same shortcut.ts.

styles.studio: A dark sculpted keycap: gradient face, top highlight, bottom edge and a soft drop, from the kbd tokens.
styles.desk: The same keycap on the Desk tokens.
styles.neutral: Light keycap from the kbd tokens of the Neutral style once it lands; no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+P</kbd> as one cap, read as C T R L plus
mistakes.right: Kbd with the shortcut string: three keycaps and the spoken names

mistakes.wrong: Hard coding ⌘ for everyone
mistakes.right: Mod+K, which draws ⌘K on a Mac and Ctrl+K elsewhere

mistakes.wrong: A shortcut in an Arabic sentence that renders K+Ctrl
mistakes.right: Kbd, which keeps the keys left to right inside right to left text

mistakes.wrong: A menu item whose shortcut is read twice
mistakes.right: aria-keyshortcuts on the item and Kbd decorative

name: Label
summary: The visible name of one control: a native label that focuses or toggles the control on click, with an optional required mark or optional text.
useWhen: A control outside a Field that needs a visible name: a Switch, a Checkbox or a Slider in a settings row
A small inspector control with a short name above or beside it, at size sm
Inside Field, which renders it as its label part through FieldLabel or the label prop
avoidWhen: A text control with a hint or an error message, where Field wires every id for you
A heading for a group of controls
A name for something that is not a form control

size.description: md is font.size.s, the label of a Field. sm is font.size.xs, for a small inspector control.

htmlFor.description: The id of the control. Not needed when the label wraps the control, or inside a Field.

required.description: Shows an aria-hidden asterisk. Outside a Field the word in requiredText joins the accessible name. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

requiredText.description: The word read after the label outside a Field. Default required, or مطلوب when the language is Arabic.

optional.description: Text after the label for a value that may stay empty, for example Optional. Never shown together with required.

disabled.description: Draws the label as disabled. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

invalid.description: Marks the label of an invalid control, for recipes. Draws nothing in the base. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

a11y.role: none: a native label element, which names the control it points at
a11y.focus: Never focusable. A click on it focuses a text control, or toggles a checkbox or a switch.
a11y.announce: Read as the control's name. The required mark is aria-hidden: inside a Field the control says required through aria-required, outside a Field a visually hidden word says it.
notes: No keys of its own: the control it names has the keyboard map.
Required is never a lone asterisk: the asterisk is a glyph that does not rely on color, plus aria-required on the control or the hidden word in the name.
Disabled keeps the words readable, in color.text.muted. The control carries opacity.disabled.
Radix Label keeps a double click on the label from selecting its text.

en.label: A noun in sentence case that names the value: Email, Board name. No colon, no question.
en.optional: Optional, in sentence case. Mark the few optional fields, or the few required ones, never both in one form.
en.required: Mark required fields with * and say once, above the form, that fields marked * are required.

ar.label: اسم بدون تشكيل يوصف القيمة: البريد الإلكتروني، اسم اللوحة. بدون نقطتين وبدون سؤال
ar.required: سطر واحد فوق النموذج: الحقول اللي عليها * مطلوبة

react.note: No motion: nothing on a label moves or fades, so there is no pattern to name and nothing to reduce.

angular.behavior: label[dsLabel], host bindings
angular.note: The host label is the root. htmlFor is the htmlFor input or the native for attribute. label[dsFieldLabel] is the FieldLabel form: the field's label id, for and data-part label. The hidden required word uses the Radix VisuallyHidden inline style, so the DOM equals React's. optional takes a string or a TemplateRef.

native.behavior: react-native:Text with nativeID, named by accessibilityLabelledBy on the control
native.note: A press on the text focuses or toggles the control.

styles.studio: Semibold text in color.text.default, the mark and the optional text in color.text.muted
styles.desk: The same, in Instrument Sans
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: A red asterisk as the only sign of a required control
mistakes.right: required on Label or Field: an aria-hidden glyph plus the word or aria-required

mistakes.wrong: A Label with no htmlFor next to a control that has no id
mistakes.right: htmlFor pointing at the control's id, or the control inside a Field

mistakes.wrong: A Label used as a section heading
mistakes.right: A heading element, or Fieldset with its legend for a group of controls

mistakes.wrong: A placeholder instead of a Label
mistakes.right: A visible Label, and an example value in the placeholder at most

mistakes.wrong: required on a Label outside a Field and aria-required on its control
mistakes.right: One of the two: the hidden word already says required, so the state would be read twice

name: LanguageSwitch
summary: Moves the reader to the same page in another language. Two languages render as a link pair, more as a menu. Each language is named in its own language, never with a flag.
useWhen: A site or app that exists in English and Arabic, in the header or footer
A page translated into three or more languages, where a menu keeps the header short
A settings screen entry point to the reader's language, when changing it reloads the page
avoidWhen: Choosing the language of content inside a form, such as the language of a document being written
Choosing a country or a currency
A page that exists in one language only

languages.description: The languages the page exists in: { code, name, href }. name is written in that language (English, العربية, Français). href is the same page in that language, so the switch keeps the page. Two render a link pair, three or more a menu. Fewer than two render nothing.

current.description: The code of the language the page is in now. When it matches no language, nothing is marked.

size.description: Type size of the pair (the item Links take Link size sm at md and xs at sm, one step up for Arabic names) and the trigger Button size.

emphasis.description: How loud the menu trigger Button is. The pair is always links.

label.description: The accessible name of the nav landmark, also the end of the trigger name (English, Language). Under an Arabic Theme the default is اللغة.

onNavigate.description: Called when a language is chosen from the menu, for client side routing. Without it the browser goes to its href. The pair links navigate on their own.

a11y.role: navigation landmark; the pair is two links, the menu form a menu button with menuitemradio items
a11y.focus: Each link of the pair is a tab stop. In the menu form the trigger is one tab stop; the menu follows DropdownMenu, with focus back on the trigger when it closes.

keys.Tab: Moves through the pair, or to the menu trigger
keys.Enter: Follows a link, or opens the menu
keys.ArrowDown, ArrowUp: Inside the menu, as DropdownMenu; Enter or Space chooses a language

a11y.announce: Each name is read in its own language (lang on the link or item). The current language in the pair reads as current page; in the menu it reads as checked. The trigger reads English, Language, menu button: the visible name first.
notes: Never a flag: a flag names a country, not a language.

Each name carries lang and its own direction (dir rtl for Arabic, Urdu, Persian and the other right to left languages, from directionOf in @the-system/shared), so screen readers switch voice and the name shapes correctly inside a page of the other direction. Pair links also carry hreflang. Menu rows are menu items with lang but no href, so the menu form needs script; the pair works without it.

The current language in the pair is marked by weight, a missing underline, data-active and aria-current page (its link is this page), never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). When current matches no language, nothing is marked. Fewer than two languages render nothing.

Escape is not in the key map: the contract suite cannot open the menu as a LanguageSwitch root (the menu is a DropdownMenu root of its own), so it would read Escape as closing LanguageSwitch. Escape closes the menu as in DropdownMenu, whose own contract checks it, axe and target size of the open menu included.
React Native: a direction change (English to Arabic) needs an app restart through I18nManager, so the native form asks before it reloads.
open and closed are the data-state of the menu trigger (a Button carrying data-part trigger) and of the menu; the LanguageSwitch root has no state.

en.names: Each language in its own language and script: English, العربية, Français. Never translate the names into the page language, never use flags or two letter codes alone.
en.label: Language

ar.label: اللغة, noun form, no diacritics.

react.behavior: nav of system Links for two languages; system Button and radix:DropdownMenu radio items for more
react.note: No motion of its own: the menu plays DropdownMenu's menu-scale. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction language-roll: when the current language changes in place, the trigger name rolls (an aria-hidden copy of the old name rolls out); in the pair the names dip and pop. Reduced: the new name fades in.

angular.behavior: nav[dsLanguageSwitch] with a[dsLink] items and the DropdownMenu port for more

native.note: A direction change on React Native needs an app restart (I18nManager.forceRTL then a reload), so the switch confirms before it applies.

styles.studio: Muted text links with the active language bright, medium weight and no underline; the menu trigger a ghost Button with the language icon.
styles.desk: The same from the Desk tokens; the trigger takes the Desk pill.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: A flag for each language
mistakes.right: The name of each language in its own language

mistakes.wrong: Language names translated into the page language (Arabic, Anglais)
mistakes.right: English, العربية, Français whatever the page language

mistakes.wrong: A switch that goes back to the home page in the other language
mistakes.right: hrefs that keep the page and swap the locale

mistakes.wrong: Names with no lang attribute, read in the wrong voice
mistakes.right: LanguageSwitch, which sets lang and hreflang on each name

name: Lightbox
summary: A full screen viewer for images, one at a time, with previous, next, zoom, a counter and a caption. Opens from a thumbnail or a Button and returns focus to it.
useWhen: A set of photos or screenshots the person wants to see large, one after another
A thumbnail grid where each thumbnail opens the full image
Detail in an image that needs zoom
avoidWhen: A single decorative image that adds no detail when large
Images that must be compared side by side
Video or documents: the viewer shows images only
Images with text the person must act on, such as a form or a contract

parts.LightboxTrigger: trigger (outside the root). One child element, a system Button (always asChild), with index: the image it opens. Focus returns to the trigger that opened the viewer.

images.description: The images in order: { src, alt (required, what the image shows), caption, srcSet, sizes, width, height, key }. Development builds warn when an alt is empty.

index.description: The image on show, controlled, with onIndexChange.

onIndexChange.description: Called for the buttons, the keys, a swipe and a trigger.

loop.description: Next on the last image goes to the first, previous on the first to the last.

label.description: The accessible name of the dialog. Arabic default: عارض الصور.

formatCounter.description: The visible counter. Default 3 of 12 (Arabic 3 من 12, Western digits).

formatStatus.description: What the status says for each image. Default Image 3 of 12: and the alt text.

rootProps.description: Props for the root layer. className and style go to the root too.

a11y.role: dialog (the panel), modal: Radix hides the rest of the page and keeps focus inside. Named by the label.
a11y.focus: On open, focus goes to the next button when there is a next image, else to the close button. On close, focus returns to the trigger that opened the viewer.

keys.ArrowRight: Shows the next image in reading order (the previous one in Arabic). While zoomed, pans the image to the right.
keys.ArrowLeft: Shows the previous image in reading order (the next one in Arabic). While zoomed, pans the image to the left.
keys.ArrowUp, ArrowDown: While zoomed, pan the image up and down
keys.Home, End: Show the first and the last image
keys.+: Zooms in to twice the fitted width (one step). = does the same, for keyboards where + needs Shift.
keys.-: Zooms back out to the fitted size. _ does the same.
keys.Escape: Closes the viewer
keys.Tab: Moves between zoom, close, previous and next, and wraps inside the viewer
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves back and wraps from the first to the last

a11y.announce: Each image is announced once through a polite status: Image 3 of 12, then its alt text. The visible counter is hidden from assistive tech, so it is not read twice. A failed image is announced as an alert.
notes: Every image needs alt text that says what it shows, never the file name. A caption does not replace it.
A swipe on the image moves to the next or previous image in reading order. The previous and next buttons and the arrow keys are the key path (WCAG 2.5.7).
A double click on the image toggles the zoom; the zoom button and + and - are its key path.
While zoomed, the arrows pan the image and do not move to another image. Press - first, then an arrow, to move on. Escape closes the viewer at any zoom.
Previous and next have a solid surface fill, so the chevrons read on any image where the buttons sit over it (on phones, and over a zoomed image).
Previous and next stay focusable when there is no image that way (aria-disabled), so focus never drops.
The neighbours of the image on show load ahead.
Images sit on the solid page color of the scheme, never on glass, in every style.
No native title attribute.

en.alt: What the image shows, in a sentence fragment: Blue hills under a pale sky. Not the file name, not Image of.
en.caption: The place, the time or the source, in sentence case: Asir mountains at sunrise.
en.trigger: Verb plus noun: View photo, View 12 photos.

ar.alt: Noun phrase, no diacritics: جبال زرقاء تحت سماء فاتحة.
ar.caption: عبارة قصيرة بدون تشكيل: جبال عسير وقت الشروق.

react.note: Built on DialogBase (Dialog folder), with IconButton and Spinner parts.

angular.behavior: cdk:portal, cdk:a11y InteractivityChecker
angular.note: On the Angular Dialog layer.

native.note: A full screen modal with a pager; pinch to zoom with the zoom button as its button path.

styles.studio: No recipe: the base CSS applies. Full screen on the page color: black in dark, the light page gray in light. The counter sits at the inline start of the toolbar, zoom and close at its end, previous and next as 44px IconButtons on a solid surface fill at the middle of each side, the caption centered under the image. The viewer fades in from 98%.
styles.desk: No recipe: the base CSS applies on the Desk page color. No glass: images never sit on glass.
styles.neutral: Tokens only: the Neutral page color and controls apply with no recipe.
styles.liquid: Planned: the toolbar may float on glass; the image stays on a solid surface.

mistakes.wrong: alt text that repeats the file name or says Image
mistakes.right: Say what the image shows: Orange dunes under a warm sky

mistakes.wrong: Swipe as the only way to the next image
mistakes.right: Keep the previous and next buttons; the arrow keys move too

mistakes.wrong: A caption used in place of alt text
mistakes.right: Both: alt says what it shows, the caption says the place, time or source

mistakes.wrong: A Lightbox for one decorative image
mistakes.right: The image in the page, at a useful size

mistakes.wrong: A Lightbox on a glass surface in Desk or Liquid
mistakes.right: The solid page color; the style recipe may only float the toolbar

name: Link
summary: Navigation to another page, place or site, inside a sentence or on its own line. Always underlined.
useWhen: Navigation inside running text: a sentence that points to a guide, a policy or a setting
A link that stands on its own line under a card, a form or an empty state, with standalone
A link to another site, with external, so it opens a new tab and says so
A router link that must look like text, through asChild
avoidWhen: An action that changes data or starts a task on this page (save, send, delete)
The main call to action of a view that must read as a button
Navigation between sections of the app shell or between tabs of one view
Link text that only says Click here, Here or More

href.description: Where the link goes. Removed while disabled.

tone.description: neutral reads as color.text.link, accent as color.primary.on-surface (the yellow family in Desk).

size.description: Font size from font.size xs, s, m and l. No default: without size the link inherits the font size of the text around it, which is what a link in a sentence wants.

external.description: Opens a new tab (target _blank, rel noopener noreferrer unless passed) and renders the end part: the external icon, mirrored in RTL, and visually hidden words after a comma.

externalLabel.description: The hidden words of an external link. Under an Arabic Theme the default is يفتح في تبويب جديد.

standalone.description: A link on its own line: an inline flex box at least size.target-min (24px) tall. Sets data-standalone. Leave it off inside a sentence, where the inline target exception of WCAG 2.5.8 applies.

disabled.description: Removes the href, sets role link, aria-disabled and data-disabled, and keeps the link in the tab order so a Tooltip can say why. Click and middle click do nothing.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element, for example a router link, as the link. A disabled child loses its href.

children.description: The link text. It names the place, not the gesture.

a11y.role: link (native a with href; role link is set while disabled, when the href is gone)
a11y.focus: In the tab order, disabled included. A 2px ring from focus.shadow.ring on keyboard focus, drawn around every line of a link that wraps.

keys.Enter: Follows the link
keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: The label is the accessible name. An external link adds the hidden words after a comma: Open the docs, opens in a new tab.
notes: The underline is drawn at rest and on hover, so a link in running text is never told apart by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Hover makes it thicker.
Inline target exception (WCAG 2.5.8): a link inside a sentence keeps the line height of the text and may be under 24px tall. A link on its own line takes standalone and is at least 24px tall.
Space does not follow a link, only Enter, as in the browser.
The external icon is hidden from assistive tech; the hidden words carry the meaning.
Under forced colors the system link color applies, the underline takes the text color and the focus outline uses Highlight.
No native title attribute. Hints come from Tooltip.

Motion of round 3 (order 1.23, proposed, interaction link-underline): on a standalone link a stronger line draws over the rest underline with clip-path from the inline start (right to left in Arabic) on hover, keyboard focus and press, and is erased toward the inline end when the state ends; the external icon nudges toward where it leads; the text color eases to its hover color. Hover only where the device can hover; a tap shows the drawn line while held. A press makes the drawn line heavier from its foot and it springs back on release. Reduced motion: Link.css sets its own durations to 0s, so the line shows and goes at once.

en.label: Name the destination in sentence case: Read the pricing guide, the sharing guide. Never Click here, Here, More or Learn more on its own.
en.sentence: Put the link on the words that say where it goes, not on a whole sentence.
en.external: Do not write opens in a new tab in the visible text: external adds it for screen readers and the icon shows it.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: دليل المشاركة، سياسة الخصوصية. Never اضغط هنا.
ar.sentence: Link only the words that name the place, and keep Latin runs in Bidi.

react.note: No motion: color and underline swap at once on hover, so there is no pattern to name and nothing to reduce.

angular.behavior: a[dsLink], host bindings, a capture listener blocks click and auxclick while disabled
angular.note: The host anchor is the root. No asChild: a[dsLink] on a routerLink anchor is the router form. href, target, rel, role and tabIndex are inputs so disabled and external can rewrite them.

native.note: A pressable Text inside running text; Linking.openURL for external links.

styles.studio: Bright text (color.text.link) with a soft control colored underline that turns to the text color and thickens on hover. Accent reads the same as neutral in Studio, since its primary is the neutral fill.
styles.desk: Accent is the yellow family: color.primary.on-surface, yellow on dark and a dark gold on light, with a yellow underline. Neutral matches Studio.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: Link text Click here or Learn more
mistakes.right: Link text that names the place: Read the pricing guide

mistakes.wrong: A link told apart from the sentence by color only
mistakes.right: Link, which keeps the underline at rest

mistakes.wrong: A Link that saves, sends or deletes
mistakes.right: A Button; a link only navigates

mistakes.wrong: target _blank with no hint
mistakes.right: external, which adds the icon and the hidden words

mistakes.wrong: A standalone link row under 24px tall
mistakes.right: standalone on links that sit on their own line

name: List
summary: A vertical list of rows, each with a title and optional start, description, end and actions. Rows can be links.
useWhen: A short list of things people open: mail, files, boards, members
Rows that each carry one or two actions, such as delete or more
Ordered steps or a ranking, as an ol
avoidWhen: Picking one or more options from the rows
Many fields per row that people compare across rows
Term and value pairs about one thing
Site or app navigation with sections and nesting

size.description: md rows are at least list.row.height plus a small inset (about 36px in the default density), sm rows are list.row.height (28px default, 24 compact, 32 comfortable).

variant.description: plain: rows only. divided: a hairline between rows. inset: rows grouped on a rounded surface with hairlines. Sets data-variant on the root.

ordered.description: Renders an ol for rows whose order means something.

empty.description: Shown when there are no rows, in a p with part empty; the root is then a div. Say what is missing and what to do next. With aria-label the empty div takes role group.

ListItem.title.description: The row's main text, one line with an ellipsis. With href it is the link.

ListItem.description.description: A second line, up to two lines then an ellipsis.

ListItem.start.description: A system icon name (hidden from assistive tech) or a node such as an Avatar.

ListItem.end.description: Trailing content that is not an action: a time, a count, a Badge. Positioned above the row link, so a link or Badge in it stays clickable.

ListItem.actions.description: Buttons or IconButtons for the row. Their own Tab stops, drawn above the row link.

ListItem.href.description: Makes the row a link: the title becomes an anchor whose hit area covers the row.

ListItem.linkProps.description: Extra anchor props: target, rel, onClick for a client router, aria-current.

ListItem.active.description: The current row. Sets data-active, the active fill, and aria-current (true, or the value in linkProps) on the link. The description and end step up to the default text color on the active fill.

ListItem.disabled.description: Dims the start icon and the title. A link loses its href, keeps focus with role link and aria-disabled (anatomy rule 5), and linkProps.onClick does not run. The description and end stay at full contrast, so the reason the row is off stays readable. Actions are the caller's to disable.

a11y.role: list (ul or ol) with listitem rows. A linked row's title is a link. An empty list is a div with a paragraph, so it is not read as a list of one.
a11y.focus: Each linked row is one Tab stop on its title link; its actions follow. A disabled row link stays focusable with aria-disabled. Rows without a link and the list itself are not focusable. A 2px ring from color.focus.ring draws inside the whole row.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next row link or row action
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves to the previous row link or row action
keys.Enter: Follows the focused row link, or activates the focused action

a11y.announce: The link name is the title only; the description, end and actions are read as the row's other content. Name each action with the row it acts on: Delete mail from Sara.
notes: No arrow key navigation: this is a list of links and buttons, not a composite widget. For arrow keys and selection use ListBox.
The row link's hit area is its ::before stretched over the row, which is also the focus layer. Actions are positioned later in the DOM, so they sit above it without a z-index.
Give the list an aria-label when the page has no heading for it.
Under forced colors the focus ring is Highlight, the active row gets a CanvasText outline and separators are CanvasText.
data-linked marks a row with a link, for CSS only; it is structure, not a state.
An active row without a link carries aria-current on the li.
ordered renders an ol for assistive tech; numbers are not drawn. Put a number in start when people need to see it.

en.title: A name people scan for: the sender, the file, the board. Sentence case.
en.description: One line of context: the subject, the last change.
en.empty: What is missing and what happens next: No mail yet. Mail you get from your team shows here.
en.actions: Accessible names say the verb and the row: Delete mail from Sara Alqahtani.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics.
ar.empty: ما فيه رسائل للحين. الرسائل اللي توصلك من فريقك بتظهر هنا.
ar.digits: Western digits in end content such as times and counts.
ar.description: سطر واحد يوضح السياق، بدون تشكيل.
ar.actions: Accessible names say the action and the row in noun form: حذف رسالة سارة القحطاني.

react.note: Hover and active swap the row fill at once. list-stagger (rows entering) is named for the catalog; the component plays no motion yet and leaves entry to the page.

angular.behavior: ul[dsList] and li[dsListItem], hand built

native.note: FlatList rows with Pressable for linked rows; 44pt rows on iOS and 48dp on Android.

styles.studio: Flat rows, a 5 percent overlay on hover, a 10 percent overlay for the active row; inset groups on surface 2.
styles.desk: The same on the Desk tokens; inset groups read as a panel inside a window.
styles.neutral: The same on the Neutral tokens; no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: A row with onClick on the li
mistakes.right: href on ListItem, so the row is a real link that keyboards and new tabs work with

mistakes.wrong: A List with checkboxes for picking rows
mistakes.right: ListBox

mistakes.wrong: An action labelled Delete in every row
mistakes.right: Delete mail from Sara Alqahtani, so each name is unique

mistakes.wrong: An empty ul with nothing in it
mistakes.right: empty with what to do next

mistakes.wrong: A long sentence as the title, cut to one line with an ellipsis that a pointer user cannot read in full
mistakes.right: A short title of a few words, with the rest in description, which wraps to two lines

name: ListBox
summary: A visible list of options to choose one or many from, with groups, descriptions, icons, typeahead and the matched part of each label marked. The same list sits inside the popups of Combobox, Autocomplete, MultiSelect, TagField and CommandPalette.
useWhen: A short to medium list of options that stays visible on the page, such as a filter panel or a settings column
Choosing several options where seeing every choice at once helps, such as folders to sync
Building a new picker on the shared option list: put a ListBox with virtualFocus inside the popup and drive it from the owner
avoidWhen: Two to five options that fit as plain controls
A long list where people know what they want and can type it
Choosing a value in a compact form row where the list should stay closed
A list of actions or commands
Navigation between pages or sections

items.description: The options, plain ({ value, label, description?, start?, disabled?, keywords? }) or in titled groups ({ label, options, key? }). A separator is drawn between groups; a group with no option is dropped. Labels are plain text, so the match can be marked and typeahead can read them.

selectionMode.description: single: one value or none (value is a string or null). multiple: any number (value is an array in the order of choice); the root gets aria-multiselectable.

value.description: Controlled selection, with onValueChange: a string or null in single mode, a string array in multiple mode.

defaultValue.description: Uncontrolled starting selection, the same shape as value.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new selection after a click, Enter, Space or Ctrl+A.

allowEmpty.description: Single mode: choosing the chosen option again clears the value.

size.description: Row height and type size: sm rows are size.control.xs (24px), md rows follow list.row.height (24, 28 and 32px in the compact, default and comfortable densities).

orientation.description: vertical: one column, ArrowDown and ArrowUp. horizontal: a wrapping row, ArrowRight and ArrowLeft in reading order (swapped in right to left layouts).

highlightedValue.description: The keyboard cursor, controlled with onHighlightedValueChange. An owner that keeps focus sets it.

onHighlightedValueChange.description: Called when the arrows, typeahead or (with virtualFocus) the pointer move the highlight.

virtualFocus.description: true: focus stays on an owner, a combobox input that points aria-activedescendant at listBoxOptionId(listId, value). Options take no focus and the list handles no keys. false: the list is one tab stop (roving tabindex) and handles its own keys.

query.description: The text the owner filtered with (filterListBoxItems, built on filterItems from @the-system/shared). The matched part of each label is wrapped in mark, drawn heavier and underlined.

loop.description: ArrowDown on the last option goes to the first, and ArrowUp on the first to the last.

empty.description: Shown when there is no option. Say what to do next, not only that the list is empty.

disabled.description: No option can be chosen. The list stays focusable and readable with aria-disabled, drawn with opacity.disabled.

readOnly.description: The selection is shown and can be moved through, not changed. aria-readonly and data-readonly.

onOptionSelect.description: Runs with the option value after a click, Enter or Space chose it. Owners use it to close their popup.

aria-label.description: The list needs a name: aria-label, or aria-labelledby pointing at a visible label.

a11y.role: listbox, with option children and group children named by their group label. aria-multiselectable in multiple mode. Options carry aria-selected, and aria-disabled when they cannot be chosen. With no option, the root is a group named the same way that holds the empty text, since a listbox must own options.
a11y.focus: Alone: one tab stop, the highlighted option, else the first selected option, else the first enabled option (roving tabindex). With virtualFocus: options never take focus; the owner keeps it and points aria-activedescendant at the highlighted option.

keys.Tab: Moves into the list, to the selected option, and out of it again
keys.ArrowDown: Moves to the next enabled option. In a horizontal list this is ArrowRight, or ArrowLeft in right to left layouts
keys.ArrowUp: Moves to the previous enabled option
keys.Home: Moves to the first enabled option
keys.End: Moves to the last enabled option
keys.Enter: Selects the highlighted option; in multiple mode, toggles it
keys.Space: Selects the highlighted option; in multiple mode, toggles it
keys.Ctrl+A: Multiple mode: selects every enabled option, or clears them when all are selected
keys.Typeahead: Typing letters moves to the next option whose label starts with them, ignoring case, accents, Arabic diacritics and alef forms

a11y.announce: Each option reads its label, its description, its selected state and its position in the list (from the browser). A group is read with its title. No live region of its own: an owner that filters announces the result count.
notes: Selected state is shown by a check icon, never by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The check slot is kept on every row so labels line up.
The matched part of a label is wrapped in mark and drawn heavier and underlined, never by color alone.
Rows are at least 24px tall (size.target-min, WCAG 2.5.8).
Disabled options use aria-disabled, stay in the list and are skipped by the arrow keys.
Separators between groups are drawn only (aria-hidden): a listbox may hold only options and groups.
No virtualization in wave 1: filterItems handles 1000 options in under a frame (unit test); render fewer than a few hundred rows at once.
Contract keys: ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End are checked from the first option of the many case. Enter, Space, Ctrl+A and typeahead are covered by the unit tests.

en.options: Nouns or short noun phrases in sentence case: Date edited, Saudi Arabia. No ending punctuation.
en.description: One short line that tells options apart: Newest first. Not a repeat of the label.
en.group: A short noun over the group: Gulf, Recent.
en.empty: Say what to do next: No cities yet. Add one from Settings.
en.name: Name the list with what is chosen: City, Sort by.

ar.options: Noun form labels, white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: تاريخ التعديل، المالك.
ar.empty: What to do next: ما فيه مدن. أضف مدينة من الإعدادات.
ar.digits: Western digits in labels and counts.

react.behavior: hand built; shared logic in @the-system/shared filter.ts and listbox.ts
react.note: The popup that holds it plays menu-scale. Interaction row-glide (order 1.22, proposed): each option holds an unnamed aria-hidden span, the fill layer, and the lit row's fill travels from the last lit row; without the span the row draws its own fill. Sources GoBanana and Figma-Killer-2 were not reachable in the lane session; the rows follow the DropdownMenu surface built from them.

angular.behavior: div[dsListBox], hand built with the shared filter.ts and listbox.ts; the highlight kept with the CDK ActiveDescendantKeyManager, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root. Inputs take the React prop names; onValueChange is the valueChange output of [(value)], onHighlightedValueChange the highlightedValueChange output of [(highlightedValue)], onOptionSelect the optionSelect output. value is one input for both modes: a string or null (single), an array (multiple). empty takes text or a TemplateRef, an option's start an icon name or a TemplateRef. Keys, typeahead and the Arabic folding come from the shared helpers, not the CDK typeahead. Angular Aria Listbox would replace the key manager once @angular/aria is installed. ListBox.css is used as is.

native.behavior: hand built on FlatList with the shared listbox.ts

styles.studio: A bordered box with the card radius and rows of the menu radius inside, the menu weight. The lit row takes the overlay step, the hover a lighter veil. Separators on surface-2. In a popup the box drops its border and takes the menu surface.
styles.desk: The panel radius with field radius rows and the regular weight. The lit row is the yellow primary fill with dark text and the on-primary keyboard ring, as in the Desk menus. Hairline separators.
styles.neutral: Planned: tokens only.

mistakes.wrong: Showing the selected option only by a colored row
mistakes.right: The check in the indicator carries the state; the color is extra

mistakes.wrong: Filtering inside ListBox or passing every option with a hidden flag
mistakes.right: The owner keeps the query, passes filterListBoxItems(items, query) as items and the query to mark the match

mistakes.wrong: Moving focus into the list from a combobox input
mistakes.right: virtualFocus on the ListBox, aria-activedescendant on the input pointing at listBoxOptionId(listId, value)

mistakes.wrong: A ListBox with no name
mistakes.right: aria-label, or aria-labelledby pointing at the visible label

mistakes.wrong: Hiding an option that cannot be chosen now
mistakes.right: disabled on the option, with a description that says why

mistakes.wrong: A ListBox of actions (Delete, Duplicate)
mistakes.right: DropdownMenu, whose items are actions

name: Menubar
summary: The application menu row (File, Edit, View), Desk's menu bar. Menu titles that open DropdownMenu style menus, arrow keys across the row in reading order, and a status slot at the end.
useWhen: A desktop style app with many commands grouped under a few titles, such as a board editor or the Desk shell
Commands people look for by name and learn by their shortcuts
The top row of an app window, once, with a clock or a save state at the end
avoidWhen: Navigation between pages of a site
A few actions on one object
Phone layouts, where the row has no room and nothing is found by hover
More than one menu row on a screen

value.description: Menubar: the value of the open MenubarMenu, "" when none is open. Controlled, with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: Menubar: the menu open at first. Default none.

onValueChange.description: Menubar: called with the value of the menu that opens, or "" when it closes.

size.description: Menubar: the row height (size.control.sm or size.control.md), the trigger height and type size, and the size of every menu (rows of 24px, or menu.item.height).

loop.description: Menubar: ArrowRight on the last title goes to the first, and back.

aria-label.description: Menubar: names the menu bar (it goes on the bar part, role menubar), for example Application menu.

MenubarMenu.value.description: The value Menubar value and onValueChange use for this menu. Default a generated id.

MenubarTrigger.description: The menu title, role menuitem with aria-haspopup menu. A short noun. disabled keeps it in the row, skipped by the arrow keys.

side.description: MenubarContent: where the menu opens, in logical words. It flips when there is no room.

align.description: MenubarContent: how the menu lines up with its trigger. start is the trigger's inline start edge.

sideOffset.description: MenubarContent: the gap to the trigger in px.

collisionPadding.description: MenubarContent and MenubarSubContent: the space kept from the viewport edge in px. A long menu scrolls inside.

MenubarItem.tone.description: An item's tone. danger marks a destructive action; the label names what is destroyed.

start.description: Items and the sub trigger: leading content, a system icon name or a node. Decorative: the text names the item. Rows without it line their text up with rows that have it.

end.description: Items: trailing content, a system icon name or a node. MenubarEnd: the status slot at the inline end of the row (text, not controls).

shortcut.description: Items: a key hint shown at the inline end as plain text, left to right in every language (for example Ctrl+D). It does not bind the key; the app does.

disabled.description: Items: aria-disabled and data-disabled; they stay focusable in the menu, skipped by the arrow keys. MenubarTrigger: the native disabled of the Radix trigger, with data-disabled: dimmed and skipped by the arrow keys (an exception to anatomy rule 5, see a11y notes).

onSelect.description: Items: runs on click, Enter and Space, then the menu closes. Call event.preventDefault() to keep it open.

checked.description: MenubarCheckboxItem, with onCheckedChange. The check icon shows it, a minus for indeterminate.

MenubarRadioGroup.value.description: With onValueChange: the chosen MenubarRadioItem value.

textValue.description: Items: the text typeahead matches. Default: the label when it is plain text.

MenubarSub.description: A submenu: a MenubarSubTrigger, then a MenubarSubContent; open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange.

className.description: Menubar: goes to the root, as style does. Every other prop goes to the bar.

a11y.role: The root is a plain element. Its bar part is role menubar, named with aria-label. Each trigger is a menuitem with aria-haspopup menu and aria-expanded, and names its menu. The menus are role menu, not modal: the page stays in the accessibility tree. The end slot sits next to the bar, outside role menubar, so its text is read in the page.
a11y.focus: The row is one tab stop: Tab reaches the current title, the arrow keys move between titles. A menu opened with the keyboard puts focus on its first item; on close, focus returns to its title.

keys.Tab: Moves into the row, onto one title, and out again; the row is one tab stop
keys.ArrowRight: Moves to the next title in reading order; with a menu open, opens the next menu. In right to left layouts this is ArrowLeft. In a menu, on a sub trigger, opens the submenu
keys.ArrowLeft: Moves to the previous title in reading order; with a menu open, opens the previous menu. In right to left layouts this is ArrowRight
keys.ArrowDown: On a title, opens its menu with focus on the first item. In a menu, moves to the next item
keys.ArrowUp: In a menu, moves to the previous item
keys.Enter: On a title, opens its menu. On an item, selects it and closes the menu
keys.Home: Moves to the first title, or the first item in a menu
keys.End: Moves to the last title, or the last item in a menu
keys.Escape: Closes the open menu and returns focus to its title
keys.Typeahead: In a menu, typing letters moves to the item whose label starts with them. The titles have no typeahead

a11y.announce: The row is read as a menu bar with its name. Each title reads its label, that it has a popup and whether it is expanded. Items read as in DropdownMenu.
notes: The current menu is shown by two cues, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): its title takes the open fill and the open weight. The title reserves the width of its open weight, so the row never shifts.
Arrow keys follow the reading direction: Radix reads the direction from Theme.
The end slot holds status text (a clock, a save state), outside role menubar. Controls go in their own row or toolbar.

A disabled title uses the native disabled that Radix Menubar sets, so it leaves the arrow key order; the WAI-ARIA menubar pattern allows either. Items inside the menus keep aria-disabled and stay focusable.
At narrow widths the titles wrap onto a second line, and long titles and status text wrap, instead of scrolling sideways (WCAG 1.4.10).
Titles are at least 24px tall (size.target-min).
Each menu is a dropdown-menu root carrying the part name content, drawn by DropdownMenu.css; its items are DropdownMenu parts.

Contract keys: ArrowRight, ArrowLeft and ArrowDown are checked on a title of the variants case; Escape on an item of the menu that the open case shows at load. The other keys are covered by the unit tests.
No native title attribute.

The item parts inside a menu (item, checkbox-item, radio-item, label, group, separator, sub-trigger, sub-content) belong to the nested dropdown-menu root and are listed in the DropdownMenu manifest (anatomy.md: a manifest lists only its own parts).

en.trigger: A short noun in sentence case: File, Edit, View, Help. No verbs, no icons alone.
en.items: Verb plus noun: Save board, Close window. A shortcut in the shortcut prop.
en.end: Status, not a call to act: Thu 12 Nov 9:41, Saved.
en.count: Up to 10 titles; up to 12 entries in each menu.

ar.trigger: Noun forms, white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: الملف، التحرير، العرض، المساعدة.
ar.items: Noun form labels: حفظ اللوحة، إغلاق النافذة.

react.note: The menus are portaled into a Theme layer marked data-menu-layer menubar, which DropdownMenu.css reads for the Radix menubar measures.

angular.behavior: cdk:menu (cdkMenuBar)

native.note: No application menu row on phones; use a header with a DropdownMenu.

styles.studio: A flat row in color.material.menubar with a hairline under it. Titles in the menu weight; the open title takes the overlay 20 fill and the bold weight.
styles.desk: The macOS style glass row: color.material.menubar with the window blur, regular weight titles that open at semibold, the field radius. Solid under reduced transparency and more contrast.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned: the glass row, with the menus never on top of other glass.

mistakes.wrong: A Menubar as the navigation of a website
mistakes.right: NavigationMenu or links in a header

mistakes.wrong: The open menu shown only by a color change on its title
mistakes.right: The open fill and the open weight, as Menubar draws it

mistakes.wrong: Buttons or a search field inside the row
mistakes.right: Status text in MenubarEnd; controls in a Toolbar next to the row

mistakes.wrong: Verbs as titles: Edit things, View options
mistakes.right: Short nouns: Edit, View

mistakes.wrong: A command that lives only in the menu bar
mistakes.right: Also a shortcut, a toolbar button or the CommandPalette

name: Meter
summary: A measured value in a known range, such as storage used or a score, with its level in words.
useWhen: A value that sits in a fixed range and is not a task: storage used, a quota, a score, a signal strength
A value whose regions matter (plenty of room, filling up, almost full), set with low, high and optimum
A list of measures to compare, one small meter per row
avoidWhen: A task that moves toward done
A value with no known maximum
A rating the person sets

value.description: The measured value. Clamped into [min, max].

max.description: The top of the range. A max at or below min falls back to min plus 100.

low.description: The top of the low region, as in the HTML meter element. Default: no low region.

high.description: The bottom of the high region. Default: no high region.

optimum.description: The best value. Its region gives tone success, the next region warning, the far region danger. Without it, or without low and high, the tone is accent.

label.description: Visible text that names the measure and labels the meter through aria-labelledby. Without it, pass aria-label.

valueText.description: (value, min, max) => string for the visible value and aria-valuetext: 72 GB of 100 GB. Default: a whole percent of the range, rounded down, Western digits.

levelLabels.description: Words per level, { low, medium, high }, each optional, said after the value: Almost full. Default Low, Medium, High; Arabic منخفض، متوسط، مرتفع under lang ar.

showLevel.description: Shows the level word after the value. Default true when low or high is set. aria-valuetext keeps the level word whenever low or high is set.

tone.description: Overrides the tone the thresholds give. Prefer thresholds, so tone and level agree.

size.description: Track thickness 4, 8 and 12 px; the text steps from font.size.xs to m.

a11y.role: meter, with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: Not a live region. A screen reader reads the label and aria-valuetext, which holds the value and the level word: 72 GB of 100 GB, Filling up.
notes: data-level on the root is low, medium or high: a valued state, listed in states as data-level=low|medium|high so the contract suite checks its values.
The level is in data-level, in the visible value text and in aria-valuetext, never only in the color.
Thresholds follow the HTML meter: low and high are clamped into the range, and high is never below low.
The indicator scales from the inline start: it fills from the right in Arabic.
Under forced colors the track has a CanvasText border and the indicator is Highlight.
With no optimum the tone is accent: no region is better than another. The HTML meter would assume the midpoint; this is a deliberate choice for Angular to copy.

en.label: Name the measure as a noun: Storage used, Accessibility score.
en.value: Say the amount in its own unit when it means more than a percent: 72 GB of 100 GB.
en.level: Say what the level means for the person: Plenty of room, Filling up, Almost full.
en.language: Pass valueText and levelLabels in the same language: the default level words follow the theme lang, the caller's value text does not.

ar.label: Noun form labels, no diacritics: المساحة المستخدمة.
ar.level: Short noun phrases: المساحة كافية، المساحة تقل، المساحة قربت تخلص.

react.note: Level and tone logic in packages/shared/src/meter.ts (pure, shared with Angular). Values formatted by the ProgressBar format.ts helper until packages/shared/src/number.ts lands. Motion: no catalog pattern. A value change eases the scaleX transform over duration.slow in Meter.css until the catalog has a fill pattern (a request to the motion owner).

angular.behavior: div[dsMeter], hand built, role meter, level and tone from @the-system/shared meter.ts
angular.note: The host element is the root. Inputs take the React prop names; React spreads a range object, Angular takes min, max, low, high and optimum as inputs. label takes a string or a TemplateRef. Meter.css is used as is.

styles.studio: The ProgressBar track; with no thresholds the fill is the strongest text color.
styles.desk: The same track; with no thresholds the fill is yellow on dark and dark gold on light.
styles.neutral: Planned: the brand color with no thresholds.
styles.liquid: Planned: a solid track on content.

mistakes.wrong: A Meter for an upload
mistakes.right: A ProgressBar: an upload is a task

mistakes.wrong: Only the red color when storage is almost full
mistakes.right: high and optimum thresholds and a level word such as Almost full

mistakes.wrong: tone set by hand that disagrees with the level
mistakes.right: low, high and optimum, and let the meter pick the tone

mistakes.wrong: showLevel false, or a hand set tone, with no level in visible text
mistakes.right: Keep the level word visible, or say the level in text next to the meter

name: MultiSelect
summary: A closed trigger that opens a list with checks and keeps any number of values from it. The trigger shows the chosen values as tags, or as a count.
useWhen: Several values from a known list, such as labels, cities or team members, in a form row with little room
Filters with more options than fit as a CheckboxGroup on the page
A list long enough to need a search field (more than 8 options turns it on)
avoidWhen: Only one value is allowed
Two to six options that fit on the page as checkboxes
People type new values that are not in any list
The chosen values must stay visible and editable one by one on the page

items.description: An array of options, plain ({ value, label, description?, start?, disabled?, keywords? }) or in titled groups ({ label, options }), as ListBox takes them (type node here means structured data). The search filters by the label, then the keywords.

value.description: The chosen values (string[]) in the order they were chosen, controlled with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: Uncontrolled starting values (string[]).

onValueChange.description: Called with the new string[] on every toggle, Select all, Clear selection and Ctrl+A.

open.description: The popup is open, controlled with onOpenChange.

summary.description: tags: the chosen labels as tags, up to maxTags, then +N. count: 3 selected.

maxTags.description: In tags mode, the most tags drawn before the +N tag.

formatCount.description: The count words. Default 3 selected; Arabic pluralized with Intl.PluralRules (عنصر واحد محدد، عنصرين محددين، 3 عناصر محددة، 11 عنصر محدد).

placeholder.description: Shown when nothing is chosen. Arabic default: اختيار من القائمة.

searchable.description: Shows the search field in the popup. Default: on when there are more than 8 options.

searchLabel.description: The name and placeholder of the search field. Arabic default: البحث في الخيارات.

actions.description: Shows Select all and Clear selection under the list.

selectAllLabel.description: Arabic default: تحديد الكل. Selects the shown enabled options (after a search, only the matches).

clearLabel.description: Arabic default: مسح التحديد. Disabled options keep their state.

size.description: Box height from size.control (28, 32, 44px at default density). sm lists use sm rows; md and lg use list.row.height.

shape.description: default: the style's control radius (a pill in Studio and Desk). pill: always fully round.

invalid.description: The danger border and aria-invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field's error.

disabled.description: aria-disabled and out of the tab order; the popup never opens. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: The values show and the trigger stays focusable with aria-readonly; the popup does not open. A dashed border, no chevron.

required.description: aria-required. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

loading.description: Options are on their way: the icon is a spinner, aria-busy and data-loading are set, the popup says loadingLabel.

empty.description: Shown in the popup when there is no option (default No options to choose from yet.) or no match for the search (default No results. Try another word.).

name.description: Submits each value under this name in a form, one hidden input per value.

a11y.role: combobox on the trigger part (the APG select-only combobox: a focusable element that is not a text box), aria-haspopup listbox, aria-expanded, aria-controls, named by the Field label. The popup has no role of its own and holds a SearchField, a ListBox with aria-multiselectable named like the trigger, and two Buttons. Not modal: the page stays in the accessibility tree.
a11y.focus: The trigger is one tab stop. Opening moves focus to the search field when there is one, else to the list (the first chosen option, else the first option). Escape or Enter in the list returns focus to the trigger; a press outside the popup closes it and leaves focus where it lands. A press on the Field label focuses the trigger.

keys.Enter: On the trigger, opens the popup. In the list, closes the popup and returns focus to the trigger
keys.Space: On the trigger, opens the popup. In the list, toggles the option
keys.ArrowDown: On the trigger, opens the popup. In the search field, moves into the list. In the list, moves to the next option, skipping disabled ones
keys.ArrowUp: On the trigger, opens the popup. In the list, moves to the previous option
keys.Home: In the list, moves to the first option
keys.End: In the list, moves to the last option
keys.Ctrl+A: In the list, selects every shown enabled option (Cmd+A on a Mac); when all are already chosen, it clears them
keys.Typeahead: In the list, typing letters moves to the next option whose label starts with them
keys.Tab: Moves between the search field, the list and the actions; focus stays inside the open popup and wraps from the last stop to the first
keys.Escape: Closes the popup without changing the values and returns focus to the trigger. In the search field, the first Escape clears the query and the second closes

a11y.announce: The trigger reads its Field label, the chosen labels as a list (Design and Copy; in Arabic تصميم ومحتوى) or the count, and that it opens a list. In the list each option reads its label, selected or not, and unavailable.
notes: The tags in the trigger are drawn only (aria-hidden) and hold no button: a remove button inside a combobox would be a control inside a control. The full list of labels is read from a visually hidden summary-text, written with Intl.ListFormat. Values are removed in the list or with Clear selection.
slots.tag.max is the default maxTags (3): more values show as one +N tag, and the full list is read from summary-text.
Checked state is the ListBox check icon, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The +N tag never hides a value from a screen reader.
The search field and the actions sit outside the Field context, so they never take the Field's id, label or error.
Every target is at least size.target-min: the trigger fills the box, list rows, the sm search field and the sm Buttons (WCAG 2.5.8).

Contract: the variants case marks one trigger with data-demo-trigger. Enter, Space and ArrowDown on the trigger are checked as state changes (aria-expanded). The box stamps no data-state; data-state open and closed is on the popup root.
required is announced (aria-required) only; it does not block a native form submit. Hidden inputs are written only for values that match an option.

Arabic count words are in white Saudi dialect, like the Combobox count (نتيجتين): عنصرين محددين for two, 11 عنصر محدد for 11 to 99. A product in Gulf modern standard Arabic passes formatCount (عنصران محددان، 11 عنصرا محددا).

en.label: A plural noun in a Field label: Labels, Cities, Assignees.
en.summary: 3 selected. With tags, the labels themselves.
en.empty: Say what to do next: No labels yet. Add one from Settings.
en.error: Say what to do: Choose at least one city.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: التصنيفات، المدن.
ar.summary: Pluralized with Intl.PluralRules, Western digits: 3 عناصر محددة.
ar.empty: ما فيه تصنيفات. أضف تصنيف من الإعدادات.

react.behavior: radix:Popover (Root, Anchor, Content); the trigger hand built (APG select-only combobox), the list on ListBox multiple, the search on SearchField
react.note: No source for this order: designed from the dials table, Select (the trigger box) and ListBox (the rows). The popup surface is styled in MultiSelect.css with the same values as the list family popup in Combobox.css.

angular.behavior: div[dsMultiSelect], hand built: a CDK ComponentPortal popup placed with the Radix Popper steps (internal/popper.ts), a multiple ListBox (CDK ActiveDescendantKeyManager kept in step), the shared filter.ts and listbox.ts, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root. Inputs take the React prop names; onValueChange and onOpenChange are the valueChange and openChange outputs of [(value)] and [(open)]. formatCount is a function input, empty takes text or a TemplateRef. React spreads rest props on the trigger: static data-* attributes on the host move to the trigger, and id, aria-label, aria-labelledby and aria-describedby are inputs. The SearchField and Spinner DOM is inline until their Angular ports exist. Angular Aria Multiselect would replace the hand built keys once @angular/aria is installed. MultiSelect.css is used as is.

native.behavior: hand built: a sheet with a FlatList of checks

styles.studio: The box is the Input box: a transparent pill with the control border, the glow and the ring on focus or while open. Tags are small overlay-10 pills. The popup is the Studio menu surface: surface-3, the card radius, the menu shadow; the lit row takes the overlay step.
styles.desk: The same box. The popup is the Desk menu glass: the strong material and blur, a hairline, the panel radius; the lit row is the yellow primary fill with dark text (the Desk ListBox recipe). Under reduced transparency and more contrast the glass turns solid.
styles.neutral: Tokens only: the Neutral control radius and border, the Neutral menu surface.

mistakes.wrong: A remove button on each tag inside the trigger
mistakes.right: Tags drawn only; remove in the list or with Clear selection (built in)

mistakes.wrong: Ten tags that wrap the trigger onto three lines
mistakes.right: maxTags with a +N tag, or summary count

mistakes.wrong: A MultiSelect for two options
mistakes.right: Two checkboxes, or a CheckboxGroup

mistakes.wrong: Typing new values into a MultiSelect
mistakes.right: TagField, which adds free tags

mistakes.wrong: Enter in the list toggles the option
mistakes.right: Space toggles, Enter closes (built in)

mistakes.wrong: A count summary written as 3 items in Arabic with one plural form
mistakes.right: Intl.PluralRules with every Arabic form (built in)

name: Navbar
summary: The top bar of a site or app: a brand, primary links and menus with panels, actions at the end, and a menu button with a list on phones.
useWhen: The main navigation of a marketing site, docs site or small app, across the top of every page
Up to about seven top level destinations, some of which open a panel of related links
A brand, a few links and one or two actions (Sign in, Start a trial) in one bar
A layout that must collapse to a menu button on phones
avoidWhen: An app with many destinations in named groups, kept in view at the side
A desktop app menu of commands (File, Edit, View)
Switching between views of one page
A bar of tools for one context, such as a text editor
Commands that run actions from a menu

label.description: The accessible name of the nav landmark: Main. Not drawn.

size.description: Link and trigger height from size.control: md 32px, lg 44px; the bar adds space.s above and below.

brand.description: The logo link to the home page, at the inline start. Use Link with standalone (or an IconButton with asChild) so it is a 24px target.

items.description: A link is { label, href, active?, start?, description? }. A menu is { label, links }: a trigger in the bar that opens a panel of links. The same data draws the phone list. With no items the menu button is not drawn.

end.description: Actions at the inline end. On phones they move into the footer of the phone Drawer; with no items they stay in the bar and wrap. Keep them to one or two.

sticky.description: Sticks the bar to the top (z.topbar) and sets scroll-padding-block-start on the page to one row of the bar plus its border, at the density of :root (WCAG 2.4.11). A bar that wraps to two rows, or a denser nested Theme, covers more. Under breakpoint.tablet the open phone list scrolls inside the bar, never past the screen. Sets data-sticky.

linkAs.description: The component every link renders as, for a router. It receives href, children and the link attributes.

menuLabels.description: The menu button's one stable name (aria-expanded carries the state) and the phone list's landmark name. Under an Arabic Theme: القائمة، قائمة الموقع.

defaultOpenMenu.description: The label of a menu whose panel is open at first render. Default none.

a11y.role: navigation (Radix NavigationMenu nav with aria-label); the list is a list of links and buttons; on phones the menu button opens a modal Drawer titled Site menu that holds a Sidebar nav named Site menu
a11y.focus: Links and triggers are tab stops. Focus moves into an open panel with ArrowDown or Tab. The menu button sits in the tab order on phones only. The phone Drawer is modal: focus moves into it, stays inside, and returns to the menu button on Escape or the close control. Following a link in the phone list closes it. When the window grows past breakpoint.tablet while the Drawer is open, it closes and focus moves to the first item of the bar.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next link, trigger or action
keys.Enter: Follows a link, or opens and closes a trigger's panel
keys.Space: Opens and closes a trigger's panel, and opens the phone Drawer from the menu button
keys.ArrowDown: From an open trigger, moves into its panel
keys.ArrowRight, ArrowLeft: Move between links and triggers in the bar, in the reading direction (flipped in RTL)
keys.Home, End: Move to the first or last item in the bar
keys.Escape: Closes the open panel and returns focus to its trigger, or closes the phone Drawer and returns focus to the menu button

a11y.announce: The current link says current page. A trigger is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls from Radix. The menu button keeps one name, Menu, with aria-haspopup dialog, aria-expanded and aria-controls from the Drawer trigger. The Drawer is a dialog named by its title, Site menu.
notes: The current page is shown by aria-current page, a bold weight and a bar under the link, never by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). A trigger whose panel holds the current page takes the bold weight.

Under breakpoint.tablet (48rem) the bar hides the list and the end actions and shows the menu button. The end actions move into the Drawer's footer, so no label is cut short at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10). With no items there is no menu button: the end actions stay in the bar at full width and wrap to a row of their own when needed.

The phone list is a Drawer (side start, size sm) with the mobile part on its root. Its body is a Sidebar built from items: plain links in one unnamed group, each menu as a named group. The Drawer covers the bar, so the menu button never moves under the finger.
The chevron of a trigger is the trigger Button's own end part (anatomy.md: a part belongs to the nearest root); the Navbar only turns it over while the panel is open.
No native title attribute.

contract.skipAxeRules aria-hidden-focus: while a panel is open, Radix NavigationMenu renders a visually hidden, aria-hidden focus proxy span (tabindex 0) beside the trigger. It catches Tab and forwards focus into the panel in the viewport, so it is never a stop a user rests on. Axe flags it by shape. Only the open panel in the long-arabic case shows it.
data-orientation horizontal comes from Radix on the root and the list.

en.link: Nouns in sentence case: Pricing, Docs, Customers. One or two words.
en.description: One short line that says what is there: Plan work on one shared canvas.
en.end: Verb plus noun on buttons: Sign in, Start a trial.

ar.link: Noun form, no diacritics: الأسعار، المستندات، العملاء.
ar.description: One short line in white Saudi dialect: كل التعليقات في مكان واحد.
ar.end: Noun form on buttons: تسجيل الدخول، تجربة مجانية.

react.behavior: radix:NavigationMenu; the phone list is a Drawer holding a Sidebar
react.note: menu-scale: the viewport scales from 0.97 and fades in, the reverse on close, faster; the indicator slides under the open trigger. Reduced motion: none, and Radix removes the closed viewport at once. The phone Drawer plays Drawer's own slide from the inline start. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed): nav-current-slide, the current link's bar (::before) slides from the old current link on the snappy spring, stretched along its travel; nav-hover-follow, the hover veil (::after) slides from the link the pointer left. Both from internal/indicator.ts, WAAPI on the pseudo elements.

angular.behavior: nav[dsNavbar], cdk:menu for the panels, the Drawer for the phone list

native.note: Apps on phones use a stack header and TabBar; a web top bar has no native form.

styles.studio: A flat bar on the surface with a hairline under it; panels on surface-3 with the menu shadow. The current link has a white bar under it.
styles.desk: The same structure; the bar under the current link and the indicator take the yellow primary. A menu bar recipe in the GoBanana style is a later addition (desk/recipes/Navbar.css).
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: The current page shown only by a different color
mistakes.right: active on the link, which adds aria-current, weight and a bar

mistakes.wrong: A trigger that is also a link to a page
mistakes.right: A trigger opens a panel; put the overview page as the first link in the panel

mistakes.wrong: Five buttons in end
mistakes.right: One or two actions; the rest go in the links or an account DropdownMenu

mistakes.wrong: A sticky bar with no scroll padding, so focused headings hide under it
mistakes.right: sticky, which reserves the bar height as scroll padding

mistakes.wrong: File, Edit and View commands in a Navbar
mistakes.right: Menubar

name: NotificationCenter
summary: The panel of notifications: a list grouped by day or by the consumer's groups, unread marks, mark all read, actions per item and an empty state. Placed by the consumer in a Popover or a Sheet.
useWhen: A place where a person reviews what happened while they were away: mentions, invites, finished exports
Notifications that stay until read, with an unread count on a bell button
Notifications that carry their own actions, such as accepting an invite
avoidWhen: Telling the person about something that just happened while they watch
A full activity history with search and filters
A single message about the page

items.description: NotificationItem[]: { id, title, body?, time (Date, timestamp or ISO), unread?, tone?, icon?, actions? (up to two { label, onAction }), group? }. Rendered in the given order; the consumer sorts, newest first.

title.description: The panel heading. Arabic default under lang ar, from the prop or else the Theme language.

headingLevel.description: The title's heading level; group labels take the next level.

onMarkAllRead.description: Renders the mark all read Button (data-part mark-all) while any item is unread, and is called by it. The consumer clears unread on its items. Before the call, focus moves to the panel title (tabIndex -1), since the Button removes itself once nothing is unread.

markAllLabel.description: A verb plus a noun. Arabic: تحديد الكل كمقروء.

size.description: sm for a narrow popover: tighter padding and font.size.s.

now.description: The clock for relative times and day groups. Default the time of render. The consumer re-renders to refresh the times.

a11y.role: A section named by its title. Each group is a group named by its heading (a heading level below the title) holding a list; each item is an article in a list item, named by its title, with a time element. Not role feed.
a11y.focus: Every item is a tab stop with a focus ring, so a keyboard user can reach and read each one; its actions follow it. No roving focus, no arrow keys.

keys.Tab: Moves to mark all read, then each item and its actions in order
keys.Enter: Runs the focused action

a11y.announce: The panel never announces. A new notification is announced once by the consumer through toast(); the panel only lists it. The count is plain text.
notes: Unread is never color alone: a dot, a bold title and a visually hidden word (Unread) before the title.
Times use Intl.RelativeTimeFormat with numeric auto; Arabic uses Western digits (nu-latn). The time element carries the ISO time.
Group headings come from the day of each time (Today, Yesterday, Earlier) unless items name a group.

en.item: Who did what to which thing: Sara mentioned you in Launch plan. Sentence case.
en.actions: A verb plus a noun: Accept invite, Open comment. Two at most.
en.empty: Say what shows up here: Mentions, invites and comments on your boards show up here.

ar.item: No diacritics; names as written: سارة أشارت لك في خطة الإطلاق.
ar.actions: Noun form labels: قبول الدعوة، فتح التعليق.
ar.digits: Western digits in times and counts.

react.note: Motion: no catalog pattern. The panel renders a static list and no stagger plays when items are inserted; only the item hover veil fades (NotificationCenter.css). list-stagger is the pattern to wire when inserted items animate.

angular.behavior: section[dsNotificationCenter], host bindings, cdk:a11y _IdGenerator
