size.description: Track 2, 4 and 6 px thick, thumb 12, 16 and 24 px in a target of 24 px, 24 px and the lg control height.

tone.description: The range fill and the thumb: the primary color the style uses on a surface.

step.description: Arrows move one step; PageUp and PageDown move ten.

label.description: Visible name above the track. Each thumb is named by thumbLabels.

showValue.description: Shows the formatted value at the end of the label row. Default true when there is a label.

unit.description: A unit after the number, in the value text and aria-valuetext: %, px, SAR.

formatOptions.description: Intl.NumberFormat options for the value text. Digits are always Western.

formatValue.description: Full control of the value text, aria-valuetext included.

marks.description: Ticks under the track: numbers, or { value, label } objects.

name.description: The form name, submitted as name[] with two values.

invalid.description: A danger tint on the track and aria-invalid on the thumb. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

disabled.description: Inside a Field it follows the Field.

rootProps.description: Props for the root element. className and style also go to the root. The ref goes to the start thumb.

value.description: Controlled low and high values. Pair with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: Uncontrolled starting values. Default [min, max].

onValueChange.description: Called with the pair on every change, while dragging too.

onValueCommit.description: Called with the pair once when a drag ends or a key changes a value.

thumbLabels.description: Required. The accessible name of the start and the end thumb.

minStepsBetweenThumbs.description: Steps that must stay between the thumbs.

a11y.role: slider, on each thumb (a Radix span). Each thumb has its own name, aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext.
a11y.focus: Each thumb is a tab stop, start then end. Focus shows the glow and a 2px ring around the drawn thumb.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the start thumb, then the end thumb, then on
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus back, end thumb then start thumb
keys.ArrowRight, ArrowUp: Raise the value by one step. In right to left text ArrowLeft raises it.
keys.ArrowLeft, ArrowDown: Lower the value by one step. In right to left text ArrowRight lowers it.
keys.PageUp, PageDown: Raise or lower the value by ten steps
keys.Shift+ArrowRight: Moves by ten steps, as PageUp
keys.Home, End: Move the focused thumb as far as it can go: Home toward the minimum, End toward the maximum, stopping before the other thumb

a11y.announce: The thumb's own name (Minimum price), then aria-valuetext with the unit (200 SAR). The visible pair is aria-hidden.
notes: thumbLabels is required: two thumbs with one name cannot be told apart.
The keys move the focused thumb. A thumb stops minStepsBetweenThumbs steps before the other, and a drag stops at the other thumb (preserveThumbOrder), so they never cross.
Every drag has the key path (WCAG 2.5.7). Each thumb is a 24px target.
Values use Western digits in every language.
With a label, the root has role group and is named by it, so the label names the pair while each thumb keeps its own name.

en.label: A noun in sentence case: Price.
en.thumbLabels: A start and an end name with the noun: Minimum price, Maximum price; Start hour, End hour.

ar.label: اسم بدون تشكيل: السعر
ar.thumbLabels: اسم للبداية واسم للنهاية مع الاسم: أقل سعر، أعلى سعر

angular.behavior: div[dsRangeSlider], on the DsSlider body with two thumbs, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root. Inputs take the React prop names; onValueChange is the valueChange output of [(value)] and onValueCommit the valueCommit output. thumbLabels and defaultValue also take a plain array, because a template array literal is not typed as a pair. aria-describedby is an input. Same keys, pointer and DOM as Slider; the thumbs never cross and Home and End stop at the other thumb. One difference from React, the batch 3 and 4 review fix: the thumb that last had focus or a press carries data-active and its wrapper gets z-index 1 in its inline position style, so overlapping thumbs at 320px keep the target a press reaches. Slider.css and RangeSlider.css are used as is.

styles.studio: A thin overlay track, the range and thumb in the bright text color
styles.desk: The same track, the range and thumb in the yellow primary (a darker gold in Desk Light)

mistakes.wrong: Two Sliders for a low and a high value
mistakes.right: One RangeSlider

mistakes.wrong: Both thumbs named Price
mistakes.right: thumbLabels: Minimum price, Maximum price

mistakes.wrong: Filtering on every onValueChange while dragging
mistakes.right: Filter in onValueCommit

name: Rating
summary: Pick or show a score from 1 to 5 (or 10) as stars. Interactive it is a radio group of stars; read only it is an image with a label, with half stars.
useWhen: Asking for a score from 1 to 5 on a review, a session or a template
Showing an average score next to a count of reviews
A 10 point score where stars read better than a number field
avoidWhen: A yes or no answer, or a like
A score with labels for each step (Poor, Fair, Good)
A precise number, a percent or a progress
Scores above 10 steps

value.description: The score, controlled. 0 means not rated. Read only accepts halves (4.5) and rounds to the nearest half.

defaultValue.description: The score at first render, uncontrolled.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new score when a person picks a star.

readOnly.description: Plain markup: the root is role img named "4.5 of 5 stars". Not focusable.

disabled.description: Disables every star.

required.description: Sets aria-required on the group and required on the hidden inputs.

name.description: The form field name of the hidden native inputs.

size.description: Stars of 16, 24 and 24 px in press areas of 24, 28 and 44 px. lg keeps the 24px star (the largest icon size) and grows the touch target.

tone.description: The color of the filled stars. warning: amber. accent: the primary color.

showValue.description: Shows the score as text after the stars.

children.description: Text after the stars, such as (128 reviews). Interactive, it joins aria-describedby.

getItemLabel.description: The name of one star. Default "3 of 5 stars", or "3 من 5 نجوم" in an Arabic Theme.

getValueLabel.description: The name of a read only rating. Default "4.5 of 5 stars", or "Not rated" for 0. In an Arabic Theme "4.5 من 5 نجوم" and "بدون تقييم".

a11y.role: Interactive: radiogroup on the root, named by aria-label or aria-labelledby, and radio on each star, named "3 of 5 stars". Read only: the stars part is role img, named "4.5 of 5 stars"; the text after it stays outside the image and is read.
a11y.focus: One tab stop. Tab lands on the checked star, or the first star when none is checked. Focus shows a 2px ring around the star. Read only is not focusable.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the checked star, and on to the next control
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus back out of the rating
keys.ArrowRight, ArrowLeft: Raise or lower the score by one, in the reading direction: in Arabic ArrowLeft raises it. They stop at 1 and at the highest score.
keys.End: Sets the score to the highest

a11y.announce: Each star is read as a radio with its name, "3 of 5 stars", its checked state and its position. The text after the stars joins aria-describedby. Read only: one image with the score as its name, then the text after it, such as (128 reviews).
notes: Behavior from Radix RadioGroup, horizontal, without wrapping. Home and End are added here: Radix only moves focus on them.
Never color alone: a filled star is a filled shape (star-filled), an empty one an outline (star), a half star the star-half shape, which mirrors in right to left.
The filled colors keep 3:1 against the page (WCAG 1.4.11): warning uses the warning text color, accent the primary border color.
Interactive scores are whole stars. Half stars show only in the read only form.
A picked score cannot be cleared to 0, as in any radio group. Offer a separate action when clearing matters.
Disabled uses native disabled: the stars leave the tab order and draw with opacity.disabled; the text after them stays readable.
Source: GoBanana admin FeedbackList could not be fetched in the lane session. Designed from the dials table in PLAN.md 3.7 and RadioGroup.
The read only stars sit in a stars part with role img, so the value text after them stays readable to assistive tech. aria-labelledby on a read only rating is joined with the score.

en.label: A visible label that says what is rated: Rate this board. It names the group through aria-labelledby.
en.item: "3 of 5 stars", the default. Never a word scale on the stars themselves.
en.value: The score with one decimal at most, and the count in brackets: 4.5 (128 reviews).

ar.label: عنوان ظاهر بصيغة الاسم: تقييم اللوحة
ar.value: الرقم بخانة عشرية وحدة بالكثير، وعدد التقييمات بين قوسين

angular.behavior: div[dsRating], hand built with the Radix RadioGroup DOM on the CDK FocusKeyManager and Directionality, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root: a radiogroup of star buttons, or with readOnly the role img stars and the text. Inputs take the React prop names; onValueChange is the valueChange output of [(value)]; getItemLabel and getValueLabel are function inputs. aria-label, aria-labelledby and aria-describedby are inputs, because React moves them to the stars when read only and merges them with its own ids. The text after the stars is projected content, read once after the first render. Default star names follow the Theme language (3 من 5 نجوم and بدون تقييم in Arabic). Behavior by hand in behavior/roving-radio.ts as React passes it to Radix: horizontal, no loop, arrows in the reading direction, Home and End pick the ends. Works with reactive and template forms. Rating.css is used as is.

native.note: accessibilityRole adjustable with increment and decrement actions, one element for the whole rating.

styles.studio: Pixel stars: outline stars in the hover control border color, filled stars in amber. accent fills in the text color through the Studio recipe, since the Studio primary is neutral and its border is the control grey.
styles.desk: The same pixel stars; accent fills in the yellow primary in dark and the dark gold primary border in light.

mistakes.wrong: Stars colored without changing shape
mistakes.right: Rating draws star-filled and star; keep both shapes in a recipe

mistakes.wrong: An interactive rating to show an average
mistakes.right: readOnly, which is one image with the score as its name

mistakes.wrong: Stars without a name, or a name only on the first star
mistakes.right: aria-labelledby on the Rating; each star is named "3 of 5 stars"

mistakes.wrong: Half stars in a rating people pick
mistakes.right: Whole stars when picking; halves only when showing an average

name: ResizablePanels
summary: Two or more panels side by side or stacked, with dividers a person drags or moves with the keys to share the room. Sizes are percents, reported through onLayout for the app to save.
useWhen: An editor layout: a layers sidebar, the canvas and an inspector the person sizes to their task
A preview over a console or a log that the person makes taller or shorter
Two views compared side by side where the person decides the split
avoidWhen: A list and its detail that should stack on phones
A fixed page frame with a header, a sidebar and main content
Content that should simply wrap to the width it gets
Phone widths: limits are percents, so at 320px panels shrink to 60 to 70px; use SplitView, which stacks

orientation.description: horizontal: panels side by side, in reading order (the first on the right in Arabic). vertical: panels stacked. Sets data-orientation.

sizes.description: Controlled sizes in percent, one per panel, with onSizesChange.

defaultSizes.description: Starting sizes in percent. Default: each panel's defaultSize, the rest shared evenly. Pass the sizes saved from onLayout to restore a layout.

onSizesChange.description: Called on every change, while a drag runs too.

onLayout.description: Called with the settled sizes when a drag ends and after each key. The component keeps no storage.

step.description: The arrow key step in percent.

ResizablePanel.defaultSize.description: The starting size in percent when the group has no defaultSizes.

ResizablePanel.collapsible.description: The panel collapses when dragged past half its min, with Enter or a double click on a handle next to it. Sets data-collapsed.

ResizablePanel.collapsedSize.description: The collapsed size in percent. 0 hides the panel and makes its content inert; a few percent leaves a rail.

ResizableHandle.label.description: The name of the separator. Name the panel it resizes: Resize sidebar. Under lang="ar" the default is تغيير حجم الأقسام.

a11y.role: separator on each handle (the WAI-ARIA window splitter): focusable, aria-valuenow is the size of the panel before it in percent, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax the values Home and End reach (a collapsed panel sits below the min), aria-controls names that panel, aria-orientation is vertical in a horizontal group.
a11y.focus: Each handle is one tab stop, in reading order between its panels. A drag focuses the handle it moves.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next handle or the next control inside a panel
keys.ArrowLeft, ArrowRight: In a horizontal group, move the handle 5 percent left or right on screen. In Arabic the first panel is on the right, so ArrowLeft grows it. An arrow that grows a collapsed panel opens it at its last size.
keys.ArrowUp, ArrowDown: In a vertical group, move the handle 5 percent up or down
keys.Home: Moves the handle to its far start: the panel before it at its min
keys.End: Moves the handle to its far end: the panel before it at its max
keys.Enter: Collapses the collapsible panel next to the handle (the one before it first) and restores it to its last size

a11y.announce: The separator's value, the size of the panel before it in percent, after each key.
notes: Every drag has a key path (WCAG 2.5.7): the arrows, Home, End and Enter do all a drag does.
The handle line is 1px, its target is 24px (size.target-min) spread over both panels (WCAG 2.5.8).
A collapsed panel at size 0 is inert, so its controls leave the tab order and the accessibility tree.
Panels and handles must be children of ResizablePanels, directly or inside fragments and arrays: the group walks them in order. A panel inside another component is not found.
The 24px handle target reaches 11.5px into each panel, so the focus ring can sit over the edge of panel content. Keep interactive content of a panel at least that far from a handle, or pad the panel.
A cancelled drag puts the sizes back. A press with no move reports no layout.
Sizes are layout and never animate; under reduced motion nothing changes.

en.label: Resize plus the panel name, in sentence case: Resize sidebar, Resize inspector.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: تغيير حجم الطبقات، تغيير حجم الخصائص.

angular.behavior: own: the shared resize math, cdk:bidi for the arrow direction
angular.note: ResizablePanels.css is used as is.

native.behavior: own: the shared resize math, an adjustable handle
native.note: Tablets only; phones show one pane at a time through SplitView.

styles.studio: A 1px line in the control border color (3:1) between flat panels; the line darkens on hover and takes the focus color while it drags or has focus, with a small pill grip.
styles.desk: The same hairline and grip on the Desk border tokens.
styles.neutral: The same parts on the Neutral border tokens once 1.10 lands.
styles.liquid: Planned.

mistakes.wrong: A divider that only moves with a pointer
mistakes.right: ResizableHandle moves with the arrows, Home, End and Enter

mistakes.wrong: Saving the layout to localStorage inside the component
mistakes.right: Save the sizes from onLayout in the app and pass them back as defaultSizes

mistakes.wrong: A 1px hit area
mistakes.right: The handle keeps a 1px line in a 24px target

mistakes.wrong: Every handle named Resize
mistakes.right: Name the panel: Resize layers, Resize inspector

name: ScrollArea
summary: A scroll container with thin styled scrollbars over native scrolling, and edge fades on the side that still has content.
useWhen: A panel, a sidebar or a list that scrolls inside a fixed height while the page stays put
A row of chips or tags that scrolls sideways inside its line
A wide table that scrolls on both axes inside a card
avoidWhen: The whole page scrolls: the browser scrollbar is the right one
A short list that fits: let it grow instead
Content that must all be seen at once, such as a form someone fills in

insteadUse.The page itself scrolls: the native page scroll, no component

orientation.description: Which axes scroll. Sets data-orientation. both adds the corner part.

size.description: The scrollbar thickness: md is scrollbar.size (6px), sm two thirds of it. The track adds space.4xs on each side.

scrollbars.description: When the scrollbars show (the Radix type). auto: while content overflows. always: always. scroll: while scrolling. hover: while the pointer is over the area.

fades.description: Edge fades on the side that still has content.

label.description: The name of the viewport when it takes focus. Under lang="ar" the default is محتوى قابل للتمرير. Name what scrolls.

focusable.description: auto: the viewport joins the tab order (tabindex 0, role region, named) only when its content overflows and it holds no focusable child.

viewportRef.description: A ref to the viewport, the element that scrolls, for scrollTo and scroll restore.

onScroll.description: Called on every scroll of the viewport.

a11y.role: none on the root. The viewport is a region named by label while it takes focus.
a11y.focus: The viewport takes focus (tabindex 0) only when its content overflows and it has no focusable child, so a keyboard user can reach it and scroll. With focusable children, Tab moves through them and the browser scrolls each into view.

keys.Tab: Moves to the viewport when it takes focus, else to the first focusable child
keys.ArrowUp, ArrowDown: Native scrolling of the focused viewport by a line
keys.ArrowLeft, ArrowRight: Native scrolling along the inline axis when it scrolls
keys.Home, End: Native scrolling to the start and the end

a11y.announce: Nothing. The scrollbars and the fades are hidden from assistive technology, which reads the content in order.
notes: Scrolling stays native: wheel, touch, keys, find in page and scroll into view all work. No custom wheel handling.
The vertical scrollbar sits on the inline end, so on the left in right to left layouts. Horizontal fades mirror too.
The keys are the browser's own scrolling of a focused scroll container, so the contract suite notes them; ScrollArea.test.tsx covers the focus rule and the overflow states.
visible and hidden are the data-state of the Radix scrollbar and thumb parts under scrollbars scroll or hover.
With orientation both, the fades and the overflow states follow the block axis only.

The scrollbar.thumb token measures under 3:1 on every surface (1.5 to 2.7), so the thumb draws in color.text.muted, which meets 3:1 on body and surface 1 to 4 in every style and scheme. It does not on surface 5 in Studio and Desk dark (2.5): keep a ScrollArea off surface 5 there until the thumb token is fixed.
The 4px and 6px thumbs are under the 24px target of WCAG 2.5.8; the equivalent exception applies, since wheel, touch and the keys on the focusable viewport scroll the same content.
A focusable viewport is a region named by label, with a built in default name. Several areas with the default give several regions of the same name, so always pass label.
Edge fades fade into --_scroll-area-fade-color, the body color by default. A parent on another surface sets that private property to its own fill from its own CSS.

en.label: Name what scrolls, in sentence case: Release notes, Activity, Board tags.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: الملاحظات، النشاط، الوسوم.

angular.behavior: own: native overflow with the same parts drawn over it, cdk:bidi for the side
angular.note: ScrollArea.css is used as is.

native.note: The platform draws its own scroll indicators; fades use a gradient overlay.

styles.studio: A 6px thumb in the muted text color on a clear track. Fades into the body color.
styles.desk: The same thumb in the Desk muted text color.
styles.neutral: The same thumb in the Neutral muted text color.
styles.liquid: Planned: content scrolls under glass bars, with the scroll edge fade.

mistakes.wrong: A scroll box with no way in for the keyboard
mistakes.right: ScrollArea gives the viewport tabindex 0 and a name when nothing inside can take focus

mistakes.wrong: Replacing wheel scrolling with a script for smooth scroll
mistakes.right: ScrollArea keeps native scrolling; only the bars are drawn

mistakes.wrong: A ScrollArea with no size from its parent, so it grows and never scrolls
mistakes.right: Give the root a block size, a max block size or a flex or grid cell

mistakes.wrong: Wrapping the whole page in a ScrollArea
mistakes.right: Let the page scroll natively; use ScrollArea for panels inside it

mistakes.wrong: scrollbars scroll or hover with fades false, so nothing at rest shows that the area scrolls
mistakes.right: Keep fades on when the bars hide at rest, or use scrollbars auto or always

mistakes.wrong: Two ScrollAreas on one page with no label, both announced as Scrollable content
mistakes.right: A label on every ScrollArea that names what scrolls

name: ScrubInput
summary: The Studio inspector number: drag the label to scrub, type a value or an expression such as 12*2, or nudge with the arrow keys.
useWhen: A design property in an inspector panel: position, size, rotation, opacity, spacing
A value people tune by feel while they watch the canvas change
A field that must show one value for a multi selection, or say the values differ (mixed)
avoidWhen: A count or an amount in a form, where step buttons help more than a drag
A value on a known range picked by eye
Touch first screens, where a horizontal drag fights the page scroll

label.description: The scrub handle: a short letter (W, H, X) or an icon name. Hidden from assistive tech; the field is named by aria-label or the Field label.

value.description: The value, controlled. null is empty.

defaultValue.description: The first value, uncontrolled. Default empty.

onChange.description: Called with every value: each pixel of a drag, each nudge, a typed commit on Enter or blur.

onChangeEnd.description: Called once when a change is done: the end of a drag, a nudge, a typed commit. One undo entry per gesture.

aria-label.description: The full name of the field (Width, Position X). Required outside a Field, since a letter label is not a name.

placeholder.description: Shown while empty, such as Auto. Mixed shows mixedLabel instead.

step.description: One arrow key press and one pixel of drag. Shift is ten steps, Alt a tenth.

precision.description: Decimals the value keeps and shows.

unit.description: The unit shown after the value: px, %, deg. A typed value may carry this unit or none; another unit is refused.

mixed.description: The values of a selection differ: the field is empty and shows mixedLabel. Drag and arrows wait for a typed value.

mixedLabel.description: The word shown while mixed. Arabic: متعدد.

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28 and 32 px at default density. Inspectors use sm or xs.

invalid.description: Marks the value invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

disabled.description: Native disabled on the input; no scrub. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: Readable and focusable; no scrub and no nudge. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

rootProps.description: Props for the root. className and style also go to the root; the ref and native input props go to the input.

a11y.role: textbox, from the native input. The scrub handle is aria-hidden: a pointer only shortcut for the arrow keys.
a11y.focus: The input is the only tab stop. A press on the handle with no move focuses the input and selects its text, read only too. Focus and a drag show the 2px ring.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the input, and on to the next control
keys.ArrowUp: Adds one step; with Shift ten steps, with Alt a tenth of a step
keys.ArrowDown: Takes away one step; with Shift ten steps, with Alt a tenth of a step
keys.Enter: Commits the typed value or expression, keeps focus and selects it
keys.Escape: Reverts the typed text and keeps focus; with nothing typed it goes on to the parent

a11y.announce: Name from aria-label or the Field label. The unit and the Field description and error through aria-describedby. Mixed reads as the placeholder.
notes: Every drag has a key path: the arrow keys move the same steps as the drag (WCAG 2.5.7).
A drag toward the inline end grows the value, so the drag direction flips in RTL. The ew-resize cursor points both ways and needs no flip.
Typing accepts arithmetic: + - * / and parentheses, the times and divide signs, Arabic Indic digits and the Arabic decimal mark. The value shows Western digits.
A typed text that is not arithmetic, or carries a unit other than the field's, goes back to the last value. It never becomes a zero.
Pass aria-label outside a Field: a letter such as W is not a name.

en.label: One letter or an icon for the handle: W, H, X, Y. The aria-label is the full noun: Width, Position X.
en.unit: The CSS unit or symbol: px, %, deg.

ar.label: حرف واحد أو أيقونة للمقبض، والاسم الكامل في aria-label: العرض، الطول

react.behavior: hand built, pointer capture for the scrub; logic in @the-system/shared scrub.ts and number.ts
react.note: Motion: fade, for the focus ring. The value follows the pointer with no animation; only the focus ring fades (an opacity transition).

angular.behavior: div[dsScrubInput], hand built, pointer capture for the scrub; logic in packages/shared scrub.ts and number.ts, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: Same DOM and keys as React. value is a model: [(value)]; defaultValue is value, onChange is valueChange (every drag move) and onChangeEnd is the changeEnd output (once per gesture). label takes a letter, an icon name or a TemplateRef. rootProps, className and style have no input: attributes on the host already land on the root.

styles.studio: A filled inspector rectangle (inspector.field.bg), no border at rest, the 2px ring on focus and while dragging
styles.desk: The same filled field on the Desk inspector fill

mistakes.wrong: A letter label as the only name of the field
mistakes.right: aria-label with the full noun, or a Field label

mistakes.wrong: A drag with no keyboard path
mistakes.right: The arrow keys on the input move the same steps

mistakes.wrong: A typed 5em in a px field kept as 5
mistakes.right: Refused and reverted: the unit must be the field's, or none

mistakes.wrong: Showing the first value of a multi selection
mistakes.right: mixed, so the field says the values differ

mistakes.wrong: ScrubInput in a checkout or a booking form
mistakes.right: NumberField, with step buttons

name: SearchField
summary: A search box: a search icon, a search input, a clear button while there is a query, an optional end slot and a loading state.
useWhen: Filtering a list, a table or a grid on the same page as the person types
A search box in a toolbar, a sidebar or a menu that runs a search on Enter
A query the person often clears and types again
avoidWhen: Picking one value from a list of known options while typing
A command palette that runs actions
A plain text value that is not a query

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px at default density. The clear button is xs, and sm at lg.

shape.description: default takes radius.control from the style, a pill in Studio and Desk. pill is always fully round.

value.description: The query, controlled. Pair it with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: The first query, uncontrolled.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new query on every edit, and with an empty string when the clear button or Escape clears it.

onSubmit.description: Called with the query on Enter. A form around the field still submits as usual.

onClear.description: Called after the clear button or Escape clears the query.

clearLabel.description: The accessible name of the clear button.

loading.description: Results are on their way: a spinner at the start of the end slot and a polite status. The end content stays, so a focused end button keeps focus.

loadingLabel.description: What the status says while loading.

end.description: Content after the clear button: a filter IconButton at size xs, or a keyboard hint (Kbd, once that component lands). The spinner shows before it while loading.

invalid.description: Inside a Field it follows the Field.

disabled.description: Native disabled on the input. Inside a Field it follows the Field. Hides the clear button.

readOnly.description: Inside a Field it follows the Field. Hides the clear button; Escape does not clear.

rootProps.description: Props for the root box. className and style also go to the root; every other native prop and the ref go to the input.

a11y.role: searchbox, from the native input with type search. Wrap a site or app search in a form or an element with role search; a filter for one list needs no landmark.
a11y.focus: The input is a tab stop, then the clear button while it shows, then any end content. Clicking the box outside a button focuses the input. Clearing returns focus to the input.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the input, then to the clear button and the end content
keys.Escape: Clears the query, before a Dialog or Popover around it sees the key, so they stay open. On an empty box it does nothing here, so the layer around it closes
keys.Enter: Calls onSubmit with the query; a form around it submits. An Enter that ends an IME composition does nothing

a11y.announce: Name from the Field label or aria-label. While loading, a polite status says the loading label once. The clear button is named by clearLabel.
notes: The browser's own clear button is hidden, so only one clear button shows.
No native title attribute. A placeholder says what is searched, never instead of a name.
Results that update as the person types: announce the count in a polite status of the page, after typing pauses, not on every key.
The clear part is an IconButton until CloseButton (order 1.1.9) lands; the part name stays clear.
The control part is the nested Input root; the native input inside it is that Input's own control part.

en.label: Search plus what is searched: Search boards, Search members.
en.placeholder: The same words as the name, or what can be typed: Search by name or email.

ar.label: البحث في اللوحات، البحث في الأعضاء

react.behavior: hand built on Input with type search
react.note: The root is the bordered box; the nested Input is the control part and keeps the Field wiring and the ref. The focus glow fades in as on Input; the spinner stops under reduced motion.

angular.behavior: div[dsSearchField] on dsInput and dsIconButton, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The root is the bordered box; the nested dsInput is the control part and keeps the Field wiring. value is a model (defaultValue is value); onValueChange, onSubmit and onClear are the valueChange, submit and clear outputs. end takes a TemplateRef. Escape clears in a window capture listener, as in React. Inside an InputGroup it is the control.

styles.studio: The Input look: a bordered transparent pill, the soft glow and the 2px ring on focus, a muted search icon at the start.
styles.desk: The same pill and glow, in Instrument Sans.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: An Input with type search and a second clear button next to the browser's own
mistakes.right: SearchField, which hides the native one

mistakes.wrong: Escape that clears and closes the dialog around the field in one press
mistakes.right: The first Escape clears; only an Escape on the empty box reaches the dialog

mistakes.wrong: A placeholder as the only name
mistakes.right: aria-label in a toolbar, a Field label in a form

mistakes.right: One polite status after typing pauses

name: Section
summary: A titled region of a page or panel: a heading at a level you set, an optional description and actions, and a body that can collapse.
useWhen: A page or a settings screen splits into titled groups
An inspector or side panel has groups of properties the user opens and closes
A group needs header actions next to its title, such as add or a menu
avoidWhen: Several groups where only one may be open at a time
Switching between views of the same content
A box that needs its own background or border
A hint that shows and hides one short line

title.description: The title. Required. It is the toggle's name when collapsible.

level.description: The heading level of the title, h1 to h6. Required, no default: it follows the page outline and is never guessed. React takes the numbers.

description.description: A line under the title. The toggle points aria-describedby at it.

actions.description: Trailing header actions, outside the toggle.

size.description: sm for panels and inspectors, md for pages.

collapsible.description: The title becomes a toggle that shows and hides the body. With no children there is nothing to disclose, so the header draws alone, with no toggle. A child component that renders nothing still counts as a body: pass no children instead.

defaultOpen.description: Open state on first render, uncontrolled.

onOpenChange.description: Called with the next open state.

landmark.description: Names the section with its title (aria-labelledby), which makes it a region landmark. The title id is added to any aria-labelledby passed.

a11y.role: No role of its own: a section element, which is a region landmark only with landmark set. The title is a heading at level. The toggle is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
a11y.focus: A static section is not focusable. A collapsible one puts the toggle in the tab order, then the actions, then the body content.

keys.Tab: Moves to the toggle, then the header actions, then the body
keys.Enter: On the toggle: opens or closes the body
keys.Space: On the toggle: opens or closes the body

a11y.announce: The heading at its level, then the toggle as a button with its expanded state and description. A closed body is hidden from everyone.
notes: The toggle sits inside the heading (the disclosure pattern), so the heading keeps its place in the outline.
Header actions are siblings of the toggle, never inside it: a control inside a control is invalid and unreachable by keyboard.
The chevron points forward when closed and down when open. chevron-forward mirrors in right to left layouts.
Radix stamps data-state on the toggle Button too (open or closed). It is the Section's state, carried by its toggle part.

en.title: A noun or short noun phrase in sentence case: Billing, Notifications.
en.description: One sentence that says what is inside. No period after a fragment.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics: الفوترة، الإشعارات.
ar.description: White Saudi dialect, one short sentence.

angular.behavior: cdk:accordion item (single, not grouped)
angular.note: Same DOM: the toggle is a dsButton inside the heading. Section.css is used as is.

native.note: The body collapses with the accordion-height preset of the style.

styles.studio: No fill, no radius, a hairline between sections, a bold title (small at size sm, as the inspector section).
styles.desk: The same on the glass of a window. The toggle is a square ghost button with no roll label.
styles.neutral: The same structure, with the Neutral hairline and type scale.
styles.liquid: Content stays solid: a Section is never glass.

mistakes.wrong: An IconButton for add placed inside the toggle
mistakes.right: The actions prop, beside the toggle

mistakes.wrong: Guessing the heading level from nesting
mistakes.right: Set level from the page outline

mistakes.wrong: A collapsible section with nothing inside and a chevron that opens an empty body
mistakes.right: Pass no children: the header draws alone

mistakes.wrong: Every section as a landmark
mistakes.right: landmark only for a few regions a user would jump to

name: SegmentedControl
summary: One choice among two to five views or modes, always one selected: a track of items with a thumb that slides to the selected one.
useWhen: Switching the view of the same content in place: list or grid, day, week or month
Picking a mode or a range that applies at once: monthly or yearly billing, 7 or 30 days on a chart
Two to five short options where exactly one is always on and all fit on one line
avoidWhen: The choice shows different panels of content, each with its own heading
A choice in a form that is saved with the form
More than five options, or options that need long labels
Options that can be on together, or none at all

value.description: The selected value, controlled. Pair with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: The value selected at first, uncontrolled. Set it: one item is always selected.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new value. Never called with an empty value: a press on the selected item does nothing.

aria-label.description: The control's name, for example Calendar range. Required unless aria-labelledby is set.

aria-labelledby.description: The id of a visible label that names the control. Required unless aria-label is set.

size.description: Height of the whole control: md 32 and lg 44 px from size.control in the default density, sm 28 px, xs 26 px (xs and sm drop the inset so every item keeps its 24px target).

shape.description: pill is fully round (radius.pill), default takes radius.control, square takes radius.sm. The item and thumb corners nest inside the track's.

disabled.description: Every item is disabled (aria-disabled, stays focusable, never selected). Sets data-disabled on the root.

fullWidth.description: Fills the width of its container; the items share it equally. A label that does not fit wraps onto a second line and the item grows in height, so keep labels short. Sets data-full-width.

children.description: Two to five SegmentedControlItems, each with a unique value. An item takes children (the label), start, icon with label for the icon only form, and disabled.

a11y.role: radiogroup of radio items with aria-checked (Radix ToggleGroup type single), named by aria-label or aria-labelledby
a11y.focus: One tab stop: Tab enters on the selected item. Selection follows focus: the arrows, Home and End move focus and select. Disabled items keep aria-disabled and stay focusable and in the arrow order (anatomy rule 5); focus on them does not select.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the selected item, then out of the control
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus out of the control, backward
keys.ArrowRight: Selects the next item in the reading direction (the previous one in RTL); wraps
keys.ArrowLeft: Selects the previous item in the reading direction (the next one in RTL); wraps
keys.Space: Selects the focused item; on the selected item it does nothing
keys.Enter: Selects the focused item; on the selected item it does nothing

a11y.announce: The control name when focus enters, then the item name with checked and its position in the set, for example Week, radio button, checked, 2 of 3.
notes: Selected is not told by color alone: the thumb is a filled shape with a 2px inner ring (as ToggleButton's on ring), and the text is the bright text.
The indicator is aria-hidden: the radio state carries the selection.
In forced colors the thumb hides and the selected item is drawn in Highlight and HighlightText.
Every icon only item needs its own label.

The contract suite checks the arrows, Home and End as focus-moves; that the selection follows focus, and that Space and Enter select, are unit tests (SegmentedControl.test.tsx), since focusing an item already selects it.
Disabled items stay focusable; Shift+Tab from one leaves the control backward.

en.name: Name the control by what it sets: Calendar range, Board view, Billing period. Sentence case.
en.labels: One or two words in sentence case, a noun for the view or mode: Day, Week, Month; List, Grid. Keep the labels about the same length. Digits are Western: 7 days.

ar.name: Noun form, no diacritics: نطاق التقويم، عرض اللوحة.
ar.labels: Short noun form labels, no diacritics: يوم، أسبوع، شهر؛ شهري، سنوي. Western digits.

react.behavior: radix:ToggleGroup type single, the value never empty, selection follows focus; items are ToggleButton roots on ButtonBase
react.note: The indicator is measured from the selected item (logical start, top, inline and block size) and slides with transform only. Reduced motion plays nothing: it jumps. A ResizeObserver re-places it, without motion, when density, fonts or labels change the size. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction tab-slide: the thumb slides with the shared pill (internal/indicator.ts) on the snappy spring, stretched along its travel, and the labels dip and pop. Reduced motion: it jumps.

angular.behavior: div[dsSegmentedControl] and button[dsSegmentedControlItem] on DsButtonBase, hand built with the Radix ToggleGroup type single DOM on behavior/roving-radio.ts (CDK FocusKeyManager and Directionality), the indicator placed by the same measuring and the motion catalog, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root (role radiogroup) with the indicator span as its first child; each item host is a ToggleButton root with data-part item, role radio and aria-checked. onValueChange is the valueChange output of [(value)]. start and icon take an icon name or a TemplateRef. Selection follows focus; a press on the selected item is ignored, so the value never goes empty. The indicator is placed after each render that changes the value (afterRenderEffect) and on resize, and slides with tab-indicator. Works with reactive and template forms. SegmentedControl.css and Button.css are used as is.

native.behavior: rn-primitives:toggle-group type single, the thumb moved with Reanimated from the tab-indicator native numbers
native.note: 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android.

styles.studio: An overlay track with a hairline; the thumb is the overlay-20 fill; a pill by default.
styles.desk: The same pill track and thumb in Desk's overlay and border colors.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: A SegmentedControl that switches between panels of content
mistakes.right: Tabs, which names and links each panel

mistakes.wrong: A SegmentedControl with no selected item
mistakes.right: Set defaultValue or value: one item is always selected

mistakes.wrong: Seven options squeezed into one control
mistakes.right: At most five; use Select for more

mistakes.wrong: A SegmentedControl inside a form that is saved with a submit button
mistakes.right: RadioGroup inside a Field

mistakes.wrong: Animating the thumb with left or width
mistakes.right: The tab-indicator pattern, transform only, that jumps under reduced motion

name: Select
summary: A closed trigger that opens a short list and keeps one value from it. The trigger shows the chosen label; the list opens under it and takes focus while it is open.
useWhen: One value from a short list of about 4 to 12 options that people read rather than search, such as a sort order, a status or a time zone region
A form row with little room, where the options need not all show at once
A value that must be one of the options, with a sensible default or a placeholder
avoidWhen: A long list (more than about 12 options) that people find faster by typing
Two to five options that fit on the page and read better side by side
Several values at once
An action to run, not a value to keep

items.description: An array of options, plain ({ value, label, description?, start?, disabled?, keywords? }) or in titled groups ({ label, options }), as ListBox takes them (type node here means structured data). A separator is drawn between groups. Typeahead reads the label.

value.description: The chosen option value, controlled with onValueChange. null: none, the placeholder shows.

defaultValue.description: Uncontrolled starting value.

onValueChange.description: Called with the chosen value.

open.description: The list is open, controlled with onOpenChange.

placeholder.description: Shown in the trigger when nothing is chosen. Arabic default: اختيار من القائمة. Never the only label: wrap the Select in a Field.

size.description: Trigger height from size.control (28, 32, 44px at default density). sm lists use sm rows; md and lg lists use list.row.height, the ListBox row. lg uses a fixed 16px type so phones do not zoom.

shape.description: default: the style's control radius (a pill in Studio and Desk). pill: always fully round.

invalid.description: The danger border and aria-invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field's error.

disabled.description: Native disabled on the trigger: out of the tab order, the list never opens. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: The value shows and the trigger stays focusable, but no key, typeahead or press opens the list or changes the value. aria-readonly, a dashed border, no chevron.

required.description: aria-required on the trigger and required on the hidden native select. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

loading.description: Options are on their way: the icon is a spinner, aria-busy and data-loading are set, the trigger is described by loadingLabel (aria-describedby), and the list does not open.

loadingLabel.description: What the trigger is described by while loading. Arabic default: جار تحميل الخيارات.

empty.default: No options to choose from yet.
empty.description: With no option the list does not open and the trigger is described by these words (aria-describedby). Pass them: the default cannot know what to do next, so say why there is no option and the next step. Arabic default: ما فيه خيارات للاختيار.

name.description: Submits the value under this name in a form (Radix renders a hidden native select).

form.description: The id of a form outside the Select's own ancestors that the hidden native select submits with (passed to Radix Root).

a11y.role: combobox on the trigger (Radix Select: aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-autocomplete none), named by the Field label. The open list is a listbox of option rows (aria-selected on the chosen one, aria-disabled on the disabled ones) in titled groups. While the list is open the rest of the page is hidden from assistive tech and Tab does not leave it.
a11y.focus: The trigger is one tab stop. Opening moves focus to the chosen item, else the first enabled one. Escape, a choice or a press outside closes the list and returns focus to the trigger.

keys.Enter: On the trigger, opens the list. On an item, chooses it and closes the list
keys.Space: On the trigger, opens the list. On an item, chooses it and closes the list
keys.ArrowDown: On the trigger, opens the list. In the list, moves to the next item, skipping disabled ones
keys.ArrowUp: On the trigger, opens the list. In the list, moves to the previous item
keys.Home: In the list, moves to the first item
keys.End: In the list, moves to the last item
keys.Typeahead: On the closed trigger, typing letters chooses the next option whose label starts with them. In the list, it moves to that item
keys.Escape: Closes the list without changing the value and returns focus to the trigger

a11y.announce: The trigger reads its Field label, the chosen label (or the placeholder), and that it opens a list. Moving through the list reads each option: its label, its description, selected or not, unavailable, and its position.
notes: Tab does not move focus while the list is open (Radix keeps it in the list); Escape or a choice returns focus to the trigger.

The open listbox is named like the trigger: through the Field label, else aria-label or aria-labelledby on the Select. With no option the list does not open (an empty listbox is not valid): the trigger is described by the empty text, as it is by the loading words while loading.
Read only, loading and empty block only the keys that open the list or choose by typeahead; Tab and browser shortcuts with a modifier pass.
The chosen item shows a check on every style, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The check column is on every row so labels line up.
Rows equal ListBox option rows: the same list.row.height (sm: size.control.xs), padding, gap, radius, type and highlight tokens. Rows and the scroll buttons are at least size.target-min (WCAG 2.5.8).
The content is portaled into a Theme copied from the trigger's Theme and is its own root carrying data-part content, as the Combobox popup is; its z-index is z.menu so it shows over a Dialog.
Disabled is native disabled (a form control, anatomy.md rule 5). Read only keeps the trigger focusable with aria-readonly and blocks every key but Tab and the pointer.
An option description is read through aria-describedby on the item.

Contract: the variants case marks one trigger with data-demo-trigger. Enter, Space and ArrowDown on the trigger are checked as state changes (aria-expanded), because Radix opens on keydown and prevents the click. The closed trigger stamps no data-state (it reads as open through aria-expanded); data-state open is on the content root.

contract.skipAxeRules aria-hidden-focus: while the list is open, Radix Select hides the rest of the page with aria-hidden and traps focus in the list (a focus scope, and pointer events off outside it), so the other triggers on the page cannot be reached until it closes. Axe flags those hidden triggers by shape. The closed pages passed axe with the rule on in the lane run before it was skipped (docs/reports/lanes/lane-3d.md).

States: open is data-state on the content root; when closed the content is not in the DOM (Radix Select has no exit presence), so no element stamps closed. closed stays in states because the contract suite treats a component as an overlay, and opens it, only when states lists both open and closed. checked and unchecked are data-state on each item.

en.label: A noun in a Field label: Sort by, Status, Region.
en.placeholder: Optional: Choose an option. Better, preselect a sensible default.
en.options: Short nouns, sentence case, parallel in form: To do, In progress, Done. Order by use or by a natural order, not alphabetically by default.
en.empty: Say what to do next: No statuses yet. Add one from Settings.
en.error: Say what to do: Choose a status for the task.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: الحالة، الترتيب حسب.
ar.options: Nouns as people write them, Western digits: قيد التنفيذ، مكتملة.
ar.empty: ما فيه حالات. أضف حالة من الإعدادات.

react.behavior: radix:Select (Root, Trigger, Value, Icon, Content in popper position, Viewport, Item, ItemText, Group, Label, Separator, ScrollUpButton, ScrollDownButton)
react.note: Sources Figma-Killer-2 Select/ and GoBanana .st-menu were not reachable in the lane session; the trigger follows the Combobox field (the Input box) and the rows the ListBox option rows. Radix Select has no exit presence, so the list leaves at once on close.

angular.behavior: button[dsSelect], hand built with the Radix Select DOM and keys: a CDK ComponentPortal list placed with the Radix Popper steps (internal/popper.ts), focus moved into the list, typeahead from the shared listbox.ts, the page hidden and scroll locked while open (behavior/dialog-behavior.ts), ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the trigger, the root. Inputs take the React prop names; onValueChange and onOpenChange are the valueChange and openChange outputs of [(value)] and [(open)]. aria-label, aria-labelledby and aria-describedby are inputs, as the list reads them too. empty takes text or a TemplateRef. The loading words and, inside a form, the Radix bubble select are siblings after the trigger, added by the component. The Radix Spinner DOM is inline until the Angular Spinner exists. Typeahead folds Arabic like the rest of the list family, with the Radix pause of 1000ms. Angular Aria Select would replace the hand built keys once @angular/aria is installed. Select.css is used as is.

styles.studio: The trigger is the Input box: a transparent pill with the control border, the glow and the ring on focus or while open, chevrons up and down at the end. The list is the Studio menu surface: surface-3, the card radius, the menu shadow; the lit row takes the overlay step.
styles.desk: The same trigger. The list is the Desk menu glass: the strong material and blur, a hairline, the panel radius with field radius rows, regular weight; the lit row is the yellow primary fill with dark text. Under reduced transparency and more contrast the glass turns solid.
styles.neutral: Tokens only: the Neutral control radius and border, the Neutral menu surface.

mistakes.wrong: A Select with 40 cities
mistakes.right: A Combobox, which filters as people type

mistakes.wrong: A Select with two options, Yes and No
mistakes.right: A RadioGroup, or a Switch for an on and off setting

mistakes.wrong: A Select whose options run actions (Delete, Duplicate)
mistakes.right: A DropdownMenu

mistakes.wrong: The placeholder as the only label
mistakes.right: A Field with a label around the Select

mistakes.wrong: Showing the chosen option by color alone
mistakes.right: The check in the indicator column (built in)

mistakes.wrong: A read only Select drawn as disabled
mistakes.right: readOnly: focusable and readable, with a dashed border

name: Separator
summary: A thin line between groups of content, horizontal or vertical, with an optional short centered label.
useWhen: Between groups of items in a menu, a toolbar or a settings list
Between two ways to do one thing, with a label such as Or
Between a day of messages and the next, with the date as the label
avoidWhen: Between every item of a list: the gap already separates them
As the border of a panel or a card
To make room: the line adds no space of its own
A heading for the group that follows

orientation.description: horizontal runs along the line, between stacked groups. vertical stands between items in a row and stretches to its height. Sets data-orientation.

decorative.description: true: role none, hidden from assistive tech, drawn with color.border.subtle. false: role separator, announced, drawn with color.border.control, 3:1 on body and surface 1 to 3 (2.4 to 2.9 on surface 4 and 5 in the dark schemes and Neutral light). Sets data-decorative when true.

label.description: Short centered text on the line, for example Or. On a semantic separator it is the accessible name (aria-labelledby). Renders the label part and two line parts, and sets data-labelled.

a11y.role: separator when decorative is false, none when it is true (Radix Separator)
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: A semantic separator is announced as a separator, with its label as the name. A decorative one is silent; its label text, if any, is read as plain text in the flow.
notes: A semantic separator is a boundary a person needs to see, so its line meets 3:1 against the surface (WCAG 1.4.11). A decorative line may be quieter.
The line is a border, so it stays visible in forced colors (CanvasText, GrayText when decorative).
The two line parts of a labelled separator are hidden from assistive tech.

en.label: One or two words in sentence case: Or, Older messages. No colon, no full stop.

ar.label: A short noun or particle: أو، الرسائل الأقدم. No diacritics.

react.note: No motion: a static line has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies. No spacing prop: the gap of the parent Stack or Grid spaces the groups.

angular.behavior: [dsSeparator] directive with role and aria-orientation host bindings
angular.note: Label through content projection with the same line and label parts.

native.note: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth; accessible false when decorative.

styles.studio: A 1px line in the subtle border color; Studio otherwise separates tiles by the 1px gap.
styles.desk: A 1px hairline inside windows.
styles.neutral: A 1px line, the main way Neutral separates groups.
styles.liquid: A 1px line on solid content; glass bars use spacing instead.

mistakes.wrong: A separator between every row of a list
mistakes.right: A gap, or a separator only between groups

mistakes.wrong: An hr with margin-left and margin-right
mistakes.right: Separator inside a Stack, which spaces it with the gap

mistakes.wrong: A decorative separator that marks the only boundary between two forms
mistakes.right: decorative false, so it is announced and drawn at 3:1

mistakes.wrong: A long sentence as the label
mistakes.right: One or two words; a sentence belongs in a heading or a paragraph

name: Sheet
summary: A modal panel that rises from the bottom of the screen, for phone layouts and quick tasks. A drag handle closes it, with the close control and Escape as the key path.
useWhen: A quick task on a phone layout: share, pick an option, a short form
More options for an item where a menu would be too cramped on touch
Content the person checks and dismisses, close to the thumb
avoidWhen: A desktop side panel for filters or details
A question about an action that cannot be undone
A short decision on a wide screen
Content that needs the full page

onOpenChange.description: Called with false for Escape, a backdrop click, the close control, SheetClose and a drag down.

size.description: The most of the screen's height it takes: sm half, md three quarters, lg all of it under a top gap. Never wider than the xl dialog width, centered on wide screens.

dismissible.description: false: Escape, a backdrop click and a drag do nothing, and the close control is aria-disabled.

title.description: SheetContent: the title for the common case, the same as a SheetTitle child.

description.description: SheetContent: the description for the common case.

closeLabel.description: SheetContent: the accessible name of the close control. Arabic default under lang ar: إغلاق النافذة السفلية.

rootProps.description: SheetContent: props for the root layer. className and style go to the root too; ref and every other prop go to the panel, Radix Content props included.

SheetTrigger.description: One child element, a system Button, rendered as the trigger (always asChild). Focus returns to it on close.

SheetClose.description: One child element, a system Button that closes the sheet (always asChild), marked data-dialog-cancel.

data-autofocus.description: Put on any focusable element inside the sheet to take focus on open.

a11y.role: dialog (the panel), modal: Radix hides the rest of the page from assistive tech and keeps focus inside. Named by the title, described by the description.
a11y.focus: The Dialog focus rule: an element marked data-autofocus, else the first field in the body, else the first footer action that is not tone danger, else the close control. On close, focus returns to the trigger, or to the element that had focus before.

keys.Escape: Closes the sheet, unless dismissible is false. The key path for the drag down.
keys.Tab: Moves to the next control inside the sheet and wraps from the last to the first
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves to the previous control inside the sheet and wraps from the first to the last

a11y.announce: The title and the description are read when the sheet opens. The handle is hidden from assistive tech: the close control is the same action.
notes: The drag to dismiss has a button path, the close control, and a key path, Escape (WCAG 2.5.7). The handle is a pointer target only, out of the tab order.
A release past a quarter of the panel's height, or a quick flick down, closes it; a shorter drag snaps back. The panel never rises above its open place.
The panel keeps clear of the home bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
Detents are wave 2.
No native title attribute.
When the whole panel scrolls (a short viewport, 400% zoom) the handle scrolls away; the close control stays.

Order 1.23: the handle holds a handle-bar part that draws the bar and takes --_dialog-handle-radius. Dragged above its place, or down on a sheet with dismissible false, the panel follows a third of the pointer (a rubber band) and springs back. Detents are not built yet.

en.title: The task as a noun phrase or a question: Share Spring launch.
en.buttons: Verb plus noun: Send invite, Cancel invite. Never OK or Continue.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics: مشاركة اللوحة
ar.buttons: Noun form labels: إرسال الدعوة، إلغاء الدعوة.

react.note: Built on DialogBase (Dialog folder). The drag uses pointer events with pointer capture on the handle. Styled by the sheet block of Dialog.css.

angular.behavior: cdk:portal, cdk:a11y InteractivityChecker
angular.note: On the Angular Dialog layer, with the handle and data-dragging.

native.note: A native bottom sheet with detents in wave 2, spring.sheet.

styles.studio: A surface panel from the bottom with radius.sheet on the top corners, a handle bar, a header without a band color, the footer band. It rises on duration.slow, ease.emphasized.
styles.desk: The Desk dialog glass, hairline and window shadow, with radius.sheet on the top corners.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass sheet.

mistakes.wrong: A bottom toast over the Sheet footer, where focus cannot reach it while the Sheet is open
mistakes.right: Nothing to do: while a Sheet is open a bottom toaster moves to the top edge (Dialog.css), and goes back when it closes. While toasts show there, the Sheet root sets --_sheet-toast-end and its top gap grows, so an lg panel and its close control stay below them

mistakes.wrong: A sheet that closes only by dragging
mistakes.right: The close control and Escape close it too; the handle is a shortcut

mistakes.wrong: A sheet as the desktop filter panel
mistakes.right: Drawer

mistakes.wrong: Content under the home bar
mistakes.right: The panel pads its block end with the safe area inset

mistakes.wrong: Waiting for transitionend after a drag
mistakes.right: The close runs from state; under reduced motion every duration is 0

name: Sidebar
summary: The side navigation of an app: groups of links with icons and counts, a header, a footer and a collapsed icon form.
useWhen: The main navigation of an app with more than five destinations, kept in view on every page
Destinations that fall into named groups (Workspace, Projects, Admin), some of which may fold away
Destinations that carry a count, such as unread messages or open tasks
Settings or admin areas with a list of sections down the side
avoidWhen: Three to five destinations on a phone layout
A narrow column of icons only, with no labels or groups
Switching between views of one page or one record
The top navigation of a marketing site with a brand and dropdown panels
Actions that change data, such as Save or Delete

label.description: The accessible name of the nav landmark: Main, Settings. Not drawn.

size.description: Row height from size.control: sm 28px, md 32px at default density. Compact makes them 24 and 28, comfortable 32 and 36.

collapsed.description: Controlled collapsed state: items show only their icons, labels stay as the accessible names.

defaultCollapsed.description: Collapsed at first render when uncontrolled.

onCollapsedChange.description: Called with the next collapsed state when the toggle is pressed.

collapsible.description: Renders the toggle, an IconButton with icon sidebar, at the inline end of the header. A header is added when none is given.

toggleLabels.description: The toggle's accessible names. Under an Arabic Theme the defaults are طي القائمة الجانبية and توسيع القائمة الجانبية.

SidebarGroup.label.description: The visible heading and the name of the group's list.

SidebarGroup.collapsible.description: The heading becomes a ghost Button that opens and closes the group (Radix Collapsible). The group then stamps data-state open or closed.

SidebarGroup.open.description: Controlled open state of a collapsible group.

SidebarGroup.defaultOpen.description: Open at first render when uncontrolled.

SidebarGroup.onOpenChange.description: Called with the next open state.

SidebarItem.href.description: Where the item goes. Removed while disabled.

SidebarItem.start.description: The leading icon, a system icon name or a node. Give every item one if the sidebar can collapse.

SidebarItem.count.description: A number after the label. Over 99 shows 99+; 0 draws nothing.

SidebarItem.countLabel.description: What the count means, read instead of the bare number: 12 unread.

SidebarItem.active.description: The current page: aria-current page, data-active, bold weight, a fill and a bar on the inline start edge.

SidebarItem.disabled.description: Removes the href, sets role link, aria-disabled and data-disabled, and stays in the tab order. With asChild the plain anchor renders instead of the router child, so the child's own click never runs.

SidebarItem.asChild.description: Renders the single child element, a router link, as the item.

children.description: SidebarHeader, SidebarGroups and a SidebarFooter. The header and footer are direct children of Sidebar; everything else goes in the scrolling body. An item's children are its label.

a11y.role: navigation (nav with aria-label); each group is a list named by its heading; items are links
a11y.focus: Every item is a tab stop, disabled ones included. The ring is an inset 2px ring from color.focus.ring inside the row. A focused item scrolls into the body, never under the header or the footer.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next item, group trigger or the toggle
keys.Enter: Follows the item, or opens and closes a group from its trigger
keys.Space: Opens and closes a group from its trigger, and presses the toggle

a11y.announce: The current item says current page. The toggle is a button named for its next action (Collapse sidebar, Expand sidebar), with no aria-expanded: every link stays in place, only drawn smaller. A group trigger has aria-expanded. A count with countLabel reads as Inbox 12 unread.

native.accessibilityRole: link (each item; the container has no role)

notes: The current page is shown by aria-current, a bold weight, a fill and an edge bar, never by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).

Collapsed items keep the label in the DOM, visually hidden, so it stays the accessible name, and show a Tooltip with the label on hover and focus, at the inline end (WCAG 1.4.13). The hint repeats the name, so it is not wired as the description. The Tooltip is turned off while expanded and never remounts the item.

The groups scroll inside the body part; the header and the footer sit outside it, so nothing is drawn over an item and a focused item is never hidden (WCAG 2.4.11). The body has a small scroll padding so a focused item stops clear of its edge.

The border and the active bar are on logical sides, so the sidebar's edge flips in RTL; the sidebar icon of the toggle mirrors. A sidebar placed at the inline end swaps --_sidebar-border-start-color and --_sidebar-border-end-color.
Group headings and counts go one font step up in Arabic, like the item labels.
A collapsed sidebar holds collapsible groups open and hides their trigger; the group stays mounted, so focus inside it is kept.
No native title attribute. Hints come from Tooltip.

en.label: Nouns in sentence case: Inbox, Billing, Team members. One or two words.
en.group: A short noun for the group heading: Workspace, Projects.
en.count: A plain number. Pass countLabel when the number alone does not say what it counts.
en.toggle: Verb plus noun: Collapse sidebar, Expand sidebar.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: الوارد، الفواتير، أعضاء الفريق.
ar.group: A short noun: مساحة العمل، المشاريع.
ar.toggle: Noun form: طي القائمة الجانبية، توسيع القائمة الجانبية.

react.behavior: hand built nav, radix:Collapsible for groups, radix:Slot for asChild, Tooltip for collapsed items
react.note: fade-rise: an opened group's list fades in and rises one step from below; closing is instant. Reduced motion: no animation, the list shows at once. The width never animates, so collapse is instant. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed): nav-current-slide (the edge bar ::before slides along the column, labels dip and pop), nav-hover-follow (the hover veil ::after slides from the item the pointer left) and sidebar-collapse (the width changes at once; on expand the labels come in from the inline start after it with staggerGroup, on collapse the icons pop).

angular.behavior: nav[dsSidebar], cdk:accordion or a disclosure directive for groups

native.note: On phones the sidebar is a drawer; the collapsed form applies to tablets.

styles.studio: Flat surface with a hairline on the inline end edge. The active item takes an overlay fill, bright text, bold weight and a white bar.
styles.desk: The same layout. The active bar takes the yellow of color.primary.on-surface.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: The current page shown only by a different text color
mistakes.right: active, which adds aria-current, weight, a fill and an edge bar

mistakes.wrong: Items with no icon in a sidebar that can collapse
mistakes.right: start on every item, so the collapsed column still shows each destination

mistakes.wrong: A Sidebar of icon buttons with no labels
mistakes.right: Rail

mistakes.wrong: Hiding the label with display none when collapsed
mistakes.right: Collapsed keeps the label as the accessible name

mistakes.wrong: Buttons that save or delete inside the item list
mistakes.right: Items only navigate; actions go in the header or footer as Buttons

name: Skeleton
summary: A placeholder shape that stands where content will appear while it loads: a text line, a circle or a rectangle.
useWhen: Content with a known layout is loading, such as a card list, a profile or a table, and the wait is short
Keeping the layout still while data arrives, so nothing jumps when it lands
A first load of a section, before any content has been shown
avoidWhen: The layout of the coming content is not known
A short action the person started, such as saving a form
A long task with a known amount of progress
The load failed

variant.description: The form. Rendered as data-variant, not data-shape: shape words are fixed for controls.

size.description: Text only: the type size of the line it stands for (font.size.s, m, 2xl), with half the normal leading above and below so lines stack like text. Not stamped on circle and rect.

width.description: Inline size, a CSS length or px. Default the full line for text and rect, size.control.md (32px at the default density) for circle. Set through --_skeleton-width.

height.description: Rect only: the block size, a CSS length or px. Default size.control.lg. A circle takes its width.

a11y.role: None. Every skeleton is aria-hidden, whatever the caller passes.
a11y.focus: Not focusable. Holds no controls.
a11y.announce: The skeletons say nothing, so the consumer says it once per region. Keep one visually hidden role="status" element mounted next to the loading container (outside it, since aria-busy can hold back what is inside). Put the words in it when loading starts: Loading members, Arabic جار تحميل الأعضاء. Empty it when the content lands. The container carries aria-busy="true" while the skeletons show. Every case of Skeleton.demo.tsx shows the pattern.
notes: The shimmer plays three times (4.2s, linear, the skeleton-shimmer pattern) and stops, so it needs no pause control (WCAG 2.2.2). Under reduced motion it does not play; the shape stays.
Forced colors draws an outline in the system text color, since the fill is not painted.

en.busy: The container's name says what is loading: Members, Profile. No text inside a skeleton.

ar.busy: Noun form names on the container, no diacritics: الأعضاء، الملف الشخصي.

angular.behavior: span[dsSkeleton], host bindings
angular.note: The host element is the root, always aria-hidden. width and height set --_skeleton-width and --_skeleton-height as inline styles, numbers as px. Skeleton.css is used as is.

native.note: A View with the same fill; the shimmer through Reanimated, still under reduce motion.

styles.studio: Tokens only: an overlay-10 fill with a second overlay-10 band sweeping across.
styles.desk: Tokens only: the same overlays, so a skeleton on glass stays visible.
styles.neutral: Tokens only.

mistakes.wrong: A skeleton for a save the person just started
mistakes.right: Button with loading

mistakes.wrong: Skeletons in a container with no aria-busy
mistakes.right: aria-busy="true" on the loading container, removed when the content lands

mistakes.wrong: A skeleton left on screen after the load failed
mistakes.right: Swap it for an ErrorState with a retry action

mistakes.wrong: data-shape="circle"
mistakes.right: variant="circle", rendered as data-variant

name: SkipLink
summary: The first link of a page. Hidden until it takes keyboard focus, then Enter moves focus past the header and navigation to the main content.
useWhen: Every page that has a header, a navigation or other blocks repeated before its main content (WCAG 2.4.1)
A long region a keyboard user may want to jump past, such as a search panel or a footer, with one extra link per target
An app shell: PageShell renders it first
avoidWhen: Navigation between sections of the same article, which readers use with a pointer too
A link that must always be visible
A page with no repeated block before the main content

href.description: The fragment of the element to jump to. The target is found by id.

children.description: The visible text. Under an Arabic Theme the default is الانتقال للمحتوى الرئيسي.

a11y.role: link (native a with href)
a11y.focus: Placed first in body, it is the first tab stop of the page. Visually hidden at rest, drawn at the block start and inline start corner on focus, with a 2px ring from focus.shadow.ring on keyboard focus.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the skip link from the top of the page, which draws it
keys.Enter: Moves focus to the target and scrolls it into view

a11y.announce: The link text is the accessible name. After Enter, the screen reader reads the target from the start.
notes: WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass blocks.

The target gets tabindex -1 only when focus does not land on it as it is. A link, a button, a field or an element with its own tabindex keeps what it has; an anchor with no href or a disabled control gets tabindex -1.
Focus moves to the target itself, not only the scroll position, so the next Tab continues from the main content in every browser.

The URL fragment changes after focus moves, so hashchange and :target fire as for a plain fragment link. A click with a modifier key or a middle click is left to the browser. When the target is missing the browser handles the link.
Drawn on any focus, keyboard or pointer, so it never vanishes under the pointer that clicked it. At 24px or more tall when shown (WCAG 2.5.8).
Under forced colors it is drawn in LinkText on Canvas with a LinkText border, and the focus outline uses Highlight.
No native title attribute.

en.label: Skip to plus the place: Skip to main content, Skip to search. Sentence case.
en.many: One link per target, in the order the targets appear on the page.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: الانتقال للمحتوى الرئيسي، الانتقال للبحث.

react.behavior: native a, focus moved by hand
react.note: No motion: the link appears at once on focus, so there is no pattern to name and nothing to reduce. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction skip-link-slide: drawn at once with its ring on focus, it slides down from distance.enter above on the bouncy spring. Reduced motion: it appears in place.

angular.behavior: a[dsSkipLink], host bindings, a click handler that moves focus

native.note: Native screen readers move by headings and containers, and there is no tab order to bypass. Start the first content block with a heading (accessibilityRole header on its title) so screen reader users can jump to it.

styles.studio: A surface-3 pill with bright text, a control border and the menu shadow.
styles.desk: The same look from the Desk tokens, on a solid surface so it reads over any backdrop.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: A skip link with display none at rest
mistakes.right: SkipLink, which stays in the tab order and the accessibility tree while hidden

mistakes.wrong: A skip link that only scrolls, so the next Tab starts from the header again
mistakes.right: SkipLink, which moves focus to the target

mistakes.wrong: tabindex 0 on the main region so it can take focus
mistakes.right: Nothing: the skip link adds tabindex -1 when it is needed, which keeps the region out of the tab order

mistakes.wrong: A skip link placed after the navigation
mistakes.right: The first element in body

name: Slider
summary: One number on a range, picked by dragging a thumb or with the arrow keys.
useWhen: A value where the rough position matters more than the exact number: volume, opacity, zoom
A bounded number with a small step that people tune while watching the result
A setting with a few named stops, shown as marks
avoidWhen: An exact number that people know and want to type
A low and a high value, such as a price range
A choice among a few named options with no order between them

size.description: Track 2, 4 and 6 px thick, thumb 12, 16 and 24 px in a target of 24 px, 24 px and the lg control height.

tone.description: The range fill and the thumb: the primary color the style uses on a surface.

value.description: Controlled value. Pair with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: Uncontrolled starting value. Default min.

onValueChange.description: Called on every change, while dragging too.

onValueCommit.description: Called once when a drag ends or a key changes the value. Save here.

step.description: Arrows move one step; PageUp and PageDown move ten.

label.description: Visible name above the track. Names the thumb through aria-labelledby. Without it, pass aria-label.

showValue.description: Shows the formatted value at the end of the label row. Default true when there is a label.

unit.description: A unit after the number, in the value text and aria-valuetext: %, px, SAR.

formatOptions.description: Intl.NumberFormat options for the value text. Digits are always Western.

formatValue.description: Full control of the value text, aria-valuetext included.

marks.description: Ticks under the track: numbers, or { value, label } objects.

invalid.description: A danger tint on the track and aria-invalid on the thumb. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

disabled.description: Inside a Field it follows the Field.

rootProps.description: Props for the root element. className and style also go to the root.

a11y.role: slider, on the thumb (a Radix span), with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext.
a11y.focus: The thumb is the one tab stop. Focus shows the glow and a 2px ring around the drawn thumb.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the thumb, and on to the next control
keys.ArrowRight, ArrowUp: Raise the value by one step. In right to left text ArrowLeft raises it.
keys.ArrowLeft, ArrowDown: Lower the value by one step. In right to left text ArrowRight lowers it.
keys.PageUp, PageDown: Raise or lower the value by ten steps
keys.Shift+ArrowRight: Moves by ten steps, as PageUp
keys.Home, End: Move to the minimum or the maximum

a11y.announce: Name from the label (or aria-label), then aria-valuetext: the formatted value with its unit, such as 40%. The visible value is aria-hidden, so it is not read twice.
notes: Every drag has the key path above (WCAG 2.5.7).
