The thumb is a target of at least 24px at every size (the lg control height at lg): the drawn circle is its content box.
Values use Western digits in every language. formatSliderValue is a stand in until packages/shared/src/number.ts lands.
Marks are aria-hidden: they repeat what aria-valuetext says. A vertical slider shows no marks.
Rest props (name, min, max, step) go to the Radix slider root; the ref goes to the thumb.
Inside a Field with a label and no label of its own, the thumb is named by the Field label through aria-labelledby.
A label that is not a native label: the thumb is not a form element, so the label is tied with aria-labelledby.

en.label: A noun in sentence case: Opacity. The unit goes in unit, not in the label.
en.unit: A symbol or a short unit: %, px, SAR.
en.marks: Only the values people aim for. Not every step.

ar.label: اسم بدون تشكيل: الشفافية
ar.unit: الأرقام إنجليزية دايم، والوحدة بعد الرقم: 12,500 ريال

angular.behavior: div[dsSlider], keys and pointer hand built with the Radix Slider DOM and arithmetic, CDK Directionality, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root. Inputs take the React prop names; onValueChange is the valueChange output of [(value)] and onValueCommit the valueCommit output. aria-label, aria-labelledby and aria-describedby are inputs, as React sends them to the thumb. label and mark labels take text; formatValue is a function input. No CDK slider: the Radix DOM is copied, with the control dir and aria-disabled, the thumb wrapper and its inline position style, data-radix-collection-item on the thumb and a hidden input per thumb in a form. Arrows follow the reading direction of the nearest dsTheme through the CDK Directionality. Value text from formatNumber in packages/shared. Slider.css is used as is.

styles.studio: A thin overlay track, the range and thumb in the bright text color
styles.desk: The same track, the range and thumb in the yellow primary (a darker gold in Desk Light)

mistakes.wrong: A slider for an exact number such as a price
mistakes.right: A NumberField, or a Slider with a NumberField beside it

mistakes.wrong: aria-valuetext left out, so 40 is read with no unit
mistakes.right: The unit prop, which sets aria-valuetext

mistakes.wrong: Saving on every onValueChange while dragging
mistakes.right: Save in onValueCommit

mistakes.wrong: Two Sliders for a low and a high value
mistakes.right: A RangeSlider

name: Spinner
summary: A small turning ring that says something is busy and its length is unknown.
useWhen: A short wait of unknown length on a small area: a list row, a card, a field that checks a value
Next to visible text such as Loading files, as decorative
Inside a region that carries aria-busy, as decorative
avoidWhen: The task reports how far it is
The layout is known while content loads
An action button is busy
A wait longer than a few seconds with no visible text

size.description: Ring size: xs 12 (size.icon.sm), sm 16 (size.icon.md), md 24 (size.icon.lg), lg 36 px with a thicker stroke.

tone.description: neutral draws the arc in color.text.default, accent in color.primary.on-surface (the neutral fill in Studio, yellow in Desk dark, dark gold in Desk light).

label.description: The accessible name, read by a status region: Loading files. Required unless decorative (a TypeScript union enforces it). Never rendered as visible text.

decorative.description: Sets aria-hidden and drops the status role and the label. Use it when visible text or an aria-busy parent already says the area is busy.

a11y.role: status (with a label), or none and aria-hidden (decorative)
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: With a label, the root is a polite status region holding the visually hidden label. It is read when a screen reader reaches it and when the label changes; a region inserted with its text already in it is not announced by every reader. Decorative spinners say nothing. aria-hidden is ignored on the labelled form.
notes: Under reduced motion the ring stops and stays as a still ring with its arc; the label is still read.
Under forced colors the ring is GrayText with a CanvasText arc, so it does not collapse into one color.
Many spinners on one view: make them decorative and say the busy state once, in a region with aria-busy or in one status line.
The turn is clockwise in both directions: a spinner is a clock and does not mirror in RTL.
WCAG 2.2.2: a busy indicator is essential motion, but a wait longer than five seconds should show visible text or move to ProgressBar.

en.label: Name the work in progress, a present participle plus a noun: Loading files, Syncing boards. Not Please wait.
en.visible: When the wait is longer than a second or two, show the same words next to a decorative spinner.

ar.label: Noun form with جار: جار تحميل الملفات، جار مزامنة اللوحات. No diacritics.

react.note: Motion: the spinner pattern from the 1.11 catalog list, today a CSS rotate keyframe on duration.spin, none under reduced motion.

angular.behavior: span[dsSpinner], hand built, role status
angular.note: The host element is the root. Inputs take the React prop names. React types label and decorative as a union; Angular cannot, so a labelled spinner without a label warns in development. Spinner.css is used as is.

native.note: Expected on ActivityIndicator or a Reanimated rotation, still under reduce motion.

styles.studio: A 2px ring in overlay 20 with a text colored arc; accent uses the neutral fill of Studio, the same as neutral in effect.
styles.desk: The same ring; accent turns the arc yellow on dark and dark gold on light, from color.primary.on-surface.
styles.neutral: Planned: the same ring with the brand color for accent.
styles.liquid: Planned: the same ring.

mistakes.wrong: A spinner with role status next to visible text that says the same thing
mistakes.right: decorative on the spinner, the visible text carries the meaning

mistakes.wrong: Ten labelled spinners in a list, each announcing Loading
mistakes.right: Decorative spinners and one aria-busy region or one status line

mistakes.wrong: A spinner while an upload reports its percent
mistakes.right: A ProgressBar or a ProgressCircle with the value

mistakes.wrong: A Spinner placed inside a busy Button by hand
mistakes.right: Button with loading and loadingLabel

name: SplitButton
summary: A main action fused to a chevron trigger that opens a menu of related actions. Both halves share one size, tone, emphasis and shape and read as one control.
useWhen: One action people run most of the time, with a few variants of it: Publish page, with Schedule publish and Publish to staging in the menu
A primary action whose other forms would crowd the toolbar as separate buttons: Save changes, with Save as copy
A footer or toolbar where the default choice should take one click and the alternatives two
avoidWhen: The menu holds actions that are not variants of the main action, such as Delete next to Publish
There is no clear default: every action is used about as often
The control picks a value or a mode that stays selected
More than seven related actions
On touch first layouts where a 24px chevron is the only path to the variants

insteadUse.Several unrelated actions behind one but: DropdownMenu with a Button or IconButton trigger
insteadUse.More than seven related actions: DropdownMenu with labels and groups, or a CommandPalette

label.description: The visible text of the main action. English: a verb plus a noun in sentence case (Publish page). Arabic: a noun form (نشر الصفحة). It ends in an ellipsis when the control is squeezed.

menuLabel.description: The trigger's accessible name, set as aria-label; it also names the menu. Name the menu, never only More: More publish options.

children.description: The menu: one to seven DropdownMenuItems, the variants of the main action. Item props (start, shortcut, tone, disabled, onSelect) work as in DropdownMenu.

onClick.description: Runs the main action on click, Enter and Space on the action half. Not called while loading or disabled.

start.description: Leading content of the action: a system icon name or a node. It sits on the start side, so on the right in Arabic.

size.description: Both halves, from the size.control tokens: 24, 28, 32 and 44px at default density. The menu rows are sm for xs and sm, md for md and lg. Inside a ButtonGroup an unset size comes from the group.

tone.description: Both halves. accent with solid is the primary action of a view. The menu items keep their own tone.

emphasis.description: Both halves, as Button. No link: a link has no fill to split. The seam is color.border.default on soft and ghost, the outline border on outline, and the text color at 35 percent on solid.

shape.description: Both halves. Only the outer corners take the shape; the inner corners at the seam are square and flip in RTL.

loading.description: The main action is in flight: the action shows the spinner, sets aria-busy and data-loading, keeps its width and blocks activation. The trigger and its menu stay usable.

loadingLabel.description: The words the action's hidden status says while loading. Arabic: جار التحميل.

disabled.description: Blocks both halves. They stay focusable with aria-disabled and data-disabled, so a Tooltip can say why. Sets data-disabled on the root.

open.description: Controlled open state of the menu, with onOpenChange.

onOpenChange.description: Called with true when the menu opens and false when it closes (an item chosen, Escape, a click outside).

actionRef.description: The action button element, for moving focus to it.

a11y.role: No role on the root. The action is a button. The trigger is a menu button: a button with aria-haspopup menu, aria-expanded and data-state open or closed, named by menuLabel, and it names the menu (aria-labelledby). The menu is a DropdownMenu root, role menu, not modal.
a11y.focus: Two tab stops: the action, then the trigger. Opened with Enter, Space or ArrowDown on the trigger, focus goes to the first item; with ArrowUp, to the last item. Escape or choosing an item closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. Each half draws the focus ring inside its own box, so the other half never covers it. Disabled halves stay in the tab order.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the action, then to the trigger, then out
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus back from the trigger to the action
keys.Enter: On the action, runs the main action. On the trigger, opens the menu with focus on the first item
keys.ArrowDown: On the trigger, opens the menu with focus on the first item
keys.ArrowUp: On the trigger, opens the menu with focus on the last item
keys.Escape: With the menu open, closes it and returns focus to the trigger

a11y.announce: The action reads its label as a button. The trigger reads its name (More publish options), menu button and collapsed or expanded. While loading, the action is busy and its hidden status says the loading label.
notes: In the open menu the DropdownMenu keys apply: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move, Home and End, typeahead, Enter and Space select and close, and Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. Unit tests cover Escape here; the generic contract suite checks it on DropdownMenu, because the root it opens is a dropdown-menu, not a split-button.
The trigger's name names the menu (More publish options), never only More: a screen reader user hears it without the action next to it (WCAG 2.4.6).
Loading blocks the action only, so a long publish does not hide the other ways to publish.

When the menu is open the trigger's chevron turns to point up and the trigger takes its pressed fill where the fill has one, with aria-expanded true, so open is not told by color alone. Under reduced motion the chevron turns at once.
Both halves are at least 24 by 24 CSS px at every size (WCAG 2.5.8); the trigger is a square of the control height.
Under forced colors the system draws every border, so the seam stays visible, the focus outline is pulled inside each half, and the open trigger takes the system Highlight.

The menu is a DropdownMenu root portaled into a themed layer under body, carrying data-part menu. The contract suite cannot own a part outside the root's subtree, so menu is listed in contract.optionalParts.
In an attached ButtonGroup a SplitButton joins the row's seam on both sides. Horizontal groups only: it is a row control and is not placed in a vertical attached group.

Motion of round 3 (order 1.23, proposed, interactions split-chevron and segment-press): the chevron drops on hover (hover capable devices only) and further while the closed trigger is held, then flips half a turn on the snappy spring as the menu opens. The pressed half keeps its box: its parts dip, the action's parts sink and Button's inner shade comes in, so the seam never opens.

en.action: A verb plus a noun in sentence case: Publish page, Save changes. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes.
en.menuLabel: More plus what the menu holds: More publish options, More save options. Never only More.
en.items: Variants of the main action, each a verb plus a noun: Schedule publish, Publish to staging, Save as draft. The most used first.

ar.action: Noun form, no diacritics: نشر الصفحة، حفظ التغييرات. Never the imperative.
ar.menuLabel: Noun form that names the menu: خيارات النشر الأخرى.
ar.items: Noun form labels, no diacritics, Western digits: جدولة النشر، النشر للتجربة، الحفظ كمسودة.

react.behavior: Button plus radix:DropdownMenu (DropdownMenuTrigger around an IconButton)
react.note: The menu opens with menu-scale from the trigger side, aligned to the control's inline end; each half keeps Button's press, and the open trigger's chevron turns over (transform, quick duration, instant under reduced motion). The seam is drawn by SplitButton.css through Button's private corner properties. Inside a ButtonGroup, unset size, emphasis and shape come from the group.

angular.behavior: div[dsSplitButton] composed of dsButton, dsIconButton with dsDropdownMenuTrigger and dsDropdownMenuContent
angular.note: The menu items come in an ng-template dsSplitButtonMenu, not as projected content: they render in the menu layer and their DI must reach the menu, which the host provides. label is a string. onClick is the action output (a click output would also fire for clicks on the trigger, since the native click bubbles to the host). onOpenChange is the openChange output of [(open)]. actionRef has no input: read the action through the dsSplitButton exportAs or a query. SplitButton.css is used as is.

native.behavior: react-native:View with two Pressables and rn-primitives:dropdown-menu
native.note: The square inner corners through the style function, flipped by I18nManager. The trigger keeps a 44pt or 48dp hit area.

styles.studio: Overlay filled halves with the control radius on the outer corners; the seam is color.border.default over the fill. The primary form is the neutral primary fill. The menu is the Studio surface-3 menu.
styles.desk: Pill halves, so the control reads as one pill with a square seam; the action's label rolls on hover as on every Desk Button. The primary form is yellow with ink text and a faint ink seam. The menu is the Desk glass menu.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: A trigger named More or Options
mistakes.right: menuLabel names the menu: More publish options

mistakes.wrong: Delete board in the menu of a Publish page SplitButton
mistakes.right: Only variants of the main action in the menu; destructive and unrelated actions in a separate DropdownMenu

mistakes.wrong: A SplitButton whose main action only opens the menu
mistakes.right: A Button or IconButton as a DropdownMenuTrigger

mistakes.wrong: Twelve items in the menu
mistakes.right: At most seven; past that, a DropdownMenu with labels and groups

mistakes.wrong: Disabling the whole control while the main action runs
mistakes.right: loading on the action; the menu stays usable

mistakes.wrong: A Button and an IconButton placed side by side with hand drawn corners
mistakes.right: SplitButton, which squares the seam on the logical sides and wires the menu button

name: SplitView
summary: A list and its detail side by side with a resize handle, stacked one at a time with a back Button under breakpoint.tablet, as in a mail reader.
useWhen: A list whose items open a detail next to it: mail, messages, tickets, files
A master and detail layout that must work on phones as well as desktops
Settings with a list of sections and the chosen section beside it
avoidWhen: Three or more panes the person sizes freely, as in an editor
The detail is a short task that should block the page
The page frame itself, with header, sidebar and footer

primary.description: The list that opens the detail.

secondary.description: The detail of the chosen item, or an empty state that says what to choose.

showSecondary.description: Controlled: the detail is the pane shown while stacked. Set it to true when an item opens, with onShowSecondaryChange.

onShowSecondaryChange.description: Called with false by the back Button.

layout.description: auto: split when the root is at least breakpoint.tablet (48rem) wide, stacked below. The root's own width counts, not the window's. The first render, before the width is measured and on the server, is split. 48rem is read at 16px, as media queries do.

defaultSizes.description: Starting sizes of the two panes in percent. Pass the sizes saved from onLayout to restore them.

onLayout.description: Called with the settled sizes when a drag ends and after each key.

primaryLabel.description: The name of the list pane, a region. Under lang="ar" the default is القائمة. Name the list: Messages.

secondaryLabel.description: The name of the detail pane, a region. Under lang="ar" the default is التفاصيل. Name the detail: Message.

handleLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تغيير حجم القائمة.

backLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is الرجوع للقائمة. Name the list: Return to messages.

a11y.role: none on the root. The panes are regions, named by primaryLabel and secondaryLabel (List and Detail by default). The handle is a separator (the window splitter of ResizablePanels).
a11y.focus: While stacked, focus moves to the detail pane when it opens, and back returns it to the last element focused in the list (the item that opened the detail), else to the list pane. When the view narrows into stacked with focus in the pane that hides, focus moves to the pane that stays. While split, focus stays where the person put it.

keys.Tab: Moves through the list, the handle and the detail
keys.ArrowLeft, ArrowRight: On the handle, move it 5 percent left or right on screen. The list is on the right in Arabic.
keys.Home, End: On the handle, move it to the list's min and max
keys.Enter, Space: On the back Button, return to the list

a11y.announce: The detail pane's name when it takes focus while stacked.
notes: Both panes stay mounted while stacked; the hidden one has the hidden attribute, so the list keeps its scroll position.
The width is read from the root, so a SplitView inside a narrow window or panel stacks there too. No sideways scroll at 320px.
Every drag has a key path (WCAG 2.5.7), from ResizablePanels.
handle-grip is the grip of the shared handle; the order's anatomy did not list it.

en.back: A verb plus the list name: Return to messages.
en.empty: The detail pane without a choice says what to do: Choose a message from the list.

ar.back: Noun form, no diacritics: الرجوع للرسائل.
ar.empty: ما فيه رسالة مختارة. اختار رسالة من القائمة.

react.behavior: own: the ResizablePanels group (PanelGroup) and @the-system/shared resize

angular.behavior: own: the shared resize math, cdk:layout for the width
angular.note: SplitView.css and ResizablePanels.css are used as is.

native.behavior: a stack on phones, two panes on tablets
native.note: The stacked form maps to a navigation stack with the platform back gesture plus the back Button.

styles.studio: Flat panes split by the 1px control line of ResizablePanels; the back Button is a ghost Button.
styles.desk: The same, on the Desk tokens; inside a Window it fills the body.
styles.neutral: The same parts once 1.10 lands.
styles.liquid: Planned: the stacked form slides like a navigation stack.

mistakes.wrong: Hiding the list with CSS media queries and losing its scroll position
mistakes.right: SplitView keeps both panes mounted and hides one with the hidden attribute

mistakes.wrong: A back control that leaves focus at the top of the page
mistakes.right: SplitView returns focus to the list item that opened the detail

mistakes.wrong: Deciding the layout from the window width while the view sits in a narrow panel
mistakes.right: SplitView reads its own width

name: Stack
summary: Lays out children in one direction, a column or a row, with a gap from the space token scale.
useWhen: Children that sit one under the other with an even gap: form fields, cards in a column, a settings list
A row of controls or chips along the line, wrapping when it runs out of room
Pushing two groups to opposite ends of a row with justify between
avoidWhen: Items that must line up in columns and rows at the same time
Centering a page or capping its width
A gap that must be a pixel number outside the space scale
Space added only to separate two groups with a visible line

direction.description: block runs top to bottom (a column). inline runs along the line from the start side (a row), so it starts on the right in Arabic. Sets data-orientation vertical or horizontal.

gap.description: A space.* step. Fluid, and follows the density axis. Never a number.

align.description: Cross axis alignment (align-items). Logical words only: start is the right edge in a right to left row.

wrap.description: Lets children wrap onto more lines. Sets data-wrap.

as.description: The element to render. ul and ol lose their bullets and get role list, so Safari keeps the list semantics.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element as the Stack through Radix Slot. Wins over as. A ul or ol child loses its bullets, so give it role list yourself.

children.description: The items to lay out.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div by default, the semantics of as or the asChild element otherwise; list on ul and ol
a11y.focus: Never focusable. Focus order is DOM order, which is also the visual order: no reverse directions.
a11y.announce: Nothing. A Stack is layout only.
notes: There is no row-reverse or column-reverse. Reversing the visual order would break the reading and focus order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
Inline direction follows dir: the first child sits on the right in Arabic with no extra prop.

en.items: No copy of its own. Children carry their own labels.

ar.items: No copy of its own. The row starts on the right in Arabic because the words are logical.

react.behavior: hand built flex box, radix:Slot for asChild
react.note: No motion: a static layout has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies.

angular.behavior: [dsStack] attribute directive on any element
angular.note: The host element is the root, so as and asChild are not needed: put the directive on a ul, nav or section.

native.note: direction inline maps to row, which I18nManager flips in right to left. Gap from the generated space values.

styles.studio: Layout only. The gap scale follows density.
styles.desk: Layout only. The gap scale follows density.
styles.neutral: Layout only. The gap scale follows density.
styles.liquid: Layout only. The gap scale follows density.

mistakes.wrong: direction row with a margin-left on each child
mistakes.right: direction inline with a gap step, which works in both reading directions

mistakes.wrong: A gap of 12 as a number
mistakes.right: gap l (12px in the default density on a wide screen), a space step that follows density

mistakes.wrong: A Stack used to make a two dimension card grid with nested rows
mistakes.right: Grid with columns or auto-fit

mistakes.wrong: Reversing the order with CSS so the last child shows first
mistakes.right: Change the order in the markup, so reading and focus order match

name: Stat
summary: One number with its label, its change since the last period and a short hint: a KPI.
useWhen: A dashboard row of key numbers: active users, revenue, failed payments
One headline number at the top of a report or a detail page, with how it moved
A count that people compare with a target or the last period
avoidWhen: Many numbers people compare row by row
A trend over time that people read point by point
A number that is a setting people change
A small count on a nav item or a tab

insteadUse.A trend over time: a chart (wave 3), with Stat above it for the latest value

label.description: What the number counts, in sentence case: Active users.

value.description: A number is formatted with Intl in the Theme language with Western digits and the format options. A node (No data) is drawn as is.

format.description: Intl.NumberFormat options for a numeric value: currency, unit, compact notation.

delta.description: The change since the last period. A number sets the trend from its sign and is drawn as its absolute value with deltaFormat (0.12 is 12%). A change that rounds to zero in that format is flat. A delta that is not a finite number is not drawn. A node is drawn as is and needs trend.

deltaFormat.description: Intl.NumberFormat options for a numeric delta.

trend.description: Default from the sign of a numeric delta. Sets data-trend on the root (up, down or flat) and the arrow icon.

tone.description: The color of the change. Default success when up, danger when down, neutral when flat. Set it when down is good: costs, errors, churn. Only stamped when there is a change.

hint.description: A short line under the value: Since last month.

icon.description: A system icon name or a node at the end of the label line. Decorative, hidden from assistive tech.

size.description: The size of the value: font.size 2xl, 4xl and 6xl.

loading.description: Draws a placeholder block for the value, sets aria-busy and data-loading, hides the change.

loadingLabel.description: What screen readers hear while loading. جار التحميل under an Arabic Theme.

emptyLabel.description: What the value says when there is none to show: undefined, null, NaN or an infinite number. لا توجد بيانات under an Arabic Theme. Sets data-empty.

trendLabels.description: Overrides the trend words: { up, down, flat }. Default Up, Down, No change, or ارتفاع، انخفاض، بدون تغيير.

a11y.role: None: a div with text. Read in order: label, value, change, hint.
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: The change is read with its trend word first: Up 12%. Value changes are not announced, so a page of refreshing KPIs stays quiet. While loading, aria-busy is set and the value says loadingLabel. With no value, or a value that is not a finite number, the value says emptyLabel (No data) instead of NaN or the infinity sign.
notes: The trend is never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): an arrow or a bar icon draws it and a visually hidden word says it.
data-trend on the root carries up, down or flat: a valued state, listed in states as data-trend=up|down|flat so the contract suite checks its values.
Numbers use tabular figures, so a refreshing value does not shift its neighbours.
Under forced colors the loading block keeps a CanvasText border.
The trend icons (trend-up, trend-down) do not mirror in right to left layouts, like chart glyphs; the trend word carries the meaning.

en.label: A noun phrase in sentence case: Active users, Revenue this month. No colon.
en.hint: Say what the change compares with: Since last month.
en.empty: No data, with a hint that says when it will show.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: المستخدمين النشطين، الإيرادات.
ar.digits: Western digits, through Intl with the latn numbering system. Currency SAR shows ر.س.

react.note: stat-roll (order 1.22): the drawn number is aria-hidden and rolls digit by digit with the digit-roll primitive when a numeric value changes after the first paint, the trend mark nudges the same way, and a visually hidden copy carries the number; at most three rolls a second; a fade of the new digits under reduced motion. Numbers go through a private formatStatNumber until packages/shared/src/number.ts (order 1.2.5) lands.

angular.behavior: [dsStat], hand built

native.note: Same props; number-roll through Reanimated in wave 2.

styles.studio: Bright value on the black body, muted label and hint; the change in the state text colors.
styles.desk: Same layout in Instrument Sans with display tracking on the value.
styles.neutral: Same layout on the Neutral tokens; no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: A green number with no arrow or word
mistakes.right: delta with its trend: the icon and the hidden word say up or down

mistakes.wrong: Errors went down, shown in red
mistakes.right: tone success on a metric where down is good

mistakes.wrong: A preformatted string like 48.2K for a number
mistakes.right: value as a number with format { notation: 'compact' }, so the language sets the digits

mistakes.wrong: A live region around a refreshing KPI
mistakes.right: No announcement; the page announces a change people asked for

name: StatusDot
summary: A small colored dot with the state in words next to it: Online, Sync failed, Syncing.
useWhen: The live state of a person, a service or a device, next to its name
A row in a list or table that needs its state at a glance, with the words in the label
A state that is going on now, such as syncing or recording, with pulse
avoidWhen: The state is the only thing on the line and needs a filled shape to read as a tag
A count of unread or new items
A message that explains what happened or what to do
The dot would be the only sign of the state, with no words anywhere

label.description: The state in words. Always rendered: visible, or visually hidden with hideLabel.

tone.description: The dot color, from the state border tokens (3:1 against body, surface and surface-2). accent takes color.primary.border.

size.description: md is an 8px dot with font.size.m text, sm a 6px dot with font.size.s. Fixed sizes: density does not change the dot.

pulse.description: A ring grows from the dot and fades, three times, then stops (under five seconds, WCAG 2.2.2). Only for a live state. Sets data-pulse.

hideLabel.description: Hides the label visually and keeps it for screen readers. Only where visible text nearby already names the same state, such as a group heading Online now; otherwise the dot would be color alone. Sets data-hide-label.

a11y.role: None: a span with the label as text. The dot is aria-hidden.
a11y.focus: Not focusable.
a11y.announce: Not announced. The label is read in reading order. A consumer that changes the state live and needs it read puts role status on the root or on a parent.
notes: Never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the label is required.
The dot is a non text mark at 3:1 against the surfaces it sits on (WCAG 1.4.11).
The pulse plays three times and stops; it does not restart on a re-render. The label carries the live state after that.

en.label: One to three words, sentence case, the state not the color: Online, Sync failed, Waiting for review.

ar.label: Noun or adjective forms, no diacritics: متصل، فشل المزامنة، في الانتظار.

react.note: Motion: no catalog pattern. The pulse (a ring that grows and fades, three times) is a keyframe in StatusDot.css until the catalog has a pulse pattern (a request to the motion owner); thinking is three bouncing dots, not this.

angular.behavior: span[dsStatusDot], host bindings
angular.note: The host element is the root. label takes a string or a TemplateRef. StatusDot.css is used as is.

native.note: A View dot and a Text label; the pulse through Reanimated, off under reduce motion.

styles.studio: Tokens only: state colors on a flat surface.
styles.desk: Tokens only: the same dot; accent is the yellow primary border.
styles.neutral: Tokens only.

mistakes.wrong: A green dot with no words
mistakes.right: A green dot with the label Online, or hideLabel with the label still set

mistakes.wrong: pulse on every dot in a list
mistakes.right: pulse only on a state that is going on now, such as Syncing

mistakes.wrong: Naming the color: Green
mistakes.right: Naming the state: Online

mistakes.wrong: hideLabel in a mixed list where only the color tells states apart
mistakes.right: Visible labels, or group the rows under headings that name the state

name: Stepper
summary: Shows the steps of a process in order, which are complete, which one is current and which are still to come.
useWhen: A task split into three to seven ordered steps, such as a checkout, an onboarding or a setup
The user needs to see how far they are and what is left
The user may go back to an earlier step, or jump between steps in free mode
avoidWhen: Views of the same content that have no order (use tabs)
Progress of a single running task with a percentage
A process of one or two steps, where a heading is enough
The main navigation of an app

steps.description: One entry per step: title (a short noun), description (one line), invalid, disabled, href, id.

current.description: The index of the current step, from 0. Controlled. Without it the stepper keeps its own, starting at defaultCurrent.

defaultCurrent.description: The first current step when current is not passed.

completed.description: Indexes of the complete steps. Default every step before the furthest step reached, so going back keeps them complete.

mode.description: linear: earlier steps can be reached, a later step only when every step before it is complete. free: any step that is not disabled. The rule lives in packages/shared/src/stepper.ts.

onStepSelect.description: Called when the user picks a step. When it is passed, or a step has href, every step the user may reach, other than the current one, renders its title as a system Button.

orientation.description: Sets data-orientation. A horizontal stepper takes the vertical layout under breakpoint.phone (30rem), so it never scrolls sideways.

size.description: md: a 32px indicator (size.control.sm) and text s. sm: a 24px indicator (size.icon.lg) and text xs.

labels.description: The list name and the hidden state words. Defaults: Steps, current step, complete, has errors, unavailable; under an Arabic Theme الخطوات، الخطوة الحالية، مكتملة، فيها أخطاء، غير متاحة.

aria-label.description: The name of the list. Name the process: Checkout steps.

a11y.role: list (an ol), each step a listitem; a step the user may reach holds a button or a link
a11y.focus: Only steps the user may reach are tab stops, each a system Button with the focus ring from focus.shadow.ring. Static steps and the current step are not focusable.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next step the user may reach
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus to the previous step the user may reach
keys.Enter: Goes to the focused step
keys.Space: Goes to the focused step when it is a button

a11y.announce: The list name, then each step with its position from the list (2 of 4), its title and hidden words: current step, complete, has errors, unavailable. The current step also carries aria-current="step".
notes: Complete shows a check and invalid shows a danger glyph, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The indicator is hidden from assistive tech; the hidden status words carry the state.
The step number is not read from the indicator: the ordered list gives the position.
The connector fill starts at the inline start, so it grows from the right in RTL.
Under forced colors the indicator border takes CanvasText, the current step Highlight, and the connector stays a border.
No native title attribute. Hints come from Tooltip.
React Native has no current state: the current step says current step in its accessibilityLabel.

en.title: A short noun in sentence case: Account, Address, Payment, Review. Not a verb, not a sentence.
en.description: One line that says what the step asks for: Email and password.
en.count: Three to seven steps. More than seven: group them, or use the vertical form.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics: الحساب، العنوان، الدفع، المراجعة.
ar.description: One short line in white Saudi dialect.

react.behavior: hand built ol; state from packages/shared/src/stepper.ts; reachable steps are system Buttons (asChild for links)
react.note: Motion tab-indicator: the connector fill scales from the start side when a step completes; under reduced motion it swaps at once. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction stepper-travel: a ring on the indicator's ::after, drawn only while it travels, slides from the old current indicator to the new one (internal/indicator.ts, ghost form), the new indicator pops, and the connector fill moves on the soft spring.

angular.behavior: ol[dsStepper] host bindings, state from packages/shared/src/stepper.ts, reachable steps as button[dsButton] or a[dsButton]
angular.note: onStepSelect is a function input: steps become actions only when it is set, as in React. Step title and description take a string or a TemplateRef. Stepper.css is used as is.

native.behavior: react-native:View list with Pressable steps, state from packages/shared/src/stepper.ts
native.note: Vertical on phones; the connector is a View.

styles.studio: Neutral: a complete step is the neutral fill with a check, the current step a bright ring, the filled connector bright on a dim track.
styles.desk: The yellow family: a complete step is the yellow fill with ink, the current step a yellow ring, the filled connector yellow.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: Complete told apart from upcoming by color only
mistakes.right: Stepper, which draws a check and says complete in hidden words

mistakes.wrong: A Stepper used as tabs for views with no order
mistakes.right: Tabs

mistakes.wrong: Step titles that are actions: Enter your address
mistakes.right: Nouns: Address

mistakes.wrong: Twelve steps in a horizontal row on a wide screen
mistakes.right: Group the steps, or use orientation vertical

mistakes.wrong: Every step clickable in a process where later steps need earlier data
mistakes.right: mode linear, the default, which opens a later step only when the ones before it are complete

name: Surface
summary: A plain background box on one surface step (body, surface 1 to 5), with an optional border, elevation, radius and padding.
useWhen: A region needs its own background step to separate it from the page, such as a sidebar fill or a summary box
Building a larger component (a tile, a panel body) that should take its fill from the surface tokens
Nesting boxes so each one sits one surface step above its parent
avoidWhen: The whole box is clickable or selectable
The box has a title, media and actions in a fixed layout
Only space is needed, with no fill or edge
A floating layer above the page, such as a menu or a popover

level.description: The surface step: body is color.bg.body, 1 is color.bg.surface, 2 to 5 are color.bg.surface-2 to -5. React takes the numbers 1 to 5 or the same digits as strings. Stamped as data-level.

bordered.description: A 1px border in color.border.default. Stamped as data-bordered.

elevation.description: Shadow from elevation.card or elevation.panel. Stamped as data-elevation.

radius.description: A radius token name. Stamped as data-radius. No pill: a block box would clip its text into the round ends.

padding.description: Inner space on every side, a space token step. Stamped as data-padding.

as.description: The element. Pick the one that says what the box is.

a11y.role: No role of its own: the native role of the element given by as (a div by default, no role). A section or aside with an accessible name becomes a landmark.
a11y.focus: Not focusable. Controls inside keep their own order.
a11y.announce: Nothing of its own. The content is read in document order.
notes: Text inside reads color.text.default, which the contrast gate checks against every surface step. Muted, dim and subtle text are checked only up to surface 3 (subtle up to surface 2): on levels 4 and 5 use default or bright text.

The border is always 1px and transparent at rest, so in forced colors mode the system draws it and the box keeps an edge without its fill or shadow. The cost: padding none still insets the content by that 1px.

en.body: Any content. The surface adds no copy of its own.

ar.body: Any content. The surface mirrors with the page through logical properties.

react.note: No motion: a static box has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies. A Surface that appears or moves gets its motion from the parent that shows it.

angular.behavior: [dsSurface] attribute directive on any element
angular.note: Stamps the same data attributes; Surface.css is used as is.

native.behavior: View with the surface, border, radius and shadow from the theme object
native.note: Elevation maps to the platform shadow or Android elevation.

styles.studio: Flat: six achromatic steps from black, no shadow. elevation card draws nothing here (the token is a zero shadow), so separate boxes by the step or a border, not by elevation.
styles.desk: The same steps on the black desk. elevation card draws nothing here (a zero shadow); elevation panel reads the deep Desk shadow.
styles.neutral: White and soft gray steps, light first. Small soft shadows for elevation.
styles.liquid: Content surfaces stay solid. A Surface is never glass: glass is for the control and navigation layer only.

mistakes.wrong: A Surface with an onClick handler as a clickable tile
mistakes.right: A Card, which has the button or link semantics, focus ring and hover

mistakes.wrong: A raw background color in a style prop to get a lighter box
mistakes.right: The level prop, one step above the parent

mistakes.wrong: Elevation on every box in Studio to separate them
mistakes.right: Studio is flat: a surface step, or the 1px gap of a Bento

mistakes.wrong: Making a Surface translucent in Liquid
mistakes.right: Content stays solid; glass belongs to bars, sheets and menus

mistakes.wrong: Muted or subtle text on a level 4 or 5 surface
mistakes.right: Default or bright text there; the contrast gate checks the quieter text colors only on the lower steps

mistakes.wrong: Elevated boxes packed edge to edge, each shadow painting over its neighbour
mistakes.right: A gap of at least space.xl between elevated siblings

name: Switch
summary: An on or off setting that takes effect the moment it changes.
useWhen: A setting that applies at once, with no save button, such as dark mode or auto save
A list of preferences where each row turns one feature on or off
Turning a service or a sync on or off where the result shows right away
avoidWhen: A value in a form that is saved later with a submit button
Several choices under one question
An action that runs once, such as sending or deleting

size.description: Track of 16, 24 and 32 px high, 1.75 times as wide, in a target of 24 px, 24 px and the lg control height (40 to 48 px by density).

tone.description: The track fill while on: the primary fill of the style.

onCheckedChange.description: Called with the new state. Apply the setting here, at once. Never called while read only.

label.description: Visible text after the switch, a native label bound to the control. Without it, pass aria-label.

description.description: A hint under the label. Joins aria-describedby.

stateText.description: { on, off }: words shown after the label for the current state, such as On and Off. Hidden from assistive tech.

thumbIcon.description: Renders the thumb-icon part: a check while on, a cross while off. Hidden unless a style or a platform shows it (--_switch-thumb-icon-opacity). Hidden from assistive tech.

name.description: The form name, when the switch sits in a form.

invalid.description: Danger border and aria-invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

disabled.description: Native disabled on the control. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: Keeps the value and focus, ignores clicks, Space and Enter, sets aria-readonly.

required.description: Sets aria-required. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

rootProps.description: Props for the root element. className and style also go to the root; the ref and every other prop go to the control.

a11y.role: switch, on the control (a Radix button). aria-checked is true or false.
a11y.focus: The control is the one tab stop. Focus shows the glow and a 2px ring around the track.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the control, and on to the next control
keys.Enter: Toggles the switch
keys.Pointer drag: Drags the thumb; on release it snaps by velocity, else to the nearer end. A tap toggles.

a11y.announce: Name from the label (or aria-label), the state as on or off, the description through aria-describedby. The state text is hidden, so it is not read twice.
notes: The anatomy adds a control part to the order's list: the 24px target that holds the track, so a 16px track still meets WCAG 2.5.8.
On: the thumb moves to the inline end and the track fills. Two signals, so the state never relies on color alone. In right to left text the thumb moves to the left.
Read only is not part of Radix: clicks are prevented, aria-readonly is set and the track draws dashed.
A switch applies its setting at once. If the change fails, set it back and say why in a Toast.

Motion, round 3 (switch-stretch and switch-drag, proposed): the thumb leans on hover, grows and stretches while pressed and travels on the bouncy spring; the on fill sweeps behind it with a clip that rides the thumb, so the track under the thumb is filled on every frame. A drag moves the thumb with the pointer (data-dragging) and snaps on release; the click that ends a drag toggles nothing; Space and Enter still toggle. Reduced motion: the thumb jumps and the fill shows at once.

The thumb-lens part is an aria-hidden layer inside the thumb. A style makes a glass thumb with --_switch-thumb-backdrop, --_switch-thumb-highlight and --_switch-thumb-solid-pressed, or a growing dot with --_switch-thumb-size-rest, -on and -pressed (transform only). The glass falls back to a solid thumb without backdrop-filter, under reduced transparency and under more contrast.

en.label: The name of the setting, a noun in sentence case: Auto save. Never a question, never On or Off in the label.
en.stateText: On and Off, or a pair that fits the setting: Visible and Hidden.
en.description: What changes when it is on, in one sentence.

ar.label: اسم الإعداد بصيغة الاسم، بدون تشكيل: الحفظ التلقائي

angular.behavior: div[dsSwitch], hand built on a native button with the Radix Switch DOM, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root. Inputs take the React prop names; onCheckedChange is the checkedChange output of [(checked)]. stateText takes { on, off } text. aria-label, aria-labelledby and aria-describedby are inputs, as React spreads them on the control. Behavior by hand with the Radix DOM: Space and Enter toggle, read only keeps the value and focus, a hidden native checkbox inside a form. Works with reactive and template forms. Switch.css is used as is.

styles.studio: Achromatic: a bordered pill with a muted thumb while off, a quiet overlay fill and a bright thumb while on
styles.desk: The same pill. On fills with the yellow primary and a dark thumb.

mistakes.wrong: A switch in a form that only applies after Save
mistakes.right: A Checkbox

mistakes.wrong: A label that says On or Off, or changes with the state
mistakes.right: A fixed setting name as the label, and stateText for the words

mistakes.wrong: Color alone shows the state
mistakes.right: The thumb side and the track fill, which this component draws

mistakes.wrong: A switch that runs a one time action, such as Send report
mistakes.right: A Button

name: TabBar
summary: The bottom bar of three to five top level destinations on phone layouts: an icon over a label for each, the current one marked.
useWhen: Three to five top level destinations of an app on a phone width layout
Destinations a person moves between often and wants one thumb tap away
A web app that replaces its Sidebar or Rail with a bottom bar under breakpoint.tablet
avoidWhen: Switching panels of content inside one page
More than five destinations, or only two
Actions such as Add or Share
Desktop width layouts

insteadUse.More than five destinations: Sidebar in a Drawer, or a More destination page

aria-label.description: TabBar: required unless aria-labelledby is set. Names the landmark: Main.

size.description: TabBar: md items are at least size.control.md (32px) with 16px icons; lg items are at least 44px (size.control.lg, never under size.touch-ios) with 24px icons, for touch layouts.

label.description: TabBarItem: the visible name, a short noun. Always shown; a long one ends in an ellipsis and stays whole in the link name.

icon.description: TabBarItem: a system icon name. Decorative.

active.description: TabBarItem: the current destination. Sets aria-current page and data-active: a bolder label and a pill behind the icon.

badge.description: TabBarItem: a count (99+ past 99, Western digits) or true for a dot. 0 and false show nothing. Its words join the link name.

badgeLabel.description: TabBarItem: the words the badge adds to the name: Inbox, 3 new. A dot says New. Arabic: جديد.

asChild.description: TabBarItem: renders its one child element (a router link) as the item.

a11y.role: navigation (the nav landmark) with a name; each item is a link, the current one with aria-current page.
a11y.focus: Every item is a tab stop, in reading order.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next item
keys.Enter: Follows the link

a11y.announce: Each link reads its label, its badge words (Inbox, 3 new) and current page for the active one.
notes: The current item is marked by aria-current, a bolder label and a pill behind its icon, never by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
Labels are always visible; icons are decorative.
The bar pads its block end by env(safe-area-inset-bottom) and its sides by the side insets.
A bar fixed to the bottom of the viewport covers content unless the page keeps the same room at its end (WCAG 2.4.11): the layout (PageShell) reserves it.
lg gives 44px targets for touch layouts (WCAG 2.5.8 and the touch template rule); md items are at least 32px.
No native title attribute; a cut label keeps its full text in the link name.
env(safe-area-inset-*) is 0 unless the page sets viewport-fit=cover in its viewport meta tag.

en.label: One short noun, sentence case: Home, Search, Inbox. No verbs.
en.landmark: Name it after the app section, never the same name as another nav on the page.

ar.label: Noun form labels, white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: الرئيسية، البحث، الوارد.
ar.badge: Western digits; the badge words read جديد.

react.note: No motion of its own: the current item's colors swap at once. fade-rise is the pattern a layout uses if it reveals the bar. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction tab-bar-pop: when an item becomes current its icon and pill pop from scale.anticipate past rest and its label rises a stagger step later (CSS keyframes that start with data-active). Reduced motion: nothing moves.

angular.behavior: hand built

native.behavior: react-navigation bottom tabs or a hand built bar
native.note: 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android; safe area from react-native-safe-area-context.

styles.studio: A surface-2 bar with a subtle top hairline, muted labels, the current item bright and bold with an overlay-20 pill behind its icon.
styles.desk: The same parts on Desk tokens: the Desk surface and type.
styles.neutral: Token driven; applies once the Neutral pack is merged.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass bar.

mistakes.wrong: Icons with no labels
mistakes.right: A short visible label on every item

mistakes.wrong: Six or seven destinations squeezed into the bar
mistakes.right: Five at most; the rest go on a More page or in a Drawer

mistakes.wrong: A TabBar that switches panels inside a page
mistakes.right: Tabs

mistakes.wrong: The current item shown only by color
mistakes.right: active: aria-current, weight and the icon pill

mistakes.wrong: A fixed bar over the last line of the page
mistakes.right: Reserve the bar's height at the end of the page

mistakes.wrong: A bottom bar on a phone page without viewport-fit=cover
mistakes.right: Set viewport-fit=cover so the safe area padding applies

name: TableOfContents
summary: Links to the headings of a long page, nested by level, with the section in view marked as the reader scrolls.
useWhen: A long document, guide or settings page with four or more sections a reader may jump between
A docs page with a side column that can hold a sticky list of its sections
A page where readers need to see which section they are in while they scroll
avoidWhen: A short page with one or two sections
Switching between separate views or pages, rather than sections of one page
Navigation of the whole site or app

items.description: The headings of the page in document order: { id, label, level }. They nest by level through buildTree in @the-system/shared; a skipped level nests one step down.

title.description: The visible title, a p that names the nav through aria-labelledby. Under an Arabic Theme the default is محتوى الصفحة. false hides it; then pass aria-label.

size.description: Type size: sm is font.size.xs, md font.size.s, one step up in Arabic. Every link is at least 24px tall.

offset.description: The height of a sticky header above the content, in px. A heading counts as reached when its top passes this line plus a fifth of the viewport, at most 64px (the reading line). A jump from a link also keeps the heading below it: a heading with no scroll-margin-block-start of its own gets one of this height inline.

sticky.description: Keeps the list in view as the page scrolls (position sticky, below offset plus space.l), scrolls inside when taller than dialog.height.max, and keeps the active link in view inside the list without scrolling the page. Sets data-sticky.

active.description: The active heading id, controlled. Default: tracked from the scroll position.

onActiveChange.description: Called when the active heading changes, from scrolling or a link.

a11y.role: navigation landmark named by its title, with ordered lists of links
a11y.focus: Each link is a tab stop. Enter or a click moves focus to the heading itself (tabindex -1 only when the heading is not focusable), so the next Tab continues from that section. A 2px ring from focus.shadow.ring.

keys.Tab: Moves through the links
keys.Enter: Scrolls to the heading and moves focus to it

a11y.announce: Navigation, On this page, list. The link of the section in view reads as current location (aria-current location). The indicator is aria-hidden.
notes: The section in view is marked by medium weight, the indicator bar and aria-current location, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
Items carry data-level (1, 2, 3 and deeper) for their nesting depth, which sets the indent. It is not listed under states because it holds a number, not an empty boolean.

Scrolling is smooth, and a jump under prefers-reduced-motion. The URL fragment is set with history.pushState, so there is no second jump; hashchange does not fire and :target does not update. While the scroll plays, sections passed on the way are not marked; scrollend lifts the hold.
A click with a modifier key or a middle click is left to the browser.

The active section comes from activeHeading in @the-system/shared at the reading line (offset plus a fifth of the viewport, at most 64px). An IntersectionObserver on that line and the scrollend event trigger a new measure, once per frame at most; nothing runs on every scroll event. A ResizeObserver keeps the indicator on its link when the list reflows.

Sticky form (WCAG 2.4.11): the list sits below offset plus space.l and keeps scroll padding around the active link. Pass the height of any sticky page header as offset: a jump then sets scroll-margin-block-start to that height inline on a heading that has none of its own, so a heading never lands under the header. A scroll margin set by the page is kept.
Under forced colors the indicator uses Highlight and the focus outline uses Highlight.

On load, the section named by the URL fragment is marked first, when there is one, and held until the reader scrolls, so the first measure does not move the mark. A malformed fragment such as #50% is read as written and never throws.
With no headings the component renders nothing: no landmark that holds only its title.

en.title: On this page, or a title that names the document: In this guide.
en.labels: The heading text as written on the page, sentence case. Shorten only when the heading is longer than a line.

ar.title: محتوى الصفحة, noun form, no diacritics.
ar.labels: The heading text as on the page. Each link text has dir auto, so a Latin term or name keeps its own direction.

react.behavior: nav with ol of anchors; IntersectionObserver in an effect; buildTree and activeHeading from @the-system/shared
react.note: The indicator moves with a transform transition (tab-indicator); under reduced motion the duration is 0ms and the scroll is a jump. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction toc-travel: the bar moves on the snappy spring (CSS) and stretches along its travel from its trailing edge (a WAAPI stretch added to the transition).

angular.behavior: nav[dsTableOfContents] with the shared buildTree and activeHeading, IntersectionObserver in afterNextRender

native.note: A list of pressables that scroll a ScrollView to measured section offsets with scrollTo; onScroll feeds activeHeading.

styles.studio: A hairline rail at the inline start, muted links that brighten on hover, a bright bar beside the section in view.
styles.desk: The same from the Desk tokens.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: The section in view marked by color only
mistakes.right: TableOfContents, which adds weight, the bar and aria-current location

mistakes.wrong: Links that only scroll, so the next Tab starts from the list again
mistakes.right: TableOfContents, which moves focus to the heading

mistakes.wrong: A scroll listener that measures every heading on every frame
mistakes.right: The IntersectionObserver in TableOfContents and activeHeading

mistakes.wrong: Headings that land under a sticky header after a jump
mistakes.right: The height of the sticky header passed as offset, so the jump keeps the heading below it

name: Tabs
summary: Switches between panels of related content in place. A labelled list of tabs, one active at a time, with its panel below or beside it.
useWhen: Two to eight panels of related content that a reader looks at one at a time, such as the settings of one board
Views of the same object that share one place on the page: General, Members, History
A small set of panels inside a dialog, a card or an inspector
avoidWhen: Moving between pages of a site or sections of an app
Content the reader needs to compare side by side
Steps that must be done in order
Choosing a value or a mode for a form or a canvas
Bottom navigation on a phone

insteadUse.Content compared side by side: Show it on the page, or use an Accordion

value.description: Tabs: controlled value, the value of the active tab, with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: Tabs: the active tab at first when uncontrolled. Required when value is not set, so a panel always shows on load.

onValueChange.description: Tabs: called with the value of the tab that becomes active.

size.description: Tabs: trigger height and type size. sm follows size.control.sm (28px at default density), md size.control.md (32px).

emphasis.description: Tabs: ghost draws a 2px line under the active tab on the list hairline; soft draws a filled pill behind it on a quiet track.

orientation.description: Tabs: horizontal puts the list above the panels; vertical puts it in a column at the inline start, and the up and down arrows move.

activationMode.description: Tabs: automatic shows a panel as soon as an arrow key reaches its tab. manual moves focus only; Enter or Space shows the panel. Use manual when a panel is slow to load.

loop.description: TabsList: the arrow keys wrap from the last tab to the first.

aria-label.description: TabsList: required unless aria-labelledby names a visible heading. Names the set: Board settings.

TabsTrigger.value.description: The value the tab shows; equal to one TabsPanel value.

start.description: TabsTrigger: a leading system icon name or node, decorative. The label still names the tab.

count.description: TabsTrigger: a number after the label, in a small pill, read with the name (Comments 12). Western digits.

disabled.description: TabsTrigger: cannot be chosen and is skipped by the arrow keys. Drawn with opacity.disabled.

forceMount.description: TabsPanel: keeps an inactive panel mounted and hidden, so its state survives a switch.

a11y.role: tablist on the list, with a name; tab on each trigger (aria-selected, aria-controls); tabpanel on each panel (aria-labelledby the tab).
a11y.focus: One tab stop for the list: the active tab. Tab moves on to the panel, which takes focus itself (tabindex 0) so a panel with only text is still reached.

keys.Tab: Moves focus into the list, onto the active tab, then on to the panel
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus back out of the list
keys.ArrowRight: Moves to the next tab and shows its panel (automatic mode). In right to left layouts this is ArrowLeft. Wraps at the end
keys.ArrowLeft: Moves to the previous tab and shows its panel (automatic mode). In right to left layouts this is ArrowRight
keys.ArrowDown, ArrowUp: In a vertical list, move to the next and the previous tab
keys.Enter, Space: In manual mode, shows the panel of the focused tab

a11y.announce: Each tab reads its label, its count, its position (2 of 4) and whether it is selected. The panel is named by its tab.
notes: The active tab is marked by the indicator and a heavier weight, never by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).

The soft pill has a 1px border in the muted text color, 3:1 or better against the track and the pill fill in Studio, Desk and Neutral, dark and light (WCAG 1.4.11). The overlay-20 fill alone measures 1.5:1 to 1.9:1.

The list scrolls inside itself when the tabs do not fit, so the page never scrolls sideways (WCAG 1.4.10). The active tab scrolls into view inside the list on load and when it changes; only the list scrolls, never the page.
The focus ring is drawn inside the tab, so a scrolling list never clips it (WCAG 2.4.7).

Disabled tabs use the native disabled attribute from Radix: a tab is not an action, so it is skipped rather than kept focusable with aria-disabled. Say why on the page or in a Tooltip next to the list.
The trigger is the button Radix renders with role tab. It is not a system Button, because its indicator and count are parts of Tabs.
Contract keys: the arrows, Home and End are checked by hints; Enter and Space in manual mode are covered by the unit tests.
No native title attribute. A tab whose label is cut short by an ellipsis should get a Tooltip once Tooltip (1.6.6) is merged.

en.label: A short noun, sentence case: General, Members, History. No verbs, no ending punctuation.
en.list: Names the set as a noun phrase: Board settings.
en.count: A number only, Western digits. Omit it at zero unless zero is the news.
en.panel: An empty panel says what to do next: No comments yet. Select a frame and press C to leave the first one.

ar.label: Noun form labels, white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: عام، الأعضاء، السجل.
ar.panel: An empty panel says what to do next, in white Saudi dialect: ما فيه تعليقات للحين. اختر إطار واضغط C عشان تضيف أول تعليق.

react.note: The indicator lives in the active trigger. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction tab-slide: the indicator slides with the shared pill of internal/indicator.ts, from the box the old one is drawn in to its own on the snappy spring, stretched along its travel by up to scale.stretch (translate and scale, center origin). The label it leaves dips and the one it reaches pops (scale.anticipate, added to its transform). Under reduced motion or a style's reduced mode nothing plays.

angular.behavior: cdk:a11y (FocusKeyManager) with the same DOM

styles.studio: Muted labels on the body, the active one bright and bold. ghost: a 2px bright line on the default hairline. soft: the overlay-20 pill with a muted text color border on an overlay-5 track, 6px corners.
styles.desk: The same parts on Desk tokens: Instrument Sans, the Desk text steps, the overlay steps over the dark or light desk. The line and the pill take the bright text color, not the yellow primary, so the active tab never reads as a primary action.
styles.neutral: Token driven; applies once the Neutral pack is merged.
styles.liquid: Planned.

mistakes.wrong: Tabs that link to other pages of the site
mistakes.right: Navbar or Sidebar links with aria-current page

mistakes.wrong: The active tab shown only by a color change
mistakes.right: The indicator and the heavier weight, which Tabs draws in every style

mistakes.wrong: Twelve tabs that push the page wider on a phone
mistakes.right: Up to eight; the list scrolls inside itself, and the rest can move into a Select or a menu

mistakes.wrong: A tab list with no name
mistakes.right: aria-label on TabsList: Board settings

mistakes.wrong: Tabs used to pick a value in a form
mistakes.right: SegmentedControl, RadioGroup or ToggleGroup

mistakes.wrong: A count typed into the label: Comments (12)
mistakes.right: The count prop, which draws the pill and keeps the name readable

name: TagField
summary: A box where people type free tags: Enter or a comma adds the text as a tag, each tag has a remove button, and optional suggestions show under the box.
useWhen: People add their own words as a list of values, such as tags on a post, keywords or email domains
Any text is a valid value, with suggestions from words used before
Pasting a list separated by commas or lines should become many values at once
avoidWhen: The values must come from a fixed list
Only one value is allowed
Long text or sentences, not short words

value.description: The tags (string[]), controlled with onValueChange. Typed string here because the schema has no array type.

defaultValue.description: Uncontrolled starting tags (string[]). Typed string here because the schema has no array type.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new string[] after an add or a removal.

suggestions.description: Suggested tags as ListBox items (type node here means structured data: an array of { value, label } or groups). The control becomes an ARIA 1.2 combobox with list autocomplete; tags already added are not suggested; choosing one adds its label.

max.description: The most tags. Text past it is not added: it stays in the control, and a visible message under the box (You can add up to 12 tags) says why.

size.description: Box height at one line from size.control (28, 32, 44px at default density). Tags are size.control.xs high; the box grows a line at a time.

shape.description: default: the style's control radius (a pill in Studio and Desk). pill: always fully round; best for one line.

invalid.description: The danger border and aria-invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field's error.

disabled.description: Native disabled on the control; remove buttons aria-disabled. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: Tags show without remove buttons; the control is read only. A dashed border.

required.description: aria-required on the control. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

removeLabel.description: The name of each remove button. Arabic default: حذف الوسم <tag>.

formatRemoved.description: The words read once after a removal. Arabic default: حذفنا الوسم <tag>.

name.description: Submits each tag under this name in a form, one hidden input per tag.

placeholder.description: A hint in the empty control, a verb plus a noun: Add a tag. Never the only label.

a11y.role: The control is a text input, named by the Field label. With suggestions it is an ARIA 1.2 combobox (aria-autocomplete list, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant) and the popup holds a ListBox named like the field. The tags sit in a group named like the field (aria-disabled when the field is disabled); each remove button is a CloseButton named Remove tag <tag>. Not modal.
a11y.focus: The control is the one tab stop; remove buttons are reached with Backspace and the arrow keys (tabindex -1). After a removal focus moves to the next tag, else the one before, else the control. With suggestions focus stays in the control.

keys.Enter: Adds the typed text as a tag, or the highlighted suggestion; with an empty control it does what the form does
keys.Comma: Adds the typed text as a tag (the comma and the Arabic comma ،)
keys.Backspace: On an empty control, focuses the last tag's remove button. On a remove button, removes that tag
keys.Delete: On a remove button, removes that tag
keys.ArrowLeft: With the caret at the start, moves to the last tag; between tags, to the one before. In right to left layouts this is ArrowRight
keys.ArrowRight: Between tags, to the next one, and past the last back to the control. In right to left layouts this is ArrowLeft
keys.Home: On a remove button, moves to the first tag
keys.End: On a remove button, moves back to the control
keys.ArrowDown: With suggestions: opens them, then moves to the next suggestion
keys.ArrowUp: With suggestions: moves to the previous suggestion. Escape closes the suggestions

a11y.announce: Each add, removal, duplicate and the max are read once from a polite status (Added tag design, Removed tag design, design is already added; Arabic أضفنا الوسم، حذفنا الوسم، الحد الأعلى للوسوم: 10). The status empties first, so the same words are read again. A duplicate or the max also shows as visible text under the box (WCAG 3.3.1), a FieldError that the control is described by, until the next edit, add or removal.
notes: Splitting and duplicates come from @the-system/shared tags.ts: the comma, the Arabic comma and new lines split; parts are trimmed; two tags are the same when their normalize() forms match (case, accents, Arabic diacritics, tatweel and alef forms ignored).
Pasting text with a separator adds every part at once; a single line pastes as typed text.

Every remove button has its own name (Remove tag design), never a bare Close (WCAG 2.4.6, 4.1.2). Remove buttons are 24px targets (size.target-min, WCAG 2.5.8) and keep the close icon, never color alone.
The suggestions popup is portaled into a Theme copied from the field's Theme and is its own root carrying data-part popup, as the Combobox popup is.
IME composition: Enter that confirms a composition never adds a tag.

Contract: the root is read as a field, not an overlay (no trigger): the popup holds no tab stop. data-state open and closed is on the popup root only. Backspace is checked on the one case control as focus-moves.
Disabled: the control is natively disabled and the tag group carries aria-disabled, so the faded tags read as unavailable (WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive components).
Escape closes the suggestions (in the ArrowUp entry): the contract suite checks Escape only on an overlay with a trigger, and a TagField has none.
Blur keeps typed text in the control and does not add it; only Enter, a separator or a paste adds. The control's text is not submitted with the form.
Text past max stays in the control, whether it ends with Enter, a separator or a paste; a paste replaces the selected text.

The refusal message is a FieldError rendered right after the root (outside the Field wiring, so a Field error keeps its own id and the Field stays valid). The control's aria-describedby names it only while it shows.

en.label: A plural noun in a Field label: Tags, Keywords.
en.placeholder: A verb plus a noun: Add a tag.
en.hint: Say how to add: Press Enter or type a comma to add a tag.
en.tags: Short words, as people write them.
en.error: Say what to do: Add at least one tag.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: الوسوم.
ar.hint: اضغط Enter أو اكتب فاصلة لإضافة وسم. The Latin run Enter goes through Bidi.
ar.remove: حذف الوسم <tag>. After removal: حذفنا الوسم <tag>.

react.behavior: hand built; suggestions on radix:Popover (Root, Anchor, Content) with ListBox virtualFocus; tags.ts from @the-system/shared
react.note: Sources Figma-Killer-2 TagPill/ and AddablePropertyField/ were not reachable in the lane session; the box follows the Combobox field, the tags Chip, the popup the list family popup.

angular.behavior: div[dsTagField], hand built with the shared tags.ts and filter.ts: the suggestions are a ListBox with virtualFocus in a CDK ComponentPortal placed with the Radix Popper steps (internal/popper.ts), the highlight on the CDK ActiveDescendantKeyManager, ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The host is the root (the Radix Anchor, with its class and data-radix-popper-side and -align). Inputs take the React prop names; onValueChange is the valueChange output of [(value)]. removeLabel and formatRemoved are function inputs. Native input props React spreads on the input (placeholder, id, name, aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby) are inputs. The CloseButton DOM is inline on a native button until the Angular CloseButton exists. Angular Aria would replace the key manager once @angular/aria is installed. TagField.css is used as is.

native.behavior: hand built: a wrapping row of tags and a TextInput

styles.studio: The box is the Input box: a transparent pill with the control border, the glow and the ring while anything inside has focus. Tags are overlay-10 pills with a ghost CloseButton. The popup is the Studio menu surface.
styles.desk: The same box and tags. The suggestions popup is the Desk menu glass; the lit row is the yellow primary fill (the Desk ListBox recipe).
styles.neutral: Tokens only: the Neutral control radius and border, the Neutral menu surface.

mistakes.right: Remove tag design: each button names its tag (built in)

mistakes.wrong: Adding Design and design as two tags
mistakes.right: Duplicates dropped, case and diacritic insensitive, and announced (built in)

mistakes.wrong: Only Enter adds a tag
mistakes.right: Enter, the comma and the Arabic comma, and pasted lists (built in)

mistakes.right: MultiSelect
