name: Textarea
summary: Multi line text in a bordered box that grows with the text, with an optional character count that never cuts the text.
useWhen: Free text longer than one line: a message, a description, notes
Text with a character limit the person should see while typing
A value where Enter must add a new line
avoidWhen: A short value on one line: a name, an email, a link
Formatted text with bold, lists or links: no component in the system covers it yet
A list of separate values such as tags

size.description: Padding and text size in step with Input. lg uses a fixed 16px text, so phones do not zoom on focus.

shape.description: default only, radius.field. A pill never wraps lines.

rows.description: Lines shown when empty, the floor of the auto height.

maxRows.description: Lines the auto height grows to before the text scrolls inside. No cap when unset.

autoHeight.description: Grows with the text through CSS field-sizing content, with a measuring fallback. false keeps rows lines and a vertical resize handle.

limit.description: The character limit for the count. Past it the value is invalid and the count turns danger. The text is never cut; there is no native maxlength.

showCount.description: Shows the count. Default true when limit is set. Without a limit it shows the plain number.

countMessage.description: (left) => string, the words announced near and past the limit. left is negative past it. Default English, or Arabic under an Arabic Theme.

invalid.description: Marks the value invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field. Past the limit it is always invalid.

disabled.description: Native disabled. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: Still focusable, selectable and readable. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

required.description: Sets aria-required. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

rootProps.description: Props for the root box. className and style also go to the root; every other native prop and the ref go to the textarea.

a11y.role: textbox, multi line, from the native textarea
a11y.focus: The textarea is the only tab stop. A press anywhere in the box focuses it. Focus shows the glow and a 2px ring around the box.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the textarea, and on to the next control
keys.Enter: Adds a new line. It never submits the form.

a11y.announce: Name from the Field label. The Field description, the error and the count in words (39 of 200 characters) through aria-describedby. A polite live region speaks once when the count enters the last tenth before the limit (at least the last 10 characters) and once when it goes past the limit, never on every key.
notes: Past the limit the text stays: no native maxlength, which would cut a paste without a word. The value turns invalid and the count turns danger. Pass a Field error that says how many characters to remove.
The count is shown as digits that run left to right in every language, at the inline end of the box.
Auto height uses CSS field-sizing content with a rows floor and a maxRows cap, so there is no script measuring where the browser supports it.
Read only looks different from disabled: a dashed border and a quiet fill, full contrast text, and it stays focusable.
Disabled uses native disabled and draws with opacity.disabled, like every control.
Say the limit in the Field description, for example Up to 200 characters, so it is known before typing.
The live region is a visually hidden child of the root with no data-part: it is not an anatomy part.

en.label: A visible Field label, a noun in sentence case: Brief, Message to the team.
en.placeholder: An example at most: For example, the review is moved to Thursday. Never the label.
en.limit: State it in the description: Up to 200 characters. Past it the error says how many to remove.

ar.label: عنوان ظاهر دايم، بصيغة الاسم وبدون تشكيل: وصف اللوحة، ملاحظات
ar.placeholder: مثال بس، مو بديل عن العنوان
ar.limit: الحد يظهر في الوصف: بحد أقصى 200 حرف. والأرقام بالأرقام الغربية

react.note: Motion is the focus glow fade of Input, named fade like Input; under reduced motion the duration token is 0ms.

angular.behavior: div[dsTextarea] around a native textarea, ControlValueAccessor, CSS field-sizing
angular.note: The host box is the root. The value is a model and, as in React, also the text content of the native textarea. The count and the live region use the Radix VisuallyHidden inline style. countMessage is a function input.

native.note: Grows with onContentSizeChange between the rows floor and the maxRows cap.

styles.studio: The Input border and glow, radius.field corners instead of a pill
styles.desk: The same, in Instrument Sans
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: maxLength on a textarea, which cuts a paste without a word
mistakes.right: limit, which shows the count, marks the value invalid past it and keeps the text

mistakes.wrong: A pill shaped textarea
mistakes.right: The default shape: lines wrap, so the corners are radius.field

mistakes.wrong: Enter that submits the form from a textarea
mistakes.right: Enter adds a line; a Button submits

mistakes.wrong: A count announced on every key
mistakes.right: The built in live region, which speaks near the limit and past it

name: Theme
summary: Stamps every runtime axis on its own element, resolves what is not passed from the nearest parent Theme, and gives the subtree its direction, icon set and style data.
useWhen: At the root of an app, once, so tokens, base CSS, direction and icons apply
Around a subtree that needs another scheme, style, density, language or direction
Around a demo or a preview that shows one combination of axes
avoidWhen: Changing one color or size in one place: use a component prop or a token
Setting dir or lang alone on an element: the tokens, Radix and the icons would not follow
Wrapping every component: one Theme per subtree that changes an axis is enough

style.description: The style pack id. Any custom id is accepted. At the root the default is studio; nested, the parent's.

scheme.description: Default from the style.json at the root, the parent's when nested. A scheme the style does not list falls back to its default.

density.description: Default from the style.json at the root, the parent's when nested.

glass.description: Read only by styles that use glass.

dir.description: Follows lang when lang is passed and dir is not. Otherwise the parent's, then from lang.

lang.description: A BCP 47 tag. The system ships en and ar.

css.description: Inline styles for the Theme element, as a React style object (CSSProperties). style is taken by the style axis.

a11y.focus: Never focusable. It adds no role.
notes: dir and lang on the element let screen readers pick the right voice and let CSS mirror the layout.
The Radix direction provider follows dir, so menus, sliders and arrow keys mirror in right to left.
Arabic text gets IBM Plex Sans Arabic, zero tracking, taller lines and small text one step up through base.css. Body text keeps its size.

A root Theme is needed even when <html> is stamped with themeAttributes(): attributes give the CSS its axes but no React context, so useTheme, useOptionalPart and the Dialog and Toaster portals would fall back to the root defaults (Studio dark, English). Stamp <html> for the first paint and wrap the app in <Theme> with the same axes.

en.lang: Set lang on the root Theme. A Latin island inside Arabic is any element with lang en; it gets the Latin type back.

ar.lang: Set lang ar on the root Theme. dir follows as rtl.

react.note: Exports Theme, useTheme, useOptionalPart, themeAttributes and resolveTheme from packages/react/src/theme. themeAttributes() on <html> does not replace the root <Theme>: attributes carry no React context.

angular.behavior: @angular/cdk Directionality
angular.note: dsTheme directive in packages/angular/src/theme, inputs named like the React props. A static style="desk" never reaches the style input (the Angular compiler parses it as inline CSS): bind [style]="'desk'" or use dsTheme="desk". Inline styles pass through css. Provides DsThemeService (value signal, optionalPart), the CDK Directionality and the icon style to its subtree. applyDocumentTheme stamps the html element.

native.note: ThemeProvider passes the resolved theme object through context, with the same axis names.

styles.studio: Black body, Inter Variable, default density
styles.desk: Black desk, Instrument Sans, default density, window and dialog controls and titlebar turned on

mistakes.wrong: <div dir="rtl" lang="ar"> around a screen
mistakes.right: <Theme lang="ar">, which also sets dir, the Radix direction and the Arabic type

mistakes.wrong: <Theme style={{ padding: 8 }}>
mistakes.right: <Theme css={{ padding: 8 }}>: style is the style axis

mistakes.wrong: Reading data-style from the DOM to pick a branch
mistakes.right: useTheme().style, or useOptionalPart for a part only one style shows

mistakes.wrong: <html {...themeAttributes({ style: "desk", lang: "ar" })}> with no Theme around the app
mistakes.right: Stamp <html> and also wrap the app in <Theme style="desk" lang="ar">: portals and useTheme read the React context, not the html attributes

name: Tile
summary: The borderless card of Studio: a thumbnail, a title, one meta line and an icon action, laid out in a TileGrid split by a 1px gap that shows the parent surface.
useWhen: A browsable grid of files, boards, templates or assets, where the thumbnail and the name do most of the work
A Studio dashboard of many equal items that should read as one surface cut into cells
A grid where every item opens on click and holds at most one or two icon actions
avoidWhen: An item that needs a description, a body or labelled buttons
A single item on its own, away from a grid
Rows of text that people scan and compare
Picking one option out of several

size.description: Padding and type size: space s with a small title, or space l with a medium title.

selected.description: Draws a 2px ring inside the tile (not color alone) and sets data-selected. Say it in words too, with aria-current on the TileLink.

asChild.description: On Tile and TileGrid: renders the single child element as the root, for example a ul grid of li tiles.

href.description: On TileLink: the target. Its hit area covers the whole tile.

children.description: TileMedia, TileTitle (with a TileLink), TileMeta, TileActions. TileGrid takes Tiles.

a11y.role: None on the tile. The title is a heading; a whole tile link is one native link inside it. A ul TileGrid with li tiles (asChild) gives a list role and a count.
a11y.focus: The tile never takes focus. Tab reaches the TileLink, then the actions. Focus draws a double ring inside the tile (2px ring, 2px gap, 2px ring), so the grid's clip never hides it and it never looks like the single selected ring.

keys.Tab: Moves to the tile link, then to its actions, then to the next tile
keys.Enter: On the tile link: opens it

a11y.announce: The link is named by the full title, even when the visible title is cut at two lines. The meta line is read after it.
notes: The title is cut at two lines with an ellipsis; the link still holds the full name. Keep names short enough to read in two lines.
Actions sit above the stretched link target and keep their own 24px targets.
Forced colors: every tile gets a CanvasText border, the selected one a Highlight outline at its edge, focus a Highlight outline one step further in.

en.title: The item's name, sentence case: Spring launch.
en.meta: One short fact: Edited 2 hours ago.
en.actions: An icon action names its item: More actions for Spring launch.

ar.title: The item's name in white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: إطلاق الربيع.
ar.meta: One short fact, Western digits: آخر تعديل قبل 3 أيام.

react.note: Motion: none of its own. The hover swaps the surface tone at once, as the source does. fade-rise is named for the entrance of a tile into its grid, which the parent drives, from the 1.11 catalog list. TileGrid is a second root (data-ds tile-grid) styled in TileGrid.css, with no manifest of its own.

angular.note: dsTileGrid and dsTile on the host, parts as attribute directives. Tile.css as is.

native.note: A FlatList with numColumns and a hairline gap on the parent surface; each tile a Pressable.

styles.studio: Borderless tiles on surface 2, square inside the grid, split by a 1px gap that shows the parent; the grid rounds the outside with radius.panel. Hover steps to surface 3.
styles.desk: recipes/Tile.css: the grid opens to a space.m gap, each tile is a rounded card on the surface with the hairline border; hover steps to surface 2.
styles.neutral: Free cards with a 1px border.default edge and a space.m gap, each on radius.panel and the surface fill (recipes/Tile.css). Hover steps to surface 2.
styles.liquid: Planned: solid tiles under the glass layer.

mistakes.wrong: Tiles with their own borders and gaps in Studio
mistakes.right: Tiles inside TileGrid; the 1px gap is the separation

mistakes.wrong: A tile with a description paragraph and two labelled buttons
mistakes.right: A Card

mistakes.wrong: Hiding the tile actions until hover
mistakes.right: Keep them visible, so keyboard and touch reach them

name: TitleBar
summary: The bar at the top of a window or a panel: window controls at the start, the title, then trailing actions.
useWhen: The header of a Window, or of a Dialog drawn as a window in Desk
A panel header that needs a title and a close button
avoidWhen: The header of a page
A toolbar of many tools with no title

title.description: The title. One line with an ellipsis.

titleId.description: id of the title, for aria-labelledby on the window or dialog.

actions.description: The end slot: IconButtons and small Buttons.

moveLabel.description: Puts the title in a focusable move handle (part move, role group) named by this label: "Move window". The host (Window) listens for the keys there.

moveHint.default: Arrow keys move the window. Shift moves it further.
moveHint.description: Description of the move handle, through aria-describedby. Under lang="ar" the default is مفاتيح الأسهم لتحريك النافذة، ومع Shift لمسافة أبعد.

a11y.role: none: a plain container. The title is a heading (h2 by default).
a11y.focus: The bar itself is not focusable. With moveLabel the move handle is a tab stop with the 2px ring; while it has keyboard focus the title wraps to show in full. Then the controls and actions take focus in order.

keys.Tab: Moves through the controls, the move handle and the actions

a11y.announce: The heading is read in document order. A window or dialog points aria-labelledby at titleId.
notes: The title truncates with an ellipsis; the full text stays in the DOM, and keyboard focus on the move handle shows it wrapped.
Parts minimize, zoom and close are IconButtons a host renders in the actions slot when it has no lights (Window in Studio). They belong to the TitleBar, their nearest root.
In right to left layouts a bar with controls keeps them at the top left and centers the title, as macOS draws it. A bar without controls mirrors.

en.title: A file or app name in sentence case.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics. Latin file names go through Bidi.

angular.behavior: div[dsTitleBar]
angular.note: A first port exists for the Desk dialog chrome (packages/angular/src/components/title-bar): controls, title (a string, a TemplateRef or an ng-template dsTitleBarTitle), actions, as, titleId, active, with the React DOM. No move handle and no demo yet; it turns ready with Window. TitleBar.css is used as is.

native.note: Native screens use the platform navigation bar.

styles.studio: A plain header on the panel surface with a hairline under it (recipes/Window.css when inside a Window).
styles.desk: Transparent, as the source .dwin-bar: the window glass shows through, no divider. The lights sit at the start.

mistakes.wrong: A title in a native title attribute to show the full text
mistakes.right: The full text stays in the title; a Tooltip shows it

mistakes.wrong: Mirroring the lights in Arabic
mistakes.right: The lights keep their place and order; only a bar without lights mirrors

name: Toast
summary: A short notice that something happened, shown in a corner and gone on its own. Called from anywhere with toast(); one Toaster renders them. Call shape: toast(title, options) or toast(options); toast.success, toast.warning, toast.danger and toast.info set the tone; each returns the id; toast.dismiss(id) closes one (or all, without an id), toast.update(id, patch) changes one in place, toast.configure(config) sets the max and the durations for the app.
useWhen: Confirming that an action the person took has finished: Draft saved, Link copied
A failure the person can fix later or retry from the toast, as tone danger with one action
A background event worth knowing now: a new version, a finished upload
Progress that ends in a result, updated in place with toast.update
avoidWhen: The person needs to make a decision before going on
Long content, a list, or anything to read twice
A critical error that blocks the task or loses data
A message tied to one field or one place on the page
Something that must stay on screen while the condition lasts

parts.Toast: root, without behavior and without data-state
parts.isInsideToaster: helper for overlays: true for a target inside the toaster

tone.description: The color and icon, and the timing: neutral, info and success close after 4s, warning after 6s, danger stays until closed.

title.description: One line: what happened, naming the thing.

description.description: More detail. Long text wraps in full; keep it to one or two sentences.

duration.description: toast() option. Milliseconds before it closes; Infinity keeps it. Default by tone. Ignored for danger and for a toast with an action, which stay until closed. toast.configure({ durations, max }) lengthens them for the whole app.

action.description: toast() option. One button: { label, onAction, altText }. A toast with an action never times out. altText is read in place of the button, for example where else the same action lives.

dedupeKey.description: toast() option. A toast that reads the same as an open one bumps its count instead of stacking; a key groups repeats with other copy; false turns it off.

id.description: toast() option. A call with the id of an open toast updates it.

lang.description: toast() option. The language of the copy when it differs from the page. The root gets lang and dir.

count.description: Toast prop. The repeat count; the Toaster passes it from the store.

onClose.description: Toast prop. Renders the close button and is called by it. The Toaster always renders it.

closeLabel.description: The accessible name of the close button. Arabic under lang ar.

position.description: Toaster prop. end is the inline end: right in English, left in Arabic. auto follows the platform axis: top-center on ios, bottom-end elsewhere (android.css places the snackbar at the start). The toaster carries the resolved value in data-position.

label.description: Toaster prop. The name of the region. {hotkey} in it is replaced by the hotkey.

hotkey.description: Toaster prop. The keys that move focus to the toasts.

store.description: Toaster prop. The store to render. Default the app wide store behind toast().

a11y.role: The Toaster is a region (named Notifications) holding a list; each toast is a list item. Announcements go through two visually hidden regions owned by the Toaster: role status (polite) and role alert (assertive, for danger).
a11y.focus: Not modal: toasts never take focus on their own. F8 moves focus to the list, which shows the focus ring; Tab moves through the toasts, newest first, and each toast's action and close button. Closing the focused toast puts focus on the list. While a dialog with a focus trap is open, keyboard focus stays in the dialog: the toasts stay visible, readable and clickable, and a toast with an action waits until the dialog closes.

keys.F8: Moves focus to the notifications list
keys.Tab: Moves to the next toast, action or close button
keys.Enter: Runs the focused action or close button
keys.Escape: Closes a toast only when the key comes from inside the toaster: the focused toast, or the newest one from the list. Escape anywhere else, in a Window, a Dialog or a form, leaves every toast alone, a danger toast included, and is not prevented, so the system Dialog still closes itself. A raw Radix Dialog from a consumer does not get that Escape while a toast shows above it (Radix gives Escape to the top layer only), so use the system Dialog or close the toast first.

a11y.announce: Once per change (WCAG 4.1.3): when a toast shows, and again on each repeat or update, as "Notification. Title. Description. Action alternative." with the toast's text in the toast's language. danger is assertive (role alert), the rest polite (role status). The toast itself has no live role and keeps its element across a repeat or update, so it is never read twice and focus stays. Radix's own announcer is muted. The close button is not read.
notes: danger toasts and toasts with an action stay until closed. The others pause while the pointer is over them, while focus is inside, and while the window is blurred or the tab hidden (WCAG 2.2.1). toast.configure({ durations }) lengthens them for the whole app.
Swipe toward the edge closes a toast; the close button is the button path for the same action (WCAG 2.5.7).

Above an open modal dialog the toasts stay visible (z.toast is above z.dialog), stay in the accessibility tree and take the pointer. A dialog calls isInsideToaster(event.target) in onFocusOutside, onPointerDownOutside and onInteractOutside and prevents the default, so a toast never closes it.
At most three toasts show at once; the rest wait their turn, so a burst never covers the page.
No native title attribute anywhere.

en.title: Say what happened and name the thing: Draft saved, Could not upload photo.jpg. Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
en.description: Optional. What it means or what to do next, in one or two short sentences. Long text wraps in full, so keep it short.
en.action: A verb plus a noun: Retry upload, Undo move, Open draft. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes. One action at most. The toast then stays until closed.
en.danger: Name the failure and what is safe: Could not publish page. Your draft is safe.
en.repeats: Keep the copy the same for the same event, so repeats fold into one toast with a count.

ar.title: Say what happened and name the thing, in noun forms where you can: المسودة محفوظة، تعذر رفع الصورة. No diacritics.
ar.action: Noun form labels, no diacritics: إعادة الرفع، تراجع عن النقل. Never the imperative.
ar.digits: Western digits. Latin names in the copy go through Bidi when the toast is rendered by hand.
ar.lang: Pass lang: "ar" when the page is not Arabic, so the toast gets the Arabic type and direction.

react.note: Toaster renders the shared store from @the-system/shared; toast is re-exported from @the-system/react. Call shape: toast(title: string, options?) or toast(options) with title inside; toast.success, toast.warning, toast.danger and toast.info take the same arguments and set tone; toast.dismiss(id?), toast.update(id, { tone, title, description }), toast.configure({ max, durations }). From packages/shared/src/toast.ts.

angular.behavior: hand built on the shared toast store and the Radix Toast DOM; CDK ComponentPortal for the themed layer
angular.note: ng-container dsToaster mounts the toaster; div[dsToast] is the static notice. toast() and the store come from @the-system/shared and are re-exported. Reuses the store and its timers, reports pause and resume like the React Toaster, owns two visually hidden live regions (no CDK LiveAnnouncer, which would add an element React does not render). onClose on dsToast is a function input. The close part is a private CloseButton twin until the Angular CloseButton lands. Toast.css is used as is. Order 1.23 as React: the stack (data-stacked and the place values from internal/toast-stack.ts, a copy of React's stack.ts), data-expanded on hover or focus inside, data-paused from the same boolean that pauses the store, the progress part of a timed toast, the swipe of internal/toast-swipe.ts (a copy of React's swipe.ts), and position auto.

native.note: The same store. Safe areas and reduce motion from the platform.

styles.studio: A flat surface card with a hairline border and a 2px edge in the tone color on the inline start side.
styles.desk: Glass notifications as on the desk: strong glass fill, window blur, window radius and the soft window shadow (recipes/Toast.css). Solid under reduced transparency and more contrast.
styles.neutral: Planned: a white card with a small shadow.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass capsule at the top center.

mistakes.wrong: A toast for an error that blocks the task, such as a lost session
mistakes.right: An AlertDialog that says what happened and how to go on

mistakes.wrong: A danger toast that closes itself after a few seconds
mistakes.right: danger stays until closed; the store ignores a duration for it

mistakes.wrong: A toast with two buttons, or an action labelled OK
mistakes.right: One action at most, a verb plus a noun: Retry upload

mistakes.wrong: The same toast stacked five times by a retry loop
mistakes.right: Same copy, one toast with a count. Dedupe is on by default.

mistakes.wrong: A second Toaster for Arabic copy
mistakes.right: One Toaster per page; pass lang: "ar" on the toast

mistakes.wrong: A toast as the only place a result lives
mistakes.right: Show the result on the page too; the toast only says it happened

mistakes.wrong: Mounting the Toaster inside a dialog or outside the root Theme
mistakes.right: Mount it once inside the root Theme, before any dialog can open

mistakes.wrong: A dialog that closes when the person clicks a toast above it
mistakes.right: Call isInsideToaster(event.target) in the dialog's outside handlers and prevent the default

mistakes.wrong: toast({ type: "success", message: "Draft saved" }), or a toast component rendered by hand for a one off notice
mistakes.right: toast.success("Draft saved"), or toast("Draft saved", { tone: "success", lang: "en" }); keep the id to call toast.update(id, patch) or toast.dismiss(id)

mistakes.wrong: Rebuilding the swipe with the Radix swipe props, or a timer bar with its own setTimeout
mistakes.right: The Toaster runs the swipe (rubber band against the edge, distance or flick to close) and the progress line is a CSS animation that pauses with the store (data-paused on the toaster), so the line and the timer never drift apart

name: ToggleButton
summary: A button that stays pressed or not: bold, mute, grid view. aria-pressed tells assistive tech the state.
useWhen: One setting that is on or off and applies at once, shown as a button in a toolbar
A formatting control (bold, italic) or a view switch that can be on alone
An icon only on and off control in a toolbar, named by its label
avoidWhen: A choice between two or more options where one is always on
A setting in a form that is saved with the form
An action that runs once (save, send)

onPressedChange.description: Called with the new pressed value.

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px in the default density. A ButtonGroup passes its size; this prop wins.

emphasis.description: As Button. No link: a link that stays pressed reads as neither.

shape.description: default takes radius.control (Desk draws it as a pill), pill is fully round, square takes radius.sm.

start.description: Leading content: a system icon name or a node. 16px at every size.

end.description: Trailing content: a system icon name or a node.

icon.description: The icon only form: an icon name or a node. Then label is the accessible name.

label.description: The accessible name of the icon only form (aria-label). Required with icon.

disabled.description: aria-disabled and data-disabled; stays focusable; does not toggle.

children.description: The visible label: the setting it turns on, a noun (Grid view).

a11y.role: button with aria-pressed
a11y.focus: In the tab order in every state. A 2px ring on keyboard focus, the doubled ring on a solid fill.

keys.Enter: Toggles the pressed state
keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: aria-pressed is announced as pressed or not pressed with the name. The name stays the same in both states.
notes: Pressed is not told by color alone: an on toggle also gets a 2px inner ring.
In forced colors an on toggle is drawn in Highlight and HighlightText.
Keep the label the same in both states. Do not swap Show to Hide: aria-pressed carries the state.
A ButtonGroup passes size, emphasis and shape through context; a prop on the toggle wins.

Motion, round 3 (toggle-pop, proposed): the state-layer part, aria-hidden, pools under the pointer while pressed; turning on, it floods from the press point across the button while the on fill crosses in; turning off, it drains back, faster. From the keyboard it floods from the centre. The button does not dip and the content does not scale. Reduced motion: no layer and no cross fade.

en.label: The setting it turns on, a noun or a short phrase in sentence case: Grid view, Mute alerts. The same in both states.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: عرض الشبكة، كتم التنبيهات.

angular.behavior: button[dsToggleButton] on DsButtonBase, host bindings
angular.note: aria-pressed and data-state on the host, as Radix Toggle sets them. onPressedChange is the pressedChange output of [(pressed)]; defaultPressed seeds the local state when pressed is not bound. start, end and icon take an icon name or a TemplateRef. Button.css is used as is.

native.note: 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android.

styles.studio: The overlay fill steps up and a 2px inner ring shows when on.

name: ToggleGroup
summary: A labelled set of toggle buttons with one tab stop, where one (type single) or several (type multiple) can be on: text style, filter chips, view options.
useWhen: Several related settings that each turn on or off and apply at once: bold, italic and underline (type multiple)
Filter chips over a list, where any number can be on (type multiple)
A compact choice in a toolbar where turning the only on item off is allowed, so none may be on (type single)
A set of toggles that should be one tab stop and move with the arrow keys
avoidWhen: Exactly one option must always be on (a view or a mode)
A choice in a form that is saved with the form
Actions that run once rather than stay on
A single setting on its own

insteadUse.One setting on its own: ToggleButton, or Switch in a settings list

type.description: single: at most one item on, Radix renders role radiogroup with radio items. multiple: any number on, role toolbar with pressed buttons.

value.description: Controlled. A string for single (empty string for none), a list for multiple. Pair with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: The value at first, uncontrolled.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new value. For single, an empty string when the on item is turned off.

aria-label.description: The group's name, for example Text style. Required unless aria-labelledby is set.

aria-labelledby.description: The id of a visible heading that names the group. Required unless aria-label is set.

size.description: Passed to every item that does not set its own size. Spaced xs and sm groups use the smaller gap.

emphasis.description: Passed to every item that does not set its own. No default: items are soft, as ToggleButton.

shape.description: Passed to every item that does not set its own. No default. Attached, only the outer corners take the shape.

orientation.description: A row with ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, or a column with ArrowUp and ArrowDown. Sets data-orientation.

attached.description: Joins the items into one seamed control: no gap, inner corners square on the logical sides (they flip in RTL), a 1px divider. Sets data-attached.

disabled.description: Every item is disabled: aria-disabled, does not toggle, stays focusable. Sets data-disabled on the root.

loop.description: Arrow keys wrap from the last item to the first and back.

children.description: ToggleGroupItems, each with a unique value. The item takes children (the label), start, end, icon with label for the icon only form, and disabled, as ToggleButton.

a11y.role: radiogroup of radio items with aria-checked (type single), or toolbar of buttons with aria-pressed (type multiple); named by aria-label or aria-labelledby
a11y.focus: One tab stop: Tab enters on the on item (or the first), the arrows move between items. Focus alone does not toggle. Disabled items keep aria-disabled and stay focusable and in the arrow order (anatomy rule 5), so a Tooltip can say why; they do not toggle.

keys.Tab: Moves focus into the group, on the on item or the first item, then out of it
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus out of the group, backward
keys.ArrowRight: Moves focus to the next item in the reading direction (the previous one in RTL); wraps
keys.ArrowLeft: Moves focus to the previous item in the reading direction (the next one in RTL); wraps
keys.ArrowDown: In a vertical group, moves focus to the next item; wraps
keys.ArrowUp: In a vertical group, moves focus to the previous item; wraps
keys.Home: Moves focus to the first item
keys.End: Moves focus to the last item
keys.Enter: Toggles the focused item

a11y.announce: The group name when focus enters, then each item by its name with checked or not checked (single) or pressed or not pressed (multiple), and its position in the set.
notes: On is not told by color alone: an on item gets the ToggleButton inner ring, and Highlight in forced colors.
Every icon only item needs its own label: the group name does not name its items.
Keep each label the same in both states; the checked or pressed state carries it.
Under forced colors the focus outline of an attached item is pulled inside it, so the next item does not cover it.
The native role above is for type single. Type multiple is a toolbar of buttons with the selected (pressed) state.
While an on item of an attached group has keyboard focus, its inner ring gives way to the focus ring; the on fill still tells the state.

en.name: Name the group by what its items set: Text style, Task filters, Board view. Sentence case.
en.labels: Each item is a short noun in sentence case: Bold, Open, Grid. The same words in both states.

ar.name: Noun form, no diacritics: فلاتر المهام، عرض اللوحة.
ar.labels: Short noun form labels, no diacritics: مفتوحة، قائمة، شبكة. Never the imperative.

react.behavior: radix:ToggleGroup; items are ToggleButton roots on ButtonBase
react.note: The axes reach the items through ButtonGroupContext, which ButtonRoot reads; an item's own prop wins. No motion of its own: items keep Button's. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction tab-slide: a single group renders an empty aria-hidden span as the first child of each item (inside the item part) that draws the on fill and ring, so the shared pill (internal/indicator.ts) slides the fill from the item it leaves on the snappy spring, stretched along its travel. A multiple group has none. The value of a single group is kept by ToggleGroup so it knows when it changes.

angular.behavior: div[dsToggleGroup] and button[dsToggleGroupItem] on DsButtonBase, hand built with the Radix ToggleGroup DOM on behavior/roving-radio.ts (CDK FocusKeyManager and Directionality), ControlValueAccessor
angular.note: The group host is the root (role radiogroup for single, toolbar for multiple); each item host is a ToggleButton root with data-part item. Inputs take the React prop names; onValueChange is the valueChange output of [(value)], a string for single and a list for multiple. start, end and icon take an icon name or a TemplateRef. The axes reach the items through DS_BUTTON_GROUP; an item input wins. Disabled items stay in the arrow order and focusable. A press is decided synchronously in a click listener added after the first render, so a caller (click) that calls preventDefault() keeps the state. With a one way [value], the local state still moves on a press, as an Angular model does. Works with reactive and template forms. ToggleGroup.css and Button.css are used as is.

native.note: 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android. Attached corners through the style function, flipped by I18nManager.

styles.studio: Overlay filled items; an on item steps up the fill and gets the 2px inner ring. Attached, the seam is color.border.default and only the outer corners take radius.control.
styles.desk: Pill items; attached, the group reads as one pill with square inner corners.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.right: SegmentedControl, which always keeps one option on

mistakes.wrong: Each item a separate tab stop, built from loose ToggleButtons
mistakes.right: ToggleGroup, one tab stop with arrow keys

mistakes.wrong: A group with no aria-label or aria-labelledby
mistakes.right: A name that says what the items set: Text style

mistakes.wrong: Icon only items with no label
mistakes.right: label on every icon only item: List view, Grid view

mistakes.wrong: A ToggleGroup of form options saved with a submit button
mistakes.right: RadioGroup or a Checkbox group inside a Field

name: Toolbar
summary: A labelled row of controls for one context, such as a text editor or a canvas. One tab stop, arrow keys between items, and a More tools menu for what does not fit.
useWhen: Several commands and toggles that act on one thing in view: the selected text, the canvas, a table
A set of tools a keyboard user should cross with one Tab and the arrow keys
A bar of icon tools that must survive a narrow window without wrapping
avoidWhen: Two or three related actions with no shared context
Navigation between pages or sections
The actions of a form: submit and cancel
Switching between panels of content

aria-label.description: Toolbar: required unless aria-labelledby names a visible heading. Names the context: Text formatting, Canvas tools.

size.description: Toolbar: passed to every item that does not set its own (xs 24, sm 28, md 32, lg 44 px at default density). A Link item takes sm at xs.

emphasis.description: Toolbar: passed to every Button and IconButton item that does not set its own. The toolbar draws its own quiet surface.

orientation.description: Toolbar: a row, or a column where the up and down arrows move. Separators run across it.

loop.description: Toolbar: the arrow keys wrap from the last item to the first.

overflow.description: Toolbar: menu measures the top level children; the ones that do not fit are hidden (data-overflowed) and appear in the More tools menu, where choosing one clicks the hidden item. wrap lets the row break onto more lines.

moreLabel.description: Toolbar: the name of the overflow trigger. Arabic default: أدوات أكثر. Name the context when the page has more than one toolbar: More text tools.

icon.description: ToolbarButton and ToolbarToggleItem: a system icon name. With it the item is an IconButton and label (its name) is required; without, a Button with a visible label.

label.description: ToolbarButton and ToolbarToggleItem with icon: the accessible name, a verb plus a noun.

disabled.description: ToolbarButton, ToolbarLink and ToolbarToggleItem: aria-disabled, drawn with opacity.disabled. The item keeps its place in the arrow key order and its click is cancelled. A disabled link loses its href.

type.description: ToolbarToggleGroup: multiple toggles each item on its own (aria-pressed): bold, italic. single keeps one at most on (radio semantics): alignment.

value.description: ToolbarToggleGroup (a string, or a list for multiple) with onValueChange; ToolbarToggleItem: its value.

a11y.role: toolbar with a name and aria-orientation. Groups are role group with a name; toggle items are buttons with aria-pressed (multiple) or radio with aria-checked (single). The overflow trigger is a menu button.
a11y.focus: One tab stop: the last focused item, else the first. Arrow keys move between items, groups included. Hidden (overflowed) items cannot take focus and are skipped.

keys.Tab: Moves focus into the toolbar, to one item
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus out of the toolbar
keys.ArrowRight: Moves to the next item. In right to left layouts this is ArrowLeft. Wraps at the end
keys.ArrowLeft: Moves to the previous item. In right to left layouts this is ArrowRight
keys.ArrowDown, ArrowUp: In a vertical toolbar, move to the next and the previous item
keys.End: Moves to the last item, the More tools trigger when it shows
keys.Enter, Space: Runs the focused item, toggles a toggle item, or opens the More tools menu

a11y.announce: The toolbar is read with its name when focus enters. Each item reads its name, its pressed state and whether it is disabled. The More tools trigger reads as a menu button.
notes: Icon only items name their action through label (aria-label). A Tooltip with the same words belongs on each one once Tooltip (1.6.6) is merged; until then there is no visible hint, and no native title attribute.
Disabled items use aria-disabled and stay in the arrow key order, so a keyboard user learns they exist.
A toggle item that is on is drawn filled; in forced colors a Highlight frame marks it, and aria-pressed carries it for assistive tech.
Overflow keeps the page from scrolling sideways (WCAG 1.4.10): the toolbar is never wider than its container.
Every item is a system Button, IconButton or Link: 24px targets at xs, 44px at lg (WCAG 2.5.8).
Contract keys: arrows, Home and End are checked by hints; Enter and Space run on the items, which are Buttons with their own contract.
open and closed are the data-state of the More tools trigger, from DropdownMenu.
Items of a single ToolbarToggleGroup (radio semantics) appear in the More tools menu as checkbox items, since the menu has no radio entry built from the DOM yet.
On a disabled item the hover fill still shows: Button draws hover from its own data-disabled, which the toolbar cannot set without trapping the arrow keys.

en.toolbar: Name the context with a noun phrase: Text formatting, Canvas tools.
en.items: Verb plus noun: Add frame, Zoom in. Toggle items name the option: Bold, Show grid.
en.more: More tools, or More text tools when two toolbars share a page.

ar.items: Noun form labels, white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: إضافة إطار، تكبير، حذف الإطار.

react.note: Items are system Button, IconButton and Link roots through Radix asChild. Toggle groups use Radix ToolbarToggleGroup until ToggleButton and ToggleGroup (batch 1) are merged; then ToolbarToggleItem should render a ToggleButton. The overflow menu is the system DropdownMenu, which plays menu-scale. Round 2 (order 1.22, proposed), interaction toolbar-press: items dip their parts to scale.anticipate while pressed (Button's --_button-part-press) and a toggle item that turns on pops its icon (CSS keyframes, animation-composition add).

angular.behavior: cdk:a11y (FocusKeyManager) and cdk:menu for the overflow

native.note: A native toolbar is a row of Pressables with accessibilityRole toolbar; overflow becomes a menu sheet.

styles.studio: A surface-2 bar with a subtle hairline and the panel radius, ghost items, a 1px separator.
styles.desk: The same parts on Desk tokens; items take the Desk Button look (pills).
styles.neutral: Token driven; applies once the Neutral pack is merged.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass bar.

mistakes.right: aria-label naming the context: Text formatting

mistakes.wrong: Every item a separate tab stop
mistakes.right: Toolbar: one tab stop and the arrow keys

mistakes.wrong: A row of tools that pushes the page wider on a phone
mistakes.right: overflow menu, the default: the rest moves into More tools

mistakes.wrong: Pressed state shown only by a color change
mistakes.right: ToolbarToggleItem: aria-pressed and the filled on state

mistakes.wrong: Hiding a tool that cannot run now
mistakes.right: disabled: it stays in the row with aria-disabled

mistakes.wrong: An icon only item named More

name: Tooltip
summary: A short hint for a control, shown on hover and on keyboard focus. The only way to show a hint in the system: never the native title attribute.
useWhen: The label of an IconButton or another icon only control, shown on hover and focus
A keyboard shortcut for a control
Why a disabled action is disabled, on a control that stays focusable
avoidWhen: The only name of a control: the control needs its own label
Content with a link, a button or a field inside it
Information a person needs to finish a task, which must be visible without hovering
Touch first screens, where nothing hovers
Text longer than one or two short lines

content.description: The hint: short text, 240px wide at most (tooltip.width.max). It describes the control and never names it.

shortcut.description: A keyboard shortcut shown after the hint, for example Ctrl+C. Always left to right, also in Arabic. Text until Kbd (1.9.5) exists.

side.description: The preferred side. start and end follow the reading direction. It flips when there is no room.

align.description: Alignment along the trigger, mirrored in right to left layouts.

sideOffset.description: Distance from the trigger in px, the arrow included.

delayDuration.description: Open delay on hover in ms. Focus opens at once.

disabled.description: Renders the trigger alone, with no tooltip.

contentProps.description: Any other prop for the root (the Radix Content).

a11y.role: tooltip (the root). The trigger points at it with aria-describedby while it shows: it is the trigger's description, the trigger keeps its own name.
a11y.focus: Never takes focus. Keyboard focus on the trigger shows it at once, with no delay; blur hides it.

keys.Escape: Hides the tooltip without moving focus; the trigger keeps focus

a11y.announce: Read as the description of the focused control, after its name and role. When the hint is the same string as the control's label (an IconButton), it is not wired as the description, so it is not read twice.
notes: WCAG 1.4.13: hoverable (the pointer can move onto the tooltip and it stays), dismissable (Escape hides it without moving the pointer or focus), persistent (it stays until the pointer leaves both, focus leaves, or Escape).
Never the only name of a control. An IconButton keeps its label prop as its name; the tooltip shows the same words to sighted pointer users. Development builds warn when the trigger has no name.
A disabled action uses aria-disabled and stays focusable, so its tooltip can say why it is disabled.
No native title attribute, anywhere in the system.
The root carries data-side and data-align from Radix; data-side is physical after the logical side prop is mapped by direction.
Pointer down on the trigger hides the tooltip, so a click never leaves it covering what the click opened. On a disabled Button the press is swallowed, so the tooltip stays and keeps saying why.
The gallery shows some tooltips open with the open prop, so the contract suite and screenshots can read them; a tooltip is never open on load in a product.
disabled true keeps the trigger mounted (focus stays) and closes the tooltip.

Order 1.23: on touch, a finger that rests 500ms on the trigger opens the hint while it stays; moving or lifting earlier cancels. The tooltip unfolds out of its trigger side (--_tooltip-enter-stretch).

en.hint: The control's action, verb plus noun, sentence case, no period: Copy link, Close panel. For a disabled action, what to do: Select a layer to delete it.
en.shortcut: The keys as printed on the keyboard, joined with a plus: Ctrl+C, Shift+Ctrl+P.

ar.hint: Noun form, no diacritics: نسخ الرابط، إغلاق اللوحة.
ar.shortcut: Latin key names, left to right inside the Arabic text: Ctrl+C.

react.note: The portal is a Theme that copies the axes of the Theme the Tooltip is in. A Tooltip with no TooltipProvider above it renders its own provider. Exports TooltipProvider (delayDuration 500 ms, skipDelayDuration 300 ms): one near the app root, inside Theme, shares the delays so the next tooltip along a toolbar opens at once.

angular.behavior: cdk:overlay

native.note: Nothing hovers on touch screens. Native controls show their label in an accessibility hint and a long press shows the label.

styles.studio: A small bubble on the raised surface with the default border, the small radius and the tooltip shadow. Fades in on duration.fast while it moves 4px (space.3xs) away from the trigger.
styles.desk: Glass: the strong glass fill, the glass border and the window blur (recipe); turns solid under reduced transparency and more contrast.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned.

mistakes.wrong: An IconButton named only by its Tooltip
mistakes.right: The IconButton label prop names it; the Tooltip shows the same words

mistakes.wrong: title="Copy link" on a button
mistakes.right: A Tooltip around the button

mistakes.wrong: A link or a button inside a tooltip
mistakes.right: A Popover

mistakes.wrong: A disabled button with the disabled attribute and a tooltip that never shows
mistakes.right: The system Button disabled prop (aria-disabled), which stays focusable

mistakes.wrong: A paragraph of help text in a tooltip
mistakes.right: A Field description or a HoverCard

name: Tour
summary: A short guided tour that points at real parts of the screen, one step at a time. Not modal: the page stays usable, a ring marks the target and skip is always there.
useWhen: Introducing three to five parts of a screen the first time someone opens it
Showing where a new feature lives after a release
A walkthrough the person starts on purpose from a help menu
avoidWhen: Steps the person must complete to finish a task
Explaining one control: a single hint is enough
Content that blocks the page until it is read
More than five steps: split the tour or write a help page

steps.description: The steps in order: { target, title, body?, side?, align? }. target is a CSS selector, a ref or a function that returns the element. A missing target (or one that leaves the page) shows the step just under the middle of the viewport, with no ring and no arrow.

open.description: Controlled open state, with onOpenChange. Open it from any Button: the tour has no trigger part.

onOpenChange.description: Called with false on Escape, Skip tour and Finish tour.

step.description: Controlled step index from 0, with onStepChange. Clamped to the steps.

onFinish.description: Called when Finish tour is pressed on the last step, before onOpenChange(false).

size.description: The panel width: sm 240 (tooltip.width.max), md 320 px (menu.width.min times 1.6).

labels.description: Overrides for next, back, skip, finish and progress(current, total). Defaults: Next step, Previous step, Skip tour, Finish tour, Step 2 of 4; Arabic under lang ar.

side.description: Per step: the preferred side of the target. start and end follow the reading direction.

align.description: Per step: alignment along the target.

a11y.role: dialog (the panel), not modal: the page stays in the accessibility tree and usable. Named by the step title, described by the body and the progress line.
a11y.focus: On open and on every step, focus moves to the panel, so the title, the body and the progress are read. Tab then reaches Skip tour, Previous step and Next step. On close, focus returns to the element that had it when the tour started.

keys.Escape: Ends the tour and returns focus
keys.Tab: Moves to Skip tour, Previous step and Next step, then out to the step's target on the page (a target that takes no focus gets tabindex -1; with no target, the element that started the tour); the tour stays open (not modal, no trap)
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves back through the step's buttons; from the first button or the panel it moves to the step's target
keys.Enter, Space: On Next step, Previous step or Skip tour: runs it

a11y.announce: Each step is read when focus moves to it: the title, the body, then Step 2 of 4.
notes: Never blocks the page: no backdrop and no dimmed page. The root layer and the ring take no pointer, so the target stays usable. A click on the page does not end the tour.
Skip tour is on every step, the last one included. Escape ends the tour too.
The ring around the target is drawn in the focus ring color and is not the only signal: the panel's arrow points at the target and the title names it.
The target scrolls into view on each step when it is not already in view: smoothly, or at once (instant) under reduced motion.
An uncontrolled tour starts again at defaultStep each time it opens.
Focus moves to the panel on each step only while focus is in the tour; a person typing in the page keeps focus there, and Escape then does not pull focus back.
The panel carries data-side and data-align from Radix; data-side is physical after the logical side is mapped by direction.

The root is a fixed layer that holds the ring and the panel (the order made the content the root): the ring must sit outside the Radix wrapper, which is positioned with a transform, and still belong to the tour. Dialog uses the same shape.
The step state is local until packages/shared/src/stepper.ts (order 1.7.7) is merged; the props do not change when it moves.

en.title: What this part of the screen is, as a short phrase: Share with your team.
en.body: One or two sentences on what to do with it.
en.buttons: Next step, Previous step, Skip tour, Finish tour. Never OK, Got it or Continue.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics: مشاركة الفريق.
ar.buttons: الخطوة التالية، الخطوة السابقة، تخطي الجولة، إنهاء الجولة.

react.note: Shares the themed portal and side mapping of Popover (FloatingLayer.tsx).

angular.behavior: cdk:overlay

styles.studio: The Popover surface with the arrow; the ring is 2px in the focus ring color, a small gap around the target, the small radius.
styles.desk: The panel is glass: the strong glass fill, the glass border, the window blur and the soft window shadow (recipe). The ring is the same.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned.

mistakes.right: Tour draws a ring around the target and leaves the page as it is

mistakes.wrong: A tour with no way out until the last step
mistakes.right: Skip tour on every step, and Escape

mistakes.wrong: Buttons that say Got it or Next
mistakes.right: Next step, Previous step, Finish tour

mistakes.wrong: A tour that starts by itself on every visit
mistakes.right: Start it once for new people, or from a help menu

name: Window
summary: An app window over the page: a title bar, a body and an optional footer. It opens from a trigger, moves, zooms, minimizes and closes. Desk draws it as a glass window with traffic lights; Studio as a flat panel with a close button.
useWhen: A tool or a document the person works in next to the page: a board, a file browser, settings
Several views the person arranges side by side and brings to the front
Content that opens from a control and should grow out of it
avoidWhen: A decision that blocks the page until it is made
A short message with no work in it
A list of actions behind one control
Content that belongs in the page flow

parts.WindowLayer: none: the positioned layer that hosts windows (data-ds window-layer, a region named Windows, النوافذ in Arabic). Not a part of a window; see a11y notes

kind.description: Sets data-kind. canvas: a large window with a margin of layer around it, no body padding. finder: wide, the layer edge around it. settings: centered, as tall as its content.

title.description: Names the window through aria-labelledby. One line with an ellipsis.

actions.description: IconButtons or small Buttons at the end of the title bar, before the window buttons. They are TitleBar parts.

footer.description: The footer part, for the window's Buttons.

open.description: Controlled open state, with onOpenChange. Keep rendering the Window with open={false}: it stays mounted while window-close plays, then renders nothing. Unmounting it instead (a conditional render) skips the close motion.

zoomed.description: Fills the layer. Sets data-zoomed and aria-pressed on the zoom light.

onZoomedChange.description: With it, or inside a WindowLayer, zoom works: the zoom light (Desk), the zoom IconButton (Studio), Enter on the move handle and a double click on the title bar.

minimized.description: Plays window-minimize toward the dock, then hides the window. Sets data-minimized.

onMinimizedChange.description: With it minimize works: the minimize light (Desk) or IconButton (Studio). The app shows the way back (a dock) and sets minimized to false.

frame.description: { x, y, width, height } in px: x from the inline start edge of the layer, y from the top. null lets the kind place the window. Controlled with onFrameChange.

onFrameChange.description: Called on every move by key or pointer, with the clamped frame.

movable.description: Drag by the title bar and move with the arrow keys. Default true inside a WindowLayer or with a frame. A Window outside a WindowLayer sits in the page flow (position relative), has no frame and does not move unless it gets a frame.

origin.description: An element, a ref or a screen rect the window grows out of and closes back into. Focus returns to it on close.

dock.description: An element, a ref or a screen rect a minimized window falls into. Default the bottom center of the layer. Focus goes to it when nothing before it in the focus order can take focus.

modal.description: aria-modal and a Tab loop inside the window. Off by default: windows sit next to the page.

closeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is إغلاق النافذة. A prop always wins.

minimizeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تصغير النافذة. A prop always wins.

zoomLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تكبير النافذة. A prop always wins.

controlsLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is أزرار النافذة. A prop always wins.

moveLabel.description: Name of the move handle: the title of a window that can move, focusable, a TitleBar part. Under lang="ar" the default is تحريك النافذة.

moveHint.description: Description of the move handle. Default names the arrow keys, Shift, and Enter when zoom works, in Arabic under lang="ar".

a11y.role: dialog, named by the title (aria-labelledby) or aria-label. Not modal unless modal is set.
a11y.focus: Focus moves into the window (the window element, tabindex -1) when it opens after mount, or on mount when its origin has focus. When the window closes or minimizes, focus goes to the first of: the origin, the next active window of the layer, the element that had focus before it opened, the dock, the WindowLayer (a region with tabindex -1). It moves only when focus was in the window or lost. Keyboard focus and pointer down both bring a window to the front.

keys.Escape: Closes the window. A control inside that handles Escape itself (a menu) prevents it first.
keys.ArrowUp: Moves the window up 16px, while focus is on the window or on its move handle (the title)
keys.ArrowDown: Moves the window down 16px, from the same places
keys.ArrowLeft: Moves the window 16px to the left on screen, in both directions
keys.ArrowRight: Moves the window 16px to the right on screen, in both directions
keys.Shift+ArrowUp, Shift+ArrowDown, Shift+Ar: Moves the window 64px, from the same places
keys.Enter: On the move handle: zooms the window or puts it back, when zoom works
keys.Tab: Moves through the lights or the title bar buttons, the move handle, the title bar actions, the body and the footer. With modal, Tab stays inside the window.

a11y.announce: The title is the accessible name of the dialog. The lights and the close button carry their own labels.
notes: Every drag has a key path (WCAG 2.1.1, 2.5.7): the arrow keys move the window from the window element or the move handle. The frame is clamped so 160px of the window and its title bar stay inside the layer.
Arrow keys pressed on a light, an action or anything in the body never move the window, so a roving toolbar in actions keeps its arrows.
Zoom has a key and a button in every style: Enter on the move handle, the zoom light in Desk, the zoom IconButton in Studio. A double click on the title bar is a pointer shortcut for the same action.
Moving is off while the window is zoomed, and for a window placed by its parent with no frame. The move handle is rendered only while the window can move.
Tab order follows the DOM order of the windows, not their stacking. Moving focus into a window with Tab brings it to the front.
A long title truncates with an ellipsis; the full text is the accessible name, and keyboard focus on the move handle wraps the title to show it in full.
No native title attribute.

WindowLayer is the container for windows, not a part of one: a positioned region (tabindex -1, named Windows) that stacks its windows, tracks the active one through the shared window manager and takes focus when its last window leaves. useWindowLayer() returns that manager, for a dock that restores minimized windows.

A Window outside a WindowLayer sits in the page flow (position relative), takes the size its parent gives it, has no frame and does not move. Give it a frame (and a positioned parent) to place and move it.
The five chrome labels (close, minimize, zoom, the controls group, the move handle) and the move hint default to Arabic under lang="ar", as Dialog and Toast do. A prop always wins.
Contract suite (many case, focus on the move handle): the arrow keys are checked with moves, Shift with the arrows with moves further, Escape with closes and Enter (zoom) with state-changes.

Arrow keys move the window in the physical direction on screen, in both directions: ArrowRight moves it right in Arabic too. A window is a spatial object on a desk, like a dragged card; a text or list control follows the reading direction, a positioned object does not (lead decision, wave 1).
Enter on the move handle zooms, and the handle is not rendered while the window is zoomed: focus moves to the window element (WCAG 2.4.3) and back to the handle when the window is restored.

native.note: Phones and tablets have no free windows. A native app shows the same content as a full screen or a sheet; see Dialog and Drawer.

styles.studio: A flat panel: the solid surface, the panel radius and shadow, no backdrop blur, a hairline under a plain title bar. No lights: minimize, zoom and close are IconButtons at the end of the title bar, minimize and zoom only when the window can do them. Open, close and minimize fade on duration.base; zoom has no motion.
styles.desk: A glass window: material glass with a 24px blur, radius 1rem, a hairline inside, the deep window shadow, a transparent title bar as in the source. The title bar starts with the traffic lights (optional part controls): idle dots at rest, colors and glyphs on hover or keyboard focus of the group. The window grows out of its trigger, closes back into it, zooms with a FLIP and falls into the dock. The layer carries the desk grain. In right to left layouts the lights stay at the top left and the title is centered.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass sheet.

name: WindowControls
summary: The traffic lights of a window: close, minimize and zoom. 12px lights with 24 by 24 px targets, each an IconButton with its own label.
useWhen: The controls slot of a TitleBar in a style that turns the window controls part on (Desk)
A window picture where the lights are shown but do nothing, with no handlers
avoidWhen: A panel in a style without lights (Studio)
Any control that is not close, minimize or zoom of a window

onClose.description: Without it the close light is disabled.

closeDisabled.description: With onClose: the close light is aria-disabled and data-disabled, stays in the tab order, blocks activation and draws as an idle dot; its glyph still shows on hover and focus. For a window or dialog that cannot be dismissed right now.

onMinimize.description: Without it the minimize light is disabled.

onZoom.description: Without it the zoom light is disabled.

closeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is إغلاق النافذة. A prop always wins.

minimizeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تصغير النافذة. A prop always wins.

zoomLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تكبير النافذة. A prop always wins.

label.description: The name of the group. Under lang="ar" the default is أزرار النافذة. A prop always wins.

active.description: data-state active or inactive, for hosts and recipes. As in the source, it does not change how the lights look.

a11y.role: group, named by label. Each light is a native button (IconButton).
a11y.focus: Each light with a handler is in the tab order with the 2px ring around its 24px target. A light with no handler is aria-disabled and out of the tab order (tabIndex -1): an accepted exception to the rule that disabled actions stay focusable, because a dead light is inert decoration of the window chrome; a screen reader still finds it, dimmed. A close light disabled through closeDisabled is an action that cannot run now: it stays focusable with aria-disabled, like any disabled Button.

keys.Enter: Presses the focused light. Nothing happens on a disabled light.
keys.Tab: Moves to the next light with a handler

a11y.announce: Each light is named by its label. The zoom light reports pressed while the window is zoomed.
notes: Never color alone: the glyphs (x, minus, arrows) show with the colors on hover and on keyboard focus of the group, and always in forced colors.
The lights do not mirror in right to left layouts. They keep the order close, minimize, zoom from the left, as macOS draws them and as the source does.
Targets are 24 by 24 px and touch, so light centers are 24px apart (WCAG 2.5.8).
No native title attribute.

angular.note: A first port exists for the Desk dialog chrome (packages/angular/src/components/window-controls), with the React DOM. The handlers are function inputs named like the React props (onClose, onMinimize, onZoom): a light with no handler is disabled, and an Angular output cannot tell whether anyone listens. No demo yet; it turns ready with Window. WindowControls.css is used as is.
